chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: components/audio/audio.c, recording.c, include/audio.h and recording.h. components/drivers/spi_per.c, gpio.c, i2s_per.c and storage.c, plus all driver headers (pin_defs.h, mcp_cmds.h, gpio.h, i2s_per.h, spi_per.h, storage.h). main/main.c, machine_registry.c and machine_stub.c. components/ui/ui.c, ui_events.h and ui.h. I also read components/machine/machine_core.c and sections of rest-api.c (remote trig/cv/ota/ice handlers), fileio.c (writeJSONFile, createConfigFile), sampfile.c (sampwav_*, sample_next_index), clock.c (set_ppb clamp) and menu_config.c, and checked the recording_poll_load callers (sampler3 and tape buffer sizes are fine).

Checked and found sound:
- Encoder ISR quadrature decoder, and the button ISR (ev.event is always assigned).
- ULP ISR to control_queue path. The queue and the ISR handler are created in the right order.
- Block handshake (machine_activate / machine_block_wait).
- Soft-MIDI held-note stack bounds.
- icepush buffer sizes: b64, req and the strlcpy fields.
- WAV header build.
- Boot order: initGPIO before initAudio, initWifi before the broadcast task, and mountSDStorage before any config read.
- Timer-event event_data is never dereferenced.
- Double-click behaviour: xTimerStart restarts the one-shot, so no phantom long press.
- Ring index wrap at 2^32 frames (a one-off glitch after about 27 h, not worth reporting).

Dropped as too speculative or benign:
- Uninitialised ctrlData before the first ULP sample.
- Possible CV latency from queue-depth drift if the ULP produces slightly faster than the audio task consumes.
- The 5 s OTA validation rollback when WiFi is absent (deliberate per its comment).
- A small leaked cJSON_Print string in the boot-only createConfigFile (fileio.c, out of scope).

Not reachable or not verified: whether the writer-park race in finding 1 is hit in practice depends on the SD scan latency (I did not measure it). Nothing in scope was left unread.

results.title: Writer parks on rec_active level; a stop during file setup strands it, bounce refused until reboot
results.claim: The writer parks until it SEES rec_active go true, but recording_stop()/recording_finish() can clear rec_active before the writer gets there, so it never sees the trigger.
results.scenario: recording_start()/audio_bounce_start() calls prepare (creates the writer) then trigger, so rec_active is set true straight away. The writer first runs find_next_filename (a readdir scan of every pool folder, tens to hundreds of ms on the first scan after boot or a prefix change) and fopen. If /bounce/stop, a Sampler gate release, or recording_set_trig_func(VOICE) calls recording_stop() inside that window, rec_active is already false when the writer reaches the park loop. It parks forever with the file handle open. rec_prepared stays true and rec_task_handle stays non-NULL, so every later recording_prepare()/audio_bounce_start() is silently refused until a reboot. Only recording_cancel_prepared() recovers it. A start-then-stop bench script or a fast double tap hits this. A separate 'triggered' latch set by recording_trigger() would avoid it.
results.reasoning: The park loop tests the level of rec_active, which recording_stop()/recording_finish() (recording.c:302/284) clear; the writer first runs find_next_filename (readdir of all 7 pool folders on first use or prefix change) and fopen, so a start then stop inside that window leaves it parked with the file open and rec_prepared true. audio_bounce_start() then returns at audio.c:168 (recording_is_prepared()), so /bounce/start and the Settings Bounce toggle (menu.c:438) report busy until reboot. Finder overstated one point: a later recording_trigger() (Sampler3 armed gate, Tape card mode) also un-parks it, but into the stale BNC_ file with the old vid and any chunks still queued. Not in the 09-16 review (1.4 and 1.7 are other stuck-prepared paths).
results.fix_sketch: Add an atomic rec_triggered latch set in recording_trigger() and cleared in recording_prepare(); park on !rec_triggered && !rec_cancel. A writer that wakes with rec_active already false falls into the existing drain loop and finalises the short take, or with an empty queue takes the existing cancel branch (fclose + remove under sd_lock).

results.title: Broadcast stream loops ignore s_bc_srv_run, no send timeout; disable not honoured, re-enable lost
results.claim: The :8000 stream loops (WAV path, and bc_stream_mp3(cl, NULL) on line 519) never check s_bc_srv_run, and the client socket has no SO_SNDTIMEO. A disable request is not honoured while a client is connected, and a stalled client blocks send() forever.
results.scenario: A client is streaming and the user turns Broadcast off in System->Settings or POST /bcast/enable?on=0. s_bc_srv_run goes false, but the task stays inside the send loop as long as the client stays connected, so the 12 KB internal stack is not freed. The stream keeps running and s_bc_on stays true, which also makes icepush answer 'listener active'. If the client stops reading (a paused VLC or browser tab), send() blocks in lwip with no timeout and the task never returns even after the client is closed locally. Turning broadcast on again meanwhile hits `if (s_bc_srv_run || s_bc_srv_alive) return;`. The task then exits when the client finally leaves, and the user's re-enable is lost.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 1.5, but it was never triaged: it is in no fix tier and not on the Watch list, no commit touches it, and the code is unchanged. The WAV loop (audio.c:522) exits only on send() < 0, bc_stream_mp3(cl, NULL) at 519 passes no run flag, and the client socket gets only SO_RCVTIMEO (501), so a disable is ignored while a client stays connected and the 12 KB stack is kept. A re-enable in that state returns at audio.c:773 on s_bc_srv_alive and the task then exits when the client leaves. Finder's 'never returns after the client closes' is overstated (a FIN/RST fails the send); consequence is wrong behaviour plus a temporary stack hold, not a permanent leak.
results.fix_sketch: Pass &s_bc_srv_run to bc_stream_mp3() (it already takes a run pointer, as icepush uses), add s_bc_srv_run to the WAV while condition, and set SO_SNDTIMEO on cl as icepush does at audio.c:821. Move run/alive onto a worker_t (worker_spawn/worker_exit) and have enable call worker_idle() briefly before spawning so an off-then-on is not dropped.

results.title: find_next_filename() calls VFS mkdir without sd_lock
results.claim: find_next_filename() (called from the writer at line 119, outside any sd_lock_take) does a VFS mkdir on the SD card without holding sd_lock, contrary to the rule that every SD I/O burst must hold it.
results.scenario: The card is busy with the Sampler/Deck reader task doing raw FatFS reads under sd_lock when a bounce or take is prepared. The unlocked mkdir goes through esp_vfs_fat, which does not share a lock with the raw reads. The two FatFS operations interleave on the shared FATFS window and the SDMMC bus. CLAUDE.md documents this as wedging or corrupting the card. It happens on every prepare, and mkdir is issued even when the directory already exists.
results.reasoning: The rule violation is real: mkdir at recording.c:106 runs outside sd_lock while sample_next_index() right after it locks every step (sampfile.c:120-136). The claimed corruption is not established: IDF 4.3 FatFS is built FF_FS_REENTRANT=1 (ffconf.h:287, 10 s timeout), so f_mkdir and the raw f_read serialise on the volume mutex, and on an existing folder f_mkdir is a read-only lookup returning FR_EXIST (usr/REC is not made at boot, so the first take on a fresh card does one real write). Same class as 6.12 (unlocked stat(), Low, Watch), a different site. Missing: evidence that a single unlocked VFS call harms anything beyond breaking the house rule.
results.fix_sketch: Wrap the mkdir in sd_lock_take()/sd_lock_give(), as sample_next_index() does for each step. Looper's identical unlocked mkdir at looper.c:309 can take the same change.

results.title: Take index above 9999 sends every take to one <PFX>OVFL.WAV, truncated each time
results.claim: Once the take index passes 9999, every new take is written to the same fixed file name and fopen("wb") truncates the previous one.
results.scenario: A card holding REC_9999 (or a long-running boot at 10000 takes) makes sample_next_index() return 10000. Every following recording or bounce opens usr/REC/REC_OVFL.WAV with "wb" and destroys the previous take. The sidecar and the auto-load then point at the same name. There is no error, log or refusal.
results.reasoning: hint > 9999 returns the fixed name without advancing, and the writer opens it with "wb" (recording.c:122), so each take destroys the previous one with no refusal or error. It is easier to reach than the finder said: sample_next_index() (sampfile.c:130-131) matches the prefix case-insensitively in every pool folder and takes atoi() of whatever follows, so with long filenames on, one uploaded file such as rec_20260913_jam.wav sets the counter to 20260914. In Sampler3 the overwritten file is also the one the voice auto-loaded and is streaming. The 8.3 limit that motivated the 4-digit cap no longer exists.
results.fix_sketch: Drop the OVFL branch: with LFN on, %s%04d prints five or more digits and still fits fname[48] and SAMPLE_ID_LEN. In sample_next_index() count only names whose digits run straight into the extension, so a date-stamped upload cannot set the counter.

results.title: s_bc_r incremented by both the audio task and the stream reader without atomicity
results.claim: s_bc_r is read-modify-written by two tasks with no atomicity: the audio task here (drop oldest) and the server/icepush task (s_bc_r++ at lines 415 and 527). Updates are lost and the reader can read slots the writer is overwriting.
results.scenario: A slow client (or a Radio-load encoder that lags) keeps the ring full. The reader loads s_bc_r, the audio task on core 1 increments it, and the reader stores its stale value +1. r goes backwards, so w-r exceeds BC_FRAMES and the reader consumes frames the writer has already overwritten. This is heard as a short burst or repeat in the live stream on every collision while lagging.
results.reasoning: s_bc_r is a plain volatile uint32_t: the audio task does s_bc_r++ at audio.c:374 when the ring is full, and the reader does s_bc_r++ at 415 (MP3) and 527 (WAV) from an unpinned prio-5 task, so a reader store can undo writer drops and leave w - r above BC_FRAMES; the reader also reads the slot the writer is overwriting when full. It only happens while the ring is full (client more than 1 s behind, or MP3 next to a playing Radio, which CLAUDE.md documents as not realtime). In that state drop-oldest is already skipping audio every block, so the extra artefact is a few out-of-order frames on top of existing dropouts. Real but low value.
results.fix_sketch: Make s_bc_r reader-owned: broadcast_push() only advances s_bc_w, and the two reader loops (audio.c:411 and 524) snap r forward to w - BC_FRAMES when they find w - r > BC_FRAMES before copying.

results.title: 64-bit s_trig_t_assert read by the audio task can tear against the GPIO ISR
results.claim: s_trig_t_assert is a 64-bit value written by the GPIO ISR (core 0 - gpio_isr_handler_add runs from app_main's core) and read here in the audio task on core 1 with two 32-bit loads, so it can be torn.
results.scenario: An assert edge lands exactly between the audio task's two loads. ta gets the new high word and the old low word (or the reverse), a garbage stamp. `ta != s_rep_t[t]` is then true, and if s_trig_low[t] is set with a huge now-ta the validity test passes. The audio task emits a phantom trig_rising bit (a spurious note or retrigger), and then again for the real stamp on the next block.
results.reasoning: The read at audio.c:581 is two 32-bit loads with no lock and the ISR (service installed from drivers/gpio.c:111 during boot) writes the same int64. But the finder's scenario is wrong for the general case: a mixed high/low word differs from the old or new stamp only when the two stamps have different high words, which happens once per 2^32 us (71.6 minutes). So the phantom or double trigger needs the first assert after that rollover to land inside a window of a few nanoseconds out of a 1.45 ms block, roughly once in years of continuous running. Present in the code, negligible in practice.
results.fix_sketch: Store the stamp as uint32_t (low 32 bits of esp_timer_get_time()) in s_trig_t_assert and s_rep_t: a single-word load is atomic and the unsigned differences and the equality de-dupe still work. Not worth a change on its own; fold it into any later edit of trig_rising_bits().

results.title: MIDI alive stamp written after the note is published; gate can all-off a fresh note
results.claim: note_on publishes s_midi_nheld inside the critical section but stamps s_midi_seen only afterwards (audio_midi_touch at line 120). The audio-task gate check can see nheld>0 with a stale stamp.
results.scenario: The first note after 5 s or more of silence (the stamp is old, or 0 at boot). The audio task calls audio_midi_gate() in the few-instruction window between the crit-section exit and audio_midi_touch(). It sees nheld==1 and now-seen > 500 ticks, and calls audio_midi_all_off(), which drops the note just pressed. The note never sounds, and the web page believes it is held. A tick edge between the tick read and the seen read gives an unsigned underflow with the same result.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 1.8, on the Watch list as low consequence, and the code is unchanged: audio_midi_touch() at audio.c:120 still runs after portEXIT_CRITICAL, and audio_midi_gate() at 149-150 reads nheld and the stamp unlocked. The window is a few instructions wide, so the Watch reasoning still holds. The tick-edge underflow the finder adds is the same unlocked stamp read and is closed by the same fix.
results.fix_sketch: Write s_midi_seen inside the s_midi_mux critical section in note_on/note_off/all_off, and compare with a signed tick difference in audio_midi_gate().

results.title: Failed or zero-chunk take leaves its header-only file in usr/REC
results.claim: A take that ends with zero chunks (or a write error) leaves the header-only 44-byte WAV on disk. Only the parked-cancel path removes its file.
results.scenario: A bounce or take is stopped before any block was queued, or the card fills at the first batch. usr/REC/BNC_nnnn.WAV or REC_nnnn.WAV remains with data size 0 (or 0xFFFFFFFF if finish failed). The pool browsers list it as a valid sample. Selecting it hands a 0-frame or bogus-length file to a machine's loader (the boot sweep only removes 0-byte files, not 44-byte ones).
results.reasoning: The failure branch at recording.c:203-207 only logs; only the parked-cancel path (143-144) removes the file. The finder's 'stopped before any block was queued' route does not occur with current callers (the writer either stays parked or at least one chunk is queued), so the real trigger is a write or close error on the first batch, such as a full card. The leftover matters slightly more than stated: sf_wav_parse() accepts a 44-byte WAV as valid with frames = 0 (sampfile_int.h:66-74), and the boot sweep covers only usr and usr/TRACKER (fileio.c:100-103), so the entry stays in the pool. Same class as 13.9 (Editor zero-frame file, Watch).
results.fix_sketch: When chunks_written == 0, remove(fname) inside the sd_lock section that already does sampwav_finish + fclose, as the cancel branch does. Keep the partial take when write_err occurs with chunks already written (the comment says that is deliberate).

chunks.coverage_notes:
I read every line of the in-scope files: components/machine/machine_core.c, clock.c, beatlisten.c, tuner.c, and include/machine.h, clock.h, trig_gate.h, cvsmooth.h, beatlisten.h, tuner.h. I also read the audio task loop (components/audio/audio.c ~545-745), svf.h/svf.c, the machine_web_apply and machine_activate call paths in rest-api.c and menu.c, sampplay_render, and the pitch_detect defines.

I found no high- or medium-confidence bugs in this scope. Paths I traced and found sound:
- The machine_activate detach / machine_block_wait / stop() ordering, including the web callback that waits for httpd, so no in-flight handler or process() reads freed state.
- The beatlisten ring, scratch and lag-array bounds, the paired s_whop/s_hop_frames snapshot, and the frame-counter wrap handling.
- The tuner double-buffer indices. The fill index reaches at most 4096 and 4096 is a multiple of 32, so it cannot overrun.
- The trig_gate pulse/debounce state machine, including the case where a rising edge arrives while the debounced level is still low. It completes the tap and does not double-fire.
- The clock_tick ring, median and guard arithmetic (no uint32 overflow at the ppb extremes) and the INT generator period math.

I dropped the following as too speculative. None has a realistic trigger.
- NaN entering clockin_set_ppb/set_int_bpm. The callers are REST-range-checked integers.
- Concurrent beatlisten_set_mode/tuner_set_enabled calls double-creating the task.
- A torn ring_n read between the UI-side cc_relock and the audio-side clock_tick. It yields one garbage period value, not an out-of-bounds access.
- The tuner analysing a buffer the audio task overwrites after 93 ms. It costs one wrong reading.

The machine.h comment "out = pre-zeroed by the core" is stale, because audio.c does not zero `out`. Every machine I checked (Editor, Freesound via sampplay_render, Tape, Stub) writes its whole output, so I did not report it as a bug. I did not audit every machine's process() for early returns without writing `out`; that belongs to the per-machine scopes. Everything in my scope was read.

results.title: cc_ensure() sets inited before initialising; cross-task race at boot
results.reasoning: The flag-before-init pattern is real, but the race window cannot be entered. initUI() calls clock_core_set_src/ppb/int_bpm/auto at components/ui/ui.c:339-342, on the main task, before initAudio() at ui.c:344 creates audio_task (components/audio/audio.c:760), and before the UI event loop (ui.c:349) and httpd (ui.c:360) exist. So cc_ensure() runs to completion single-threaded, and every later caller (clock_core_block at audio.c:653, clock_ui.c, rest-api.c:1202-1205) finds inited already true with all fields set. The finder's unconfirmed ordering assumption is the opposite of the actual order; not recorded in the 09-16 review.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Files read in full: components/util/reverb.c, flanger.c, fxdelay.c, fxfilter.c, svf.c, tremolo.c, overdrive.c, lfo.c, pitch_detect.c, bpm_analysis.c. Headers read in full: reverb.h, flanger.h, fxdelay.h, fxfilter.h, svf.h, tremolo.h, overdrive.h, lfo.h, pitch_detect.h, bpm_analysis.h, fxchain.h, fixed.h. Also read in full: components/fxrack/fxrack.c and include/fxrack.h. I checked the callers in synth, tape, instsampler, drums and slicer only for how they call process and free (machine_block_wait ordering, frames == 32, so the 64-float scratch buffers are safe). I did not audit those machines themselves.

Checked and found clean:
- pitch_detect: scratch sizing, index bounds and the unsigned window walk are all fine.
- bpm_analysis: buffer bounds, error-path frees and the ladder indexing are fine. The only defect I found is a trivial one: an abort during the harmonic step is not checked when the refinement ladder is skipped on very short tracks. I dropped it as negligible.
- svf, tremolo, lfo and fxfilter: fine, apart from unreachable-with-current-callers cases such as svf_coef with fmax <= 0 or a NaN param reaching fxfilter.
- reverb: the tap and length arithmetic never exceeds the line length. The mid-block resize by the UI (tank_resize while the audio task is inside a block) can give a one-block out-of-range read inside the slab. Mode is muted and the fade masks it, so I dropped it. The `static int s_tap[14]` is shared across reverb instances, but only one machine holds a running reverb at a time.

Dropped as unreachable or design: fixed.h has unparenthesised macros, but it is used only by machine_sampler2, which is not built. Concurrent REST and panel calls into slot_gc and init could double-free, but I judged that speculative.

Everything in scope was read; nothing was skipped.

results.title: Flanger float wrap can round rp to exactly cap, reading one element past each line
results.claim: The fractional read position is wrapped with a float add. When w - dl is a tiny negative number, adding cap rounds to exactly cap (float ulp near 529 is about 6e-5). i0 then equals cap and indexes one element past the line.
results.scenario: cap is 529 and w - dl falls in about (-3e-5, 0). That gives rp == 529.0f, i0 == 529, fr == 0. bufL[529] is really bufR[0], so L reads the wrong channel. bufR[529] is one float past the end of the PSRAM slab, so R reads whatever the heap holds there, at full weight. The garbage is written into the feedback ring through lpR and heard as a click. If the word is NaN or huge, the +/-60000 clamp does not catch NaN (comparisons are false). The NaN reaches lpR, the block-end guard fires and flanger_clear runs, and you hear a burst. This is rare, roughly once every few minutes of running flanger audio, but it is reachable and deterministic given the state. The fix is to wrap i0 (if (i0 >= cap) i0 -= cap) instead of relying on the float compare.
results.reasoning: cap is 529 (FLG_MAX_FR); for w - dl in [-3.05e-5, 0) the float add rp + 529 rounds to 529.0f, so i0 == 529 with fr == 0 and only i1 is wrapped (line 114). A float32 replay of the loop gave 2 hits in 600 s at the default rate 0.3 / depth 0.6, 1 at rate 1.0 / depth 1.0, 0 at rate 0.05 / depth 0.3. bufL[529] is bufR[0] and bufR[529] is 4 bytes past the PSRAM slab; on IDF 4.3 TLSF with poisoning disabled that word is the next block's size field, which reads as a denormal (about 0), so the result is a one-sample dropout in the R tap and a channel-swapped sample in L, fed into the ring. The finder's NaN burst is overstated (heap metadata is not a NaN pattern) and there is no crash. The 09-16 review listed flanger positions as checked in bounds, but missed this rounding case.
results.fix_sketch: After `int i0 = (int)rp;` add `if (i0 >= cap) i0 -= cap;`, the same integer wrap already used for i1 on line 114.

results.title: fxrack_menu_val/adj use stale cached row params after a preset load changes the slot kind
results.claim: fxrack_menu_val and fxrack_menu_adj index the descriptor's param table with a cached row param and check nothing. There is no check against gen_desc[kind].np, and none for p == NULL when the slot is FXK_OFF. The rows come from an earlier fxrack_menu_rows call, and fxrack_load can change the slot kind from another task in between.
results.scenario: The panel is on the Setup > FX page for slot 0 with Delay selected, so s_*fx_param[] holds row params 0..6. A web POST /remote/params, or any preset load in the httpd task, runs fxrack_load with fxsl [FXK_FILT or FXK_OFF, ...]. The next menu redraw calls fxrack_menu_val with param 5 or 6. For Filter (3 params) that is a read past filt_params[] and a call through a garbage function pointer. For Off, gen_desc[FXK_OFF].p is NULL, so NULL[param].fmt is a load fault. Either one is a panic and reboot. fxrack_menu_adj has the same pattern at line 363. Fix: clamp param against gen_desc[k].np and check p != NULL.
results.reasoning: The mechanism is a stale cache, not a cross-task race: POST /remote/params is queued as EV_REMOTE_PRESET and preset_load runs on the UI task (menu.c:618-630), which returns with no page re-entry. The hosts rebuild their rows only on EV_ENTERED_MENU or a param<0 adjust (e.g. synth_menu.c:675,690), so s_*fx_n and s_*fx_param keep the old kind's rows. The next encoder event on the FX page calls setup_menu draw, then render, then fxrack_menu_val with the old param: for Off, gen_desc[FXK_OFF].p is NULL, so even param 0 loads from address 8 and panics; for a kind with fewer params it reads past the table and calls whatever pointer is there. fxrack_menu_adj at line 363 has the same problem when the row is in edit mode.
results.fix_sketch: In fxrack_menu_val and fxrack_menu_adj return early when param >= gen_desc[k].np (np is 0 for Off, so this also covers p == NULL). In menu.c EV_REMOTE_PRESET, queue EV_ENTERED_MENU after preset_load, as EV_REMOTE_SETUP already does, so the FX page rebuilds its rows.

results.title: CV-modulated FX value is visible to save and menu during the stage, and can be stored as the base
results.claim: cv_push writes the CV-modulated value into the shared param field for the duration of the stage, and cv_pop restores the base afterwards. The header says the menu and preset always see the un-modulated base, but a UI-task write or a save that runs during that window sees the modulated value.
results.scenario: A CV is routed to Dly Mix, Flg Depth, Trm Depth or Rev Mix and is moving. The 2 s autosave (fxrack_save in the UI/httpd task) reads rk->dly->wet, rk->flg->depth or rk->rv->wet while the audio task sits between cv_push and cv_pop, which is a few percent of each block. The instantaneous modulated value is saved as the base, and on reload the patch comes back with a shifted base. Likewise a menu detent (dl_am and similar) does read-modify-write on the modulated value, and cv_pop's compare then declines to restore, so the CV offset gets baked into the base. Both are slow, silent parameter drift.
results.reasoning: cv_push writes the modulated value into the shared field for the whole stage; for the reverb that is all of reverb_block_f (fxrack.c:232-234), a large share of each block. The audio task is pinned to core 1 (audio.c:760) and the UI loop to core 0 (ui.c:349), so autosave_now, GET /remote/params (httpd, via preset_save then fxrack_save) and the menu adj functions (rv_ax, dl_am, fl_ad read-modify-write) do run inside that window. A save stores the modulated value, and a detent written from it fails cv_pop's compare, so the offset stays in the base. Only Tape feeds cv1/cv2/cv_rv (tape.c:360-364), so it needs a Tape CV route to an FX destination; the 09-16 note that offsets are restored correctly covers the restore, not this cross-task read.
results.fix_sketch: Stop writing the modulated value into the base field: give each effect struct an audio-only offset (for example cv_a / cv_b) that fxrack sets from cv1/cv2/cv_rv and the *_block_f functions add and clamp locally, then delete cv_push/cv_pop. Save, menu fmt and menu adj then only ever see the base.

results.title: fxrack_load accepts the same effect kind in both slots, so one effect instance runs twice per block
results.claim: fxrack_load does not enforce the one-effect-per-kind rule that slot_set enforces. An fxsl array such as [4,4] or [2,2] puts the same effect kind in both slots.
results.scenario: POST /remote/params, or a hand-edited preset or AUTOSAVE, contains "fxsl":[4,4]. run_gen_slots then calls fxdelay_block_f twice per block on the one fxdelay_t. The write cursor advances 2x frames per block and the second call reads taps from the region the first call just wrote. The delay time is effectively wrong, the repeats are time-scrambled, and CPU doubles. The flanger and tremolo LFO phases likewise advance twice as fast. The menu can no longer produce this state, and the display shows the same effect in both slots.
results.reasoning: fxrack_load stores each fxsl entry with only a range and no_filter check (lines 417-422); the one-per-kind rule lives only in slot_set (line 309). The web FX card offers the full list in both FX1 and FX2 dropdowns with no exclusion (index.html:1821; fxGroups only dedupes the displayed groups with `seen`), and rpApply posts fxsl as picked, so choosing Delay twice and pressing Apply reaches this. run_gen_slots then calls fxdelay_block_f twice on the one fxdelay_t per block: w advances 128 frames and the second pass reads taps across chunks the first pass just wrote; flanger and tremolo phase run at double speed, and the filter's single svf state is stepped twice.
results.fix_sketch: In fxrack_load, after the fxsl loop, apply slot_set's rule: if a later slot holds the same non-Off kind as an earlier one, set it to FXK_OFF. Optionally hide the other slot's kind in the web fxSel using its existing skip argument.

results.title: Overdrive tone filter has no NaN guard
results.reasoning: No reachable path delivers a NaN to this stage. The rack input is always unpacked from int32 (fxchain.h:29), the only caller is fxrack.c:183, and every stage that can sit in front of it is finite on finite input: delay feedback is capped at 0.95, tremolo gain is at most 1, the flanger ring is clamped, and fxfilter is a stable trapezoidal svf with its own guard (fxfilter.c:9-15). Inside the stage fast_tanh is bounded to +/-1 (overdrive.c:22-25), the svf runs at q 1.0 with fc capped at sr/6, and drive/tone/level come from integer JSON or clampf of finite CV offsets. The guard would be hardening only.

results.title: fxdelay_init/flanger_init publish bufL before cap and bufR while the slot is already live
results.claim: fxdelay_init and flanger_init memset the whole struct and then publish bufL before cap and bufR are set. fxrack_load has already set rk->slot[s] to FXK_DLY or FXK_FLG before calling init, so the audio task's only guard is `if (rk->dly->bufL)`.
results.scenario: fxrack_load, running in a UI or httpd task, sets the slot to Delay or Flanger and calls init. Between the store of bufL and the stores of cap and bufR, the audio task on the other core passes the bufL guard and sees cap == 0 and bufR == NULL. In fxdelay_block_f, r = w - len is negative, so bufR[r] dereferences NULL and panics. In flanger_block_f, cap == 0 makes `while (rp < 0) rp += cap` loop forever, which hangs the audio task and trips the task watchdog. The window is a few instructions wide, so this is very unlikely, but it can be closed by filling cap and bufR first and publishing bufL last.
results.reasoning: fxrack_load stores rk->slot[s] (line 420) before calling init (lines 432-433), unlike slot_set, which inits first. It runs on the UI task on core 0 (EV_REMOTE_PRESET, patch load, machine bind) while the audio task on core 1 is already running process(), and the only guard is `if (rk->dly->bufL)`. In the window the delay sees cap 0 and bufR NULL, so r is -1 and bufR[-1] faults; the flanger captures cap 0 and `while (rp < 0) rp += cap` never exits, and with TASK_WDT_PANIC and the CPU1 idle check both off that is a silent audio hang, not a reboot. What is missing is evidence the window is ever hit: it is a few instructions wide (tens of ns per 1.45 ms block) unless the UI task is interrupted exactly there.
results.fix_sketch: In fxrack_load keep the parsed kind in a local, run fxdelay_init/flanger_init first and store rk->slot[s] only afterwards (slot_set's order, fxrack.c:303-310). In both init functions also set cap, bufR and len before storing bufL, so bufL is the last field published.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: components/util/{sampfile.c, sampfile_int.h, sampfile_f.c, sample_ram.c, sampimport.c, mp3.c, fileio.c, sd_lock.c, list.c, preset_store.c, sampplay.c, sample_list_recent.c, string_tools.c, c_timeutils.c, timer_utils.c, disp_lock.c}, plus headers sampfile.h, sampfile_f.h, sample_ram.h, sampplay.h, sampimport.h, mp3.h, fileio.h, list.h, preset_store.h, string_tools.h, timer_utils.h, c_timeutils.h, sd_lock.h, disp_lock.h and worker.h. I also checked callers in fs_machine.c, menu.c, ui.c, rest-api.c and sampler_menu.c. worker.h's spawn/stop/idle logic held up: alive is raised before create, stop never frees on timeout, and I found no defect in it. sampplay.c's ring and flush handshake showed only theoretical races and no reachable defect.

I dropped or left unreported:
- Dead or unbuilt paths: getFilesInDir (its `break` on the first non-regular entry, its d_name[-4+len] read for short names, no sd_lock), parseJSONAudioTags (NULL valuestring), repairAudioFileAssigment (NULL derefs and cJSON_Print leaks), decodeMP3File (NULL fPars), and ftoa (garbage for negative values). These are used only by machine_sampler2 or legacy sampler/freesound code.
- preset_store_save clamping to PAT_999 and overwriting it.
- Possible NaN to int in float32 import.
- timer_utils portMAX_DELAY sends from the timer daemon, and setTimerSingleShot ignoring its delay after the first call. Neither is reachable in the built configuration.
- The 32-bit tv_sec*1000 wrap in c_timeutils.

Not covered: I did not read the helix decoder internals (the vendored library is out of scope). I did not trace every downstream consumer of sf.frames or sf_seek_pos in the machines. I did not verify whether FatFS FF_FS_REENTRANT already serialises the unlocked stat calls. That is why the sample_resolve finding is only low confidence.

results.title: Freesound convert and import scan can run MP3 decodes at once on the shared global `input` buffer
results.claim: decodeMP3FileSync uses the file-scope globals `input` and `readPtr`, and the header says one decode at a time. Nothing enforces that. The Freesound task calls samp_import_file without checking or setting samp_import_busy, so it can run at the same time as the import scan task. Both also write the same IMPNEW.TMP / IMPMP3.TMP names in the same directory.
results.scenario: A Freesound download reaches its convert step (fs_machine.c:353) while an import scan is running (REST /import, or the automatic samp_import_start after an upload, rest-api.c:1478) and both hit an MP3. The two tasks overwrite `input`, so one frees or decodes the other's buffer. That is a double free or use-after-free in the decoder, or interleaved garbage in the output. The scan also lists usr/, sees the half-written or still-converting usr/<name>.mp3, passes magic_is_mp3 (ID3 or chained frames), and converts it. imp_publish then remove()s the source, which corrupts or destroys the Freesound file. Two conversions in one directory also clobber the same IMPNEW.TMP.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 3.4, which sits in themes G/H but in no fix tier and not in Watch; it was never fixed (samp_import_file, sampimport.c:300, still ignores samp_import_busy and fs_machine.c:353 calls it directly). The same-directory half of the claim is wrong: CONFIG_FATFS_FS_LOCK=5 makes the second open of usr/IMPMP3.TMP / IMPNEW.TMP fail, so the scan cannot double-convert or destroy the Freesound mp3 (one side just reports 'decode failed'). The real path is two decodes in different folders (Freesound in usr/, the scan on an MP3 in usr/DRUMS, KEYS etc.): both reach `input = malloc` (mp3.c:296), one block leaks, both decode through the other, then use-after-free and a double free. Both tasks are prio 5 and unpinned, and every web upload starts a scan.
results.fix_sketch: Make `input` and `readPtr` locals of decode() so the decoder holds no shared state. Have one import slot cover both callers: fs_pipeline claims samp_import_busy (or a static mutex inside samp_import_file) before it creates usr/<name>.mp3, and samp_import_start refuses while it is held.

results.title: Sync search scans 4096 bytes after a short first read; offset past nRead wraps the memmove length
results.claim: MP3FindSyncWord scans all MAX_FRAME_SIZE bytes of `input`, but only nRead bytes are valid after a short read. `input` is a fresh uninitialised malloc. If the sync is found at offset >= nRead, the unsigned `nRead - offset` wraps to about 4 GB.
results.scenario: An upload or import of a small (<4 KB) file that starts with 'ID3' (so magic_is_mp3 passes) but has no real frame. The read after the ID3 skip returns a few bytes. Stale heap bytes beyond nRead, for example from a previous decode's freed `input`, contain 0xFF 0xE? and FindSyncWord returns an offset past nRead. memmove then runs with a huge length and the module panics.
results.reasoning: mp3.c:100 calls MP3FindSyncWord(input, MAX_FRAME_SIZE) whatever nRead was, and `input` is an uninitialised malloc (heap poisoning is off, so freed contents survive; any FF FF pair matches the sync mask). If the first read is short and has no sync in the valid part, an offset > nRead makes the unsigned `nRead - offset` at :116 wrap and memmove panics. It needs a file that starts with 'ID3' (so magic_is_mp3 passes) with under 4 KB and no frame after the tag, plus stale bytes that look like a sync; the heap contents are what I could not establish. The memmove was added by the 3.5 fix (38239db), so this is a regression from it; later reads are safe because the stale tail was already scanned clean.
results.fix_sketch: Pass nRead to MP3FindSyncWord at mp3.c:100 and treat offset >= nRead as not found.

results.title: sample_load reads to EOF and ignores sf.frames, so chunks after the audio load as samples
results.claim: sample_load loops until max_frames or EOF and never bounds the read by sf.frames. For a WAV with chunks after `data` (LIST/INFO from ffmpeg, Audacity, sox, id3 chunks) the trailing chunk bytes are loaded as audio. The same happens for an AIFF with a chunk after SSND when nframes is zero.
results.scenario: Load a stereo 16-bit 44.1k WAV with a trailing LIST chunk into a slicer or granular buffer. The returned frame count is larger than the real data, and the last tens of frames are metadata bytes, heard as a noise burst or click at the loop or end point. The header's data size is parsed but not used to stop.
results.reasoning: The loop at sample_ram.c:130-145 stops only on max_frames or a zero read; sf.frames (set from the data chunk size at sampfile_int.h:73, and from COMM nframes at :124) is never used. A native 16-bit 44.1k WAV with LIST/smpl/cue chunks after `data` therefore loads those bytes as audio and returns a frame count that is too long. Such files reach the card untouched: the web page uploads WAV verbatim (index.html DEV_EXTS) and the importer leaves native files alone (sampimport.c:358). Callers are Drums, Keys, Granular and the Synth wavetable, so it shows as a click at the end of a one-shot or at the loop point. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: In sample_load clamp the limit once after the probe: `if (max_frames > sf.frames) max_frames = sf.frames;`. The streaming readers already bound by sf.frames.

results.title: AIFF SSND offset field is not validated; a bad value gives a wrapped data offset and huge frame count
results.claim: The AIFF SSND `offset` field is unvalidated. A large `off` wraps the 32-bit data_off or pushes it past EOF. Then `(uint32_t)(fsize - sf->data_off)` wraps to a huge avail. In addition, COMM nframes is trusted whenever `nframes <= avail`.
results.scenario: A hostile or corrupt AIFF has SSND offset = 0xFFFFFFF0 (data_off wraps into the header) or an offset larger than the file. The probe returns 0 with frames up to about 2^32. sampplay_open accepts it and reports a huge sampplay_frames. The reader hits got == 0 and spins restarting the loop, playing silence. Editor and deck UIs and sf_seek_pos (`(long)frame * stride`) do arithmetic on the bogus length and overflow. With the wrapped offset the header bytes play as noise.
results.reasoning: `pos + 8 + 8 + off` is 32-bit and wraps, and when data_off lands past EOF `(uint32_t)(fsize - sf->data_off)` at :123 wraps too, so the probe returns 0 with frames near 2^30 (or an unchecked COMM nframes). The 3.6 fix hardened the chunk walk at :127 but not this field. The consequence is smaller than claimed: sample_load just gets 0 frames, and sampplay resets src and sleeps a tick per retry (sampplay.c:67, :103), so it is silence with a bogus length, not a spin; a wrapped offset plays header bytes. It needs a corrupt or hand-made AIFF, since real files have offset 0.
results.fix_sketch: Compute the data offset in int64 like the chunk walk at sampfile_int.h:127 and reject with `sf->why = "AIFF: bad SSND offset"` when it is >= fsize.

results.title: MP3 decode stops at the first frame error and still reports success, so a truncated import replaces the source
results.claim: The decode loop ends silently at the first MP3Decode error (any corrupt frame or unsupported frame). f_write results are unchecked (line 198). decodeMP3FileSync reports success if any bytes were written, so a truncated decode counts as success.
results.scenario: A 3-minute MP3 with one bad frame at 0:20, or an SD write failure or full card mid-decode, produces a 20 s IMPMP3.TMP. samp_import_file converts it and imp_publish then remove()s the original .MP3. The remaining audio is lost with no error. That is silent data loss of a user file.
results.reasoning: The loop ends on any MP3Decode error and never resyncs (mp3.c:164, :207), and decodeMP3FileSync returns 0 whenever any output exists (:312). samp_import_file then converts the short IMPMP3.TMP and imp_publish removes the original (sampimport.c:280), so an MP3 with one undecodable region mid-file becomes a shortened WAV with no error. The f_write at :198 is also unchecked, though a full card mostly fails safe later because convert_pcm checks its own fwrite (sampimport.c:248). Same class as 13.3/13.8, but this path was not in the 09-16 review and e327f6f did not touch mp3.c; it needs a damaged MP3.
results.fix_sketch: On a non-underflow error, resync with MP3FindSyncWord and continue, as radio.c:312-318 does; only INDATA_UNDERFLOW with nothing left to read ends the file. Have decode() return a status (check f_write's result and bw) so decodeMP3FileSync fails when the input was not consumed to the end.

results.title: getFileSize returns uninitialised stack data when the file is missing
results.claim: getFileSize ignores the stat return value and `struct stat st` is uninitialised, so it returns stack garbage when the file is missing.
results.scenario: On a fresh card or missing /sdcard/AUTOSAVE.JSN, readJSONFileAsCJSON returns NULL and menu.c:708 calls getFileSize("/sdcard/AUTOSAVE.JSN") > 2. If the stack garbage is > 2, autosave logs 'read failed on existing file' and skips saving. The AUTOSAVE.JSN file is then never created.
results.reasoning: The stat result is ignored and `st` is uninitialised; IDF 4.3 vfs_fat_stat returns -1 before its memset (vfs_fat.c:597-603), so st_size is whatever was on the stack. The only caller is autosave_now (menu.c:708), reached when AUTOSAVE.JSN is missing; if the garbage is > 2 every save logs 'read failed on existing file' and the file is never created. Whether that slot holds a value > 2 depends on the build's stack layout, which I could not establish from reading. The stat also runs without sd_lock.
results.fix_sketch: Use the existing fileExists() (fileio.c:209, zero-inits and checks the return) at menu.c:708, or make getFileSize return 0 when stat fails, under sd_lock.

results.title: Files with base names over 31 chars are listed under a truncated id that cannot be resolved
results.claim: sample_name_id silently truncates base names longer than 31 chars. The listings then show a truncated id that sample_resolve cannot find, and different long files with the same first 31 chars collapse into one dedup'd entry.
results.scenario: Copy 'My_very_long_field_recording_take_01.wav' (>31 chars) onto the card with LFN on. The browser lists the first 31 chars as its id. Selecting it makes resolve fail, falls to usr/<id>.RAW, and the load silently fails or plays silence. Two files that differ only after character 31 appear as one.
results.reasoning: sample_name_id clamps to id_len-1 and returns true; both listers use it (sample_ram.c:59, sample_list_recent.c:43) and dedup on the clamped id. sample_resolve (sampfile.c:90) stats the 31-char name, finds nothing and falls back to usr/<id>.RAW, so the load fails with 'cannot open'. CONFIG_FATFS_MAX_LFN=64, so names of 32 to 64 chars copied onto the card are read in full and hit this; web uploads and Freesound are capped at 31 and do not. Not in the 09-16 review, and plans/long-filenames-20260913.md does not describe it as intended.
results.fix_sketch: Return false from sample_name_id when the base does not fit id_len, so both listers skip a file that cannot be addressed, and log it once. The import scan could rename such files to a 31-char id if they should stay usable.

results.title: writeJSONFile truncates in place with no write check; a cut mid-save empties CONFIG.JSN or AUTOSAVE.JSN
results.claim: writeJSONFile truncates the target in place, does not check fwrite, and has no temp+rename. It is used for CONFIG.JSN, AUTOSAVE.JSN and every preset. preset_store_save ignores the outcome and returns 0.
results.scenario: Power loss, card removal or a full card during an autosave leaves a zero-length or truncated AUTOSAVE.JSN or CONFIG.JSN. Every other machine's saved state is gone, and validateConfig then regenerates CONFIG.JSN with placeholder wifi credentials. preset_store_save reports success for a preset that was not written.
results.reasoning: fopen "wb" zeroes the file on disk at open, fwrite and fclose are unchecked and the function is void, so preset_store_save returns 0 whatever happened (preset_store.c:63-67). A power cut between open and close leaves a zero-length file: for AUTOSAVE.JSN the next save mints a new object and every other machine's state is gone (menu.c:707-713); a truncated non-empty one fails to parse and then every later save is skipped for good. An empty CONFIG.JSN fails validateConfig and is regenerated with placeholder WiFi credentials, losing encres/encdir (fileio.c:138-141). The window is tens of ms per save, 2 s after any edit; not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: Write to a sibling temp file, check fwrite and fclose, then swap it in with the backup-rename pattern of imp_publish (sampimport.c:283-297), since FAT cannot rename over a file. Return int and let preset_store_save and the autosave log pass the failure on; on read, fall back to the backup when the main file is missing or empty.

results.title: AIFF convert path reads to EOF, so chunks after SSND become audio
results.claim: For AIFF, src_data_len is `fsize - data_off` (to EOF) and ignores nframes and the SSND size. Chunks after SSND (MARK/INST/ANNO/COMT) are converted as audio.
results.scenario: Importing a 24-bit or 48k AIFF that has metadata chunks after SSND. The converted WAV gets extra garbage frames at the end (a noise burst) and the original is removed.
results.reasoning: sf_aiff_parse sets src_data_len = fsize - src_data_off (sampfile_int.h:114) and ignores both the SSND chunk size and COMM nframes; the native path at :123-124 does cap by nframes, the convert path does not. samp_import_file (sampimport.c:375) turns that into src.frames, and src_read runs to that count, so any MARK/INST/COMT/ID3 chunk after SSND is decoded as PCM and appended to the converted WAV that replaces the source. The WAV parser is not affected (it uses csz, :56-58). Not in the 09-16 list (3.9 was the 8-bit sign only).
results.fix_sketch: In sf_aiff_parse, bound src_data_len by the SSND size (csz - 8 - off) and by nframes*ch*(bits/8) when nframes is non-zero, clamped to fsize - src_data_off. This is the same self-heal shape sf_wav_parse uses at :56-58 and the native AIFF path uses at :123-124; sampfile_f.c picks it up through the shared parser.

results.title: Boot sweep deletes IMPBAK.TMP, the in-place import backup; pool subfolders never swept
results.claim: The boot sweep deletes every *.TMP in usr/, including IMPBAK.TMP. imp_publish parks the original there as its backup when converting X.WAV in place. The sweep also does not cover usr/REC, LOOPS, SLICES, DRUMS, KEYS or TAPE, so leftover IMPNEW.TMP and IMPMP3.TMP files sit there forever.
results.scenario: Power is cut between rename(src, IMPBAK.TMP) and rename(tmp, dst) while converting a 48k or 24-bit usr/X.WAV in place. The next boot's sweepDir removes IMPBAK.TMP, which is the only copy of the audio. A crash mid-conversion in a subfolder leaves multi-MB IMP*.TMP files that are never cleaned up.
results.reasoning: imp_publish (sampimport.c:285-296) parks X.WAV as <dir>/IMPBAK.TMP and then renames IMPNEW.TMP over it; a power cut between those two renames leaves the audio only in two *.TMP files, and sweepDir (fileio.c:82-96, run from checkSDStructure:144) removes both in usr/. The window is narrow: two back-to-back FAT renames under sd_lock, per converted file. sweepIncompleteFiles (fileio.c:100-103) covers only usr and usr/TRACKER while import_task scans seven folders (sampimport.c:401-404), so IMP*.TMP leftovers in REC/LOOPS/SLICES/DRUMS/KEYS/TAPE stay until the next conversion in that folder overwrites or removes them (not strictly forever), and nothing ever restores a stranded backup. The backup name came in with the 3.3 fix (e327f6f); 3.3 itself is fixed.
results.fix_sketch: Name the backup after the file it protects (e.g. X.WAV.BAK, not a .TMP and not a pool extension) so the sweep can put it back when X.WAV is missing and delete it otherwise. Run sweepDir over the same seven pool folders the importer scans, plus TRACKER.

results.title: sample_resolve stat() burst runs without sd_lock
results.claim: sample_resolve does up to 28 VFS stat() calls without taking sd_lock. sd_lock.h says every SD touch must hold the lock because raw-FatFS streaming readers bypass the VFS lock. Callers such as sample_load, sampplay_open, editor, deck and REST do not lock around it.
results.scenario: The user opens a sample in the Editor or loads one from the browser while a deck or slicer SD reader task is mid f_read. The unlocked stat burst interleaves with it on the same card, which is the documented bus-wedge or corruption hazard (empty browser, noisy reads).
results.reasoning: True as code: sample_resolve takes no lock and most callers (sample_ram.c:112, sampplay.c:152, deck.c:135, slicer.c:231, editor.c:63, rest-api.c:529/2590) call it before their sd_lock_take; only the rename handler (rest-api.c:448) wraps it. That breaks the CLAUDE.md rule, but I could not establish the claimed corruption: FatFS is built re-entrant (esp-idf-v4.3 fatfs/src/ffconf.h:287 FF_FS_REENTRANT 1, sdkconfig CONFIG_FATFS_TIMEOUT_MS=10000), so each f_stat is serialised against every f_read on the volume by FatFS's own mutex, and the deck/slicer readers named in the scenario use VFS fread, not raw f_read. The 09-16 review filed the same pattern in REST handlers as 6.12 and left it on the Watch list as low consequence; what is missing is any evidence that an unlocked stat, as opposed to an unlocked read/write, does harm.
results.fix_sketch: Take and give sd_lock around each stat() inside sample_resolve, the way sample_next_index does per readdir step (sampfile.c:126-128), so audio refills still interleave. The mutex is recursive, so the rename handler that already holds it is unaffected.

results.title: list_free frees only the head value and locks before the NULL check
results.claim: list_free frees only the head item's value, then frees the nodes. Every other element's value leaks. The mutex is also locked before the `l != NULL` check.
results.scenario: Each list_free of a list with N string values leaks N-1 allocations. The callers are freesound.c tag_list and machine_sampler2 (not built), so it is low impact.
results.reasoning: The defect is in the code (list.c:25 locks before the NULL test, :30 frees only the head's value), but nothing built calls it. The freesound.c:49 call the finder names sits inside a /* */ block (freesound.c:32-276); every other caller is in machine_sampler2, which is in EXCLUDE_COMPONENTS (CMakeLists.txt:10), and getFilesInDir (fileio.c:335) has no built caller. The 09-16 review, chunk 3, recorded exactly this: 'Not reported: legacy list.c ... only callers are in Sampler2 (not built)', and that reason still holds.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: menu.c, menusys.c, menu_config.c, setup_menu.c, menu_nav.c, menutft_utils.c, menutft.c, clock_ui.c, text_entry.c, and headers menu_types.h, menutft.h, menusys.h, menutft_utils.h, setup_menu.h. Also read the relevant parts of ui.c (event loop, queue, timers), timer_utils.c, fileio.c (read/write/getFileSize/createConfigFile), ui_events.h, and the rest-api handlers that post UI events.

Not read: menu.h, menu_config.h, text_entry.h beyond the TEXT_ENTRY_MAX define, and the other files in components/menu (cvmtx.c, sample_browser.c, wave_edit.c, and their headers), which are outside the listed scope.

Checked and dropped as not real bugs: setup_menu_remote_json buffer math (worst-case row length stays under the 96-byte margin); text_entry buffer bounds (TEXT_ENTRY_MAX 47, buffer sized +2); menuEllipsize; the s_bind_pending event-drop logic (event_data frees are correct for the remote events).

Unbuilt code, not reported: loadPresetConfig, savePresetConfig, menuTFTPrintInputError (sprintf into str[32]), the HSpaced print helpers (divide by n_items), and the bbox-list highlight helpers. Their only callers are in machine_sampler2, which is excluded from the build. savePresetConfig, loadPresetConfig and validateConfig also have leak and NULL-deref paths.

Dropped for lack of a confirmed trigger: unchecked malloc/realloc in menusys.c; the httpd task calling setup render callbacks concurrently with machine stop()."

results.title: Failed AUTOSAVE.JSN read on bind loads defaults, next autosave overwrites the saved entry
results.claim: On bind, a failed read of an existing AUTOSAVE.JSN (DMA-capable alloc failure, parse OOM) is treated the same as 'no saved entry', so the machine loads defaults. The autosave path has a guard for this case; the load path does not.
results.scenario: Switch to a machine while internal RAM is tight (Radio playing, web open). readJSONFileAsCJSON returns NULL, so preset_load(NULL) loads defaults. The next encoder event arms autosave, which re-reads the file successfully and overwrites that machine's saved entry with the defaults. The saved state is lost silently.
results.reasoning: menuMachineBindNow treats a NULL from readJSONFileAsCJSON (DMA alloc of the ~5 KB file at fileio.c:245, short fread, parse fail) exactly like a missing entry and calls preset_load(NULL). s_bind_pending is already false, so the next encoder event or dirty poll arms autosave_now (menu.c:688), whose read now succeeds and replaces this machine's key with the defaults. autosave_now has the 'existing file but NULL read' guard (menu.c:707-712); the load side has none. 5b4ea8e moved cJSON nodes to PSRAM so the parse-OOM trigger is rarer, but the internal DMA buffer alloc and card errors remain.
results.fix_sketch: In menuMachineBindNow, when root is NULL and fileExists("/sdcard/AUTOSAVE.JSN") > 2, retry the read once; if it still fails set a static 'load failed' flag that autosave_now checks (next to the s_bind_pending check) and skips with a log until a later bind loads successfully. Still call preset_load(NULL) so the machine runs.

results.title: writeJSONFile truncates in place and ignores fwrite result (AUTOSAVE.JSN, CONFIG.JSN)
results.claim: writeJSONFile truncates the target in place and never checks the fwrite result. AUTOSAVE.JSN, which holds every machine's state, is rewritten this way after every edit. CONFIG.JSN is written the same way.
results.scenario: Power is cut (normal for Eurorack) or the card fills during the ~60 ms rewrite. The file is left empty or truncated. If it is truncated but non-empty, menu.c autosave_now sees a NULL parse and getFileSize > 2, logs 'read failed on existing file' and skips every future save. Autosave stays dead until the file is deleted by hand. All other machines' saved state is already gone. A damaged CONFIG.JSN fails validateConfig at boot and is replaced with defaults, which wipes the ssid, passwd and apikey.
results.reasoning: fopen("wb") zeroes the directory entry at open and FatFS only writes the new size at fclose, so a power cut inside the write leaves a 0-byte file: for AUTOSAVE.JSN every machine's state is gone (autosave_now mints a fresh object), for CONFIG.JSN checkSDStructure (fileio.c:138) sees validateConfig()==-1 and createConfigFile rewrites defaults, wiping ssid/passwd/apikey/machine/encres/encdir. A short fwrite (card full, line 329 unchecked) leaves a truncated non-empty file; autosave_now (menu.c:707-711) then hits 'read failed on existing file - skip' on every save until the file is deleted by hand. Not recorded on 09-16 (6.8/13.8 cover other unchecked writes).
results.fix_sketch: Write to a sibling temp file under sd_lock, check fwrite == len and fclose == 0, then remove + rename over the target (the temp-then-rename pattern mod_upload in rest-api.c already uses); on failure delete the temp and keep the old file. Return a status so callers can log.

results.title: Settings re-entry re-reads CONFIG.JSN without freeing the held cfgData tree
results.claim: settings_def_handler overwrites the static cfgData on every EV_ENTERED_MENU without freeing the previous tree. Only the long-press exit deletes it. Entering About or Tuner and coming back, or a re-sent EV_ENTERED_MENU (screenshot warm-up, web Setup mirror), leaks a parsed CONFIG.JSN each time.
results.scenario: System > Settings > Tuner (or About), long-press back to Settings. EV_ENTERED_MENU runs with _state_json == NULL, so cfgData is re-read and the old tree is never freed. Repeated visits or repeated /screenshot warm-ups leak PSRAM, or internal RAM once PSRAM is exhausted.
results.reasoning: Settings > Tuner (line 442) and Settings > About (line 436) return without setting _state_json; their long-press returns M_SETTINGS, menusys calls the handler with EV_ENTERED_MENU (-1), _state_json is NULL so line 366 overwrites the static cfgData; only the long-press exit (464, 535) deletes it. The same happens for a re-sent EV_ENTERED_MENU (menu.c:642, rest-api.c:631/692/895). 09-16 finding 4.3 noted the leak for the web Setup re-entry only and it was never placed in a tier; the Tuner/About panel path is new. Leak is ~1-2 KB of PSRAM per visit (cJSON hooks, ui.c:316), and the re-read also resets a staged Remote toggle.
results.fix_sketch: In EV_ENTERED_MENU, when _state_json is NULL and cfgData is non-NULL, cJSON_Delete(cfgData) before the readJSONFileAsCJSON (or keep the held tree and skip the re-read). No new mechanism needed.

results.title: menusys loops forever on an unregistered menu id
results.claim: If a handler returns a menu id that is not registered in the current menusys, the for loop finds no match. new_item_id is unchanged, so the while loop spins forever. The same pattern is at line 102. Machine pages and main_targets tables are hand-maintained, so a typo or a missing register_pages entry triggers it.
results.scenario: A machine returns a target id it never registered, for example a main_targets entry or a boot_target without a page. The UI task (prio 11) busy-loops while holding disp_lock. The panel freezes and the task watchdog fires or the unit hangs.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 4.7, word for word (menusys.c:79 and :102, unregistered page id, UI task hangs holding disp_lock). Triage lists it under Watch as 'already known, never observed'; menusys.c is unchanged since and still has no guard. Nothing new to add.

results.title: menuBindMachineUI blocks forever when called on the UI task with a full event queue
results.claim: menuBindMachineUI is called from the UI task itself (menuSwitchMachine, from EV_REMOTE_MACHINE or a panel press). It blocks forever on the queue that only the UI task drains. If the 64-slot queue is full, the UI task deadlocks on itself.
results.scenario: machine_activate takes seconds (Tracker or Keys arena) while the encoder is spun or REST floods /remote/enc and the two timer tasks keep posting. The queue fills to 64. menuSwitchMachine then calls menuBindMachineUI, which never returns. The UI is dead with no watchdog trip, because the task is blocked, not spinning.
results.reasoning: menuSwitchMachine (menu.c:292/296) runs inside menuProcessEvent on ui_ev_loop, the queue's only consumer, and posts EV_MACHINE_BIND with portMAX_DELAY to the 64-slot queue (ui.c:325). While it is inside autosave_now + machine_activate + configSetStringSetting nothing drains: the two timer tasks add 4.3 events/s (ui.c:270/281), the encoder ISR adds one per detent (gpio.c:55-82), REST adds more. Radio stop waits up to 7 s (radio.c:367) and Tape stop waits on a take save with no bound (tape.c:1034-1037), so ~15 s alone, or a slow stop plus ~35 encoder detents, fills it; the UI task then sleeps forever holding disp_lock, no watchdog. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: s_bind_pending is already the truth: make the send non-blocking (timeout 0) and have menuProcessEvent run menuMachineBindNow() on the first event it sees with s_bind_pending set, so the queued EV_MACHINE_BIND is only a wake-up. app_main's call keeps working unchanged.

results.title: getFileSize returns uninitialised st_size when stat fails
results.claim: getFileSize ignores stat()'s return value and returns an uninitialised st_size when the file does not exist.
results.scenario: On a card with no AUTOSAVE.JSN, readJSONFileAsCJSON returns NULL. autosave_now then calls getFileSize("/sdcard/AUTOSAVE.JSN") and gets stack garbage. If the garbage is > 2, autosave logs 'read failed on existing file' and never creates the file, so nothing persists.
results.reasoning: The defect is real: st is not initialised, stat's result is ignored, and IDF's vfs_fat_stat returns -1 without touching st, so a missing file yields stack residue. Its only caller is autosave_now (menu.c:708) right after a NULL read; on a card with no AUTOSAVE.JSN a residue > 2 (any heap pointer) logs 'read failed on existing file' and the file is never created, so nothing persists. Whether the slot holds >2 depends on what earlier calls left at that stack depth in a given build; that cannot be settled by reading. A serial log from a card with no AUTOSAVE.JSN would settle it.
results.fix_sketch: Use the existing fileExists() (fileio.c:209, zero-inits and checks stat) in autosave_now, or make getFileSize return 0 when stat() != 0; take sd_lock around the stat.

results.title: CONFIG.JSN read-modify-write is not locked across the cycle (UI task vs httpd)
results.claim: configSetStringSetting and configSetIntSetting do an unlocked read, modify, write of the whole CONFIG.JSN. They are called from several tasks: UI (machine, clk_*), httpd (broadcast, settings), and the Tape machine (tapelast at tape.c:48 and 1040). sd_lock is only held per read and per write, not across the cycle.
results.scenario: The UI task writes 'machine' while httpd writes 'broadcast', or Tape writes 'tapelast'. Both read the same old file, and the second writer's copy overwrites the first's key. A persisted machine choice or setting is silently rolled back. A failed read (NULL) also drops the write with no error.
results.reasoning: configSetStringSetting/configSetIntSetting, the Settings exit merge (menu.c:499-513) and three REST writers (rest-api.c:1229, 1826, 2317) each read, modify and rewrite the whole file with sd_lock held only inside the read and inside the write. Writers run on two tasks: UI (machine, clk_*, tapelast; the Tape calls at tape.c:48/1040 are UI context, not a third task) and httpd. If the prio-11 UI task completes a cycle between httpd's read and write, the UI's key is rolled back; a NULL read drops the write silently. The trigger needs a web settings write and a panel/remote-machine write within the same ~100 ms, which I could not show happens in an ordinary flow. 09-16 finding 4.2 fixed the page-lifetime snapshot rollback, not this.
results.fix_sketch: sd_lock is recursive: take it around the whole read-modify-write in one shared helper in menu_config.c and route configSet*, the Settings-exit merge and the three rest-api.c writers through it. Log when the read returns NULL.

results.title: initTimeshift NULL dereference when settings.tz_shift is missing
results.reasoning: initMenu (ui.c:345) runs after mountSDStorage (ui.c:330), which calls checkSDStructure (storage.c:50). That runs validateConfig, which requires settings to be an object and tz_shift a number (menu_config.c:152-153, 161-162); otherwise fileio.c:138-140 rewrites CONFIG.JSN with defaults that include tz_shift (fileio.c:55-56). REST is not started until ui.c:360, so nothing can remove the key in between, and a failed read is handled by the root != NULL check at line 11.

results.title: menuTFTPrintSettings: unterminated strncpy of passwd/apikey (>=32 chars) makes hideString's strlen over-read; NULL-deref part refuted
results.claim: menuTFTPrintSettings dereferences val->valuestring for ssid, passwd and apikey with no NULL or string-type check. It also does strncpy(buf, ..., 32) into buf[33] without terminating, so a value of 32 or more characters leaves buf[32] uninitialised. hideString then runs strlen over it.
results.scenario: settings.ssid, passwd or apikey is missing or a number (valuestring NULL), for example written by POST /settings. Opening the Settings page crashes the UI task. Separately, a 40-character Freesound API key makes strlen read past the 32-byte copy.
results.reasoning: The crash half is refuted: validateConfig() (menu_config.c:155-160, run at every boot from fileio.c:138) regenerates the config unless ssid/passwd/apikey are strings, and the only later writers create strings and never delete them (rest-api.c:1097-1111 is gated on j->valuestring; menu.c:584). The strncpy half is real: strncpy(buf, v, 32) into buf[33] leaves no NUL for a 40-char Freesound key or a long WiFi password, so hideString's strlen (string_tools.c:88) reads on up the UI task stack. It has no visible effect: len is clamped to 22, buf is memset and 22 stars are drawn either way. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Use strlcpy(buf, cJSON_IsString(val) ? val->valuestring : "", sizeof buf) and pass sizeof buf to hideString. Guard the ssid print with the same cJSON_IsString check that configGetStringSetting uses.

results.title: wifiSettingsChanged pairs file and in-memory settings by string-count index; strcmp on NULL valuestring
results.claim: wifiSettingsChanged pairs items by position. The counter i counts only string elements of the file's settings, but it indexes all elements of curSettings. val->valuestring is used without checking that val is a string.
results.scenario: If settings key order differs from ssid, passwd, apikey, tz_shift, ..., or a numeric key sits before ssid or passwd, the compare runs against the wrong key. It either misses a real WiFi change, so no reconnect, or spuriously reconnects. If val is a number, valuestring is NULL and strcmp crashes on Settings exit.
results.reasoning: i advances only on string elements of the file but indexes every element of curSettings, and val->valuestring goes to strcmp unchecked (line 32). With settings such as {"encres":4,"ssid":..}, ssid pairs with cur[0], a number, so strcmp(.., NULL) panics the UI task on every long-press out of Settings (menu.c:472), before anything is saved; a string before it gives a spurious reconnect instead. It does not fire on firmware-written configs: createConfigFile (fileio.c:49-52) puts ssid and passwd at 0 and 1, and every writer replaces in place or appends. It needs a CONFIG.JSN that was hand-edited or re-sorted by a tool with a numeric key ahead of ssid/passwd, which validateConfig accepts because it checks by name only.
results.fix_sketch: Drop the positional loop and compare by key: cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive(..., "ssid"/"passwd") on both objects, require cJSON_IsString on both, then strcmp. This is the same shape as the wifiChanged check in settings_post_handler (rest-api.c:1098-1104).

results.title: Settings text-entry finds ssid/passwd/apikey by array position 0..2, not by key
results.claim: The text-entry page finds ssid, passwd and apikey by array position (menu_pos 0..2), not by key. Accept replaces whichever key sits at that position. Position 0..2 is assumed to be ssid, passwd, apikey.
results.scenario: If CONFIG.JSN settings has a different key order, for example added by hand or rewritten by a tool, editing 'SSID' seeds and overwrites another key. It could put a WiFi password into 'machine' or 'tz_shift'. WiFi then fails to connect, or a setting is corrupted.
results.reasoning: Lines 562 and 582 use cJSON_GetArrayItem(settings, menu_pos), then replace whichever key sits there. The 09-16 triage note for 4.2 and the comment at menu.c:496 record the positional lookup as a constraint, not as a finding, so this is not KNOWN. It is correct for firmware-written configs (fileio.c:49-54 puts the three keys at 0..2 and no writer reorders them); it needs a hand-ordered or tool-sorted CONFIG.JSN. The finder overstates the damage: since the 4.2 fix only the own[] keys persist (menu.c:497), so 'machine' is not corrupted on the card and tz_shift is rewritten as a number at exit. The real effect is that the intended SSID/password/key edit is silently lost, another key's value is seeded on screen, and in a sorted file apikey (position 0) is overwritten by the SSID text and saved.
results.fix_sketch: Map menu_pos to a key table {"ssid","passwd","apikey"} and use cJSON_GetObjectItemCaseSensitive for the seed. On accept, replace or add by that key, as configSetStringSetting already does.

results.title: Tuner stays enabled when a web machine switch rebinds pages while the Tuner page is open
results.claim: A machine bind (for example the web EV_REMOTE_MACHINE switch) replaces all pages without running the page-exit code of whichever core page was open. If the Tuner page was open, tuner_set_enabled(false) never runs, and the tuner stays enabled.
results.scenario: The Tuner page is open and a web /remote/machine request switches the machine. The line-in tuner keeps running, costing about 40% of a core and PSRAM/scratch, and adding audio-loop load, until the user re-enters and leaves the Tuner page or calls /tuner/enable.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 4.6, on the Watch list and not fixed. It is still present: tuner_set_enabled(false) is called only from the Tuner page long-press (menu.c:858) and /tuner/enable (rest-api.c:2333); menuMachineBindNow and menuSwitchMachine do not call it. Nothing new to add: the cost is the rate-limited ~4 detections/s (CLAUDE.md: aus 504 -> ~545-585), not 40% of a core, and it clears on re-entering and leaving Tuner or GET /tuner/enable?on=0.
results.fix_sketch: Call tuner_set_enabled(false) in menuMachineBindNow before menusys_free; every bind lands on the machine's boot page, never on Tuner.

results.title: Timer tick events carry an uninitialised event_data pointer
results.reasoning: ev.event_data is indeed uninitialised in timerRepeatSlow/Fast and is forwarded (ui.c:173 -> menu.c:658 -> menu.c:76), but nothing reads it. Every page handler and every machine main_event either casts it to void or never references it (e.g. menu.c:847, tape_menu.c:1011, synth_menu.c:797); a grep of all ev_data/event_data uses in built code shows no dereference outside the EV_REMOTE_* branches (menu.c:609-634), which timer events never enter. The pointer is only passed through, so there is no crash path today. It is a latent hazard only.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: components/menu/cvmtx.c, cvmtx.h, wave_edit.c, wave_edit.h, text_entry.c, text_entry.h, sample_browser.c, sample_browser.h, clock_ui.c, clock_ui.h.

Also read: menutft.c (PrintChar, PrintAllCharSettings, Ellipsize), menutft_utils.c (GetCharPos), menu.c settings_input_def_handler (text_entry host), fs_menu.c fs_entry_handler (text_entry host), editor_menu.c (full, wave_edit host), editor.c (load, scan, audition), tape.c and tape_menu.c (cvmtx host), the cvmtx_init call and label/default array sizes in all 12 hosts, sample_ram.c, sample_list_recent.c, sampfile.c sample_name_id, and every sample_browser_selected() caller.

Checked and clean:
- text_entry buffer bounds. buf is 49 bytes, pos is at most maxlen (47 at most), the wheel index range matches C_MAX, and the write-then-clamp logic holds.
- cvmtx array indexing and load clamping. Label arrays all match their _N counts.
- wave_edit integer maths. long is 32-bit, but the values stay in range.
- sample_browser index bounds. SAMPLE_DIR_N is 7 and k_fold has 8 entries, so BR_NFOLD matches.

Not chased: configSetIntSetting rewrites the whole CONFIG.JSN four times per clock_ui_flush() (about 4 x 64 ms of SD I/O). That is the documented design, so I dropped it. Also dropped as cosmetic: the cvmtx page truncates amt to an int percent when drawing, while save rounds it. A 47-character entry made only of wide glyphs can run off the right edge of the text-entry page.

Everything in scope was read; nothing was skipped.

results.title: Editor Live strip is not repainted when the peak scan finishes after a panel load
results.claim: The Live page only repaints the waveform when the frame count changes. editor_load() sets ed.frames synchronously before the scan task fills ed.peaks, so nothing triggers a repaint when the scan finishes.
results.scenario: Load a long file through Setup > Source, then hold to open the Live page while scan_task is still running. live_full_redraw() draws the partly filled or all-zero peaks. When the scan ends, s_wave.frames already equals ed.frames, so the SLOW tick never redraws. The strip stays blank or partial until some other event repaints it, such as a cursor turn.
results.reasoning: editor_load() sets ed.frames before the scan task runs (editor.c:382), and editor_load_handler calls wave_sync() straight after (editor_menu.c:334), so s_wave.frames already equals ed.frames. Entering Live mid-scan draws the partly filled ed.peaks; the SLOW tick then only repaints the header, because the frames test at line 181 is false when the scan ends. The scan reads 2048 frames per 10 ms tick (about 2 s per 10 s of audio), so one hold from Setup reaches Live well before it finishes. The strip stays partial until an encoder turn or press calls wave_edit_draw().
results.fix_sketch: Latch that the strip was drawn while a scan was pending (set in live_full_redraw and on the SLOW tick from ed.scanning) and repaint on the SLOW tick when ed.scanning drops, alongside the existing frames test. Have editor_load() raise ed.scanning itself before xTaskCreate so the flag is never seen false before the task starts.

results.title: Playhead line does not draw a row below the waveform strip
results.reasoning: TFT_drawLine on a vertical line calls _drawFastVLine(x0, y0, y1-y0) (tft.c:212), which pushes exactly h pixels, rows y..y+h-1 (tft.c:178). With y1 = e->y + e->h that is rows e->y..e->y+e->h-1, the same rows draw_col() and draw_blit() clear. The 09-16 review also lists 'wave_edit playhead height' as checked clean.

results.title: sample_name_id() truncates stems over 31 chars and lists an id that cannot be opened
results.claim: sample_name_id() silently truncates any filename stem longer than 31 characters and still returns true. The browser lists the truncated id, but that id is not a real file name.
results.scenario: usr/ holds a 40-character file name, or two files that share the same first 31 characters. The browser and the REST list show the truncated id, and the two files collapse into one entry after dedup. Picking it calls sample_resolve()/fopen on the truncated name, so the load fails with 'cannot open'. The file is unreachable through the browser.
results.reasoning: CONFIG_FATFS_MAX_LFN is 64, so a 32-60 char stem reaches sample_name_id(), which cuts it to 31 chars and returns true. sample_list_dir, sample_list_recent_dir and sample_folder_counts then list or count that id, and the strcasecmp dedup merges two files sharing a 31-char prefix; sample_resolve() stats the truncated name, fails, and the load reports cannot open. One correction to the finder: GET /files does not show it, it skips over-long stems (rest-api.c:237), so only the panel browsers are affected. Web upload refuses such names, so it needs a file copied onto the card from a computer.
results.fix_sketch: Return false from sample_name_id() when the stem is SAMPLE_ID_LEN or longer, which is the same skip rule the /files walk already applies at rest-api.c:237. The browsers, the folder counts and the web list then agree.

results.title: cvmtx rearm read-then-clear on the audio task can lose a rearm from the UI or httpd task
results.claim: cvmtx_track() reads and clears rearm non-atomically in the audio task, while the UI and httpd tasks set it to 0xFFFF in cvmtx_load(), the menu handlers and cvmtx_rearm().
results.scenario: A preset load or a source change sets rearm = 0xFFFF between the audio task's read and its clear. The write is lost. The ABS entries are not recaptured, so capt[] and live[] keep the previous preset's state. A knob at a different position can then drive the destination straight away with a parameter jump, instead of waiting to pass the takeover threshold. The window is a couple of instructions, so this is rare.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 5.3, word for word the same two lines, placed on the Watch list as low consequence. The code is unchanged and the reason still holds: the window is two instructions and the result is one knob going live without takeover. The preset-load writer the finder adds (cvmtx_load line 325) is the same race and adds nothing new.

results.title: sample_list_recent_dir holds sd_lock across all folders and the in-RAM dedup
results.claim: sd_lock is held across the whole walk of all seven folders. The walk includes an O(n^2) strcasecmp dedup over up to SAMPLE_LIST_RECENT_MAX entries, and an O(MAX) oldest-scan for each file once the list is full.
results.scenario: On a card with hundreds of samples, opening a dated browser (Editor, Deck, Tape) while a streaming machine or audition is playing blocks every other sd_lock user for the length of the scan. The scan can take tens to hundreds of ms. Streaming readers underrun and the audio drops out.
results.reasoning: The lock is taken once at line 22 and released at line 70, covering up to seven folder reads plus the O(n^2) dedup and the evict scan; sample_list_dir and the /files walk release it per folder. Holding the bus for one folder's name scan is deliberate and measured at about 100 ms (rest-api.c:223-225), so the hold itself is not the defect, only its length. A dropout needs the hold to exceed the reader's ring slack: 1 s for sampplay (Editor audition), 4 s Sampler3, 8 s Deck. My estimate for a 500-file ALL view is 300-400 ms, so this likely needs a library of about 1000 files or more with the Editor audition playing; I could not establish the real hold time from reading.
results.fix_sketch: Take and give sd_lock per folder inside the di loop, as sample_list_dir (sample_ram.c:54-70) does, so readers get the bus between folders. If needed, collect names under the lock and run the dedup/evict pass after releasing it.

results.title: No other task rebuilds the shared list buffers under the open browser
results.reasoning: The claimed web path does not exist: s3_list_samples() (sampler3.c:450) has no callers anywhere in the tree, only its declaration in sampler3_priv.h:220. The only callers of sample_list_recent_dir and sample_list_shared_dir are sample_browser.c:57-58, which run on the UI task, and remote encoder events go through the same UI queue. sample_ram.h:35 documents the buffer as shared with one browser at a time, and that holds.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: components/rest-api/rest-api.c (all 2739 lines), components/wifi/wifi.c, components/wifi/espnow_probe.c, components/wifi/include/wifi.h and espnow_probe.h, components/freesound/freesound.c, components/freesound/include/freesound.h, components/rest-api/include/rest-api.h and CMakeLists.txt.
