I also read parts of components/util/sampfile.c (sample_resolve and sample_name_id), util/string_tools.c, util/sampimport.c (scan and start), audio/audio.c (remote trig/CV, soft MIDI, icepush start), machine/machine_core.c (machine_activate), menu/menu.c (remote event consumers) and menu/setup_menu.c (remote json and adjust). I did not read machine_freesound, the machines' web_uris handlers, or fileio.c beyond its sd_lock usage; those are outside this scope.

Checked and found safe:
- Fixed buffers: /files fidx and obuf batching, sysinfo, status, tftread, ice and setup_menu_remote_json all stay within their buffers.
- Machine URI swap: machine_activate clears s_active first, so the httpd-side swap ordering holds.
- SAMPLE_ID_LEN: name[32] buffers match SAMPLE_ID_LEN.
- Web UI events: the queued event pointers are freed by their menu.c consumers.

The freesound.c instance_request path has real bugs: read_len is uint32_t so a -1 error return is never caught, content_length is uint32_t so a -1 (chunked) response wraps and overflows the 512-byte buffer, NULL dereferences on non-matching JSON, and asserts on open failure and on the missing /pool directory. freesoundGetInstance is called only from components/machine_sampler2, which is not built, so I did not report them. If sampler2 is ever resurrected they need fixing first.

Dropped as low value:
- mod_upload does not run mod_name_safe on its Name header, but it is limited to module extensions.
- Unlocked /remote/setup GET and freesound_token races.
- /bootlogo deletes the existing logo on a rejected upload.
- espnow init leaves state half-initialised after a failed add_peer.
- settings_post ReplaceItemInObject leaks when the key is absent.

results.title: GET /files/raw `../` traversal to CONFIG.JSN
results.reasoning: The handler does pass an unvalidated name, but a `..` path segment cannot be opened on this build. IDF 4.3 FatFS has FF_FS_RPATH=0 (~/esp/esp-idf-v4.3/components/fatfs/src/ffconf.h:171) with LFN on, so create_name() strips the trailing dots and returns FR_INVALID_NAME (ff.c:2869-2875); esp_vfs does no path normalisation. Every stat() in sample_resolve and the final fopen("/sdcard/usr/../CONFIG.JSN") therefore fail and the handler returns 404. A '/' in the name only reaches subfolders under /sdcard/usr, where no credentials live.

results.title: DELETE/move/rename `../` traversal deletes CONFIG.JSN
results.reasoning: Same guard as #0: FF_FS_RPATH=0 (ffconf.h:171) makes FatFS reject any `..` segment with FR_INVALID_NAME (ff.c:2869-2875). So remove("/sdcard/usr/../CONFIG.JSN") fails, and the stat() that gates each rename in move/rename (rest-api.c:383, 468) fails too. The name can contain '/', but that only addresses audio/.JSN/.OT files in subfolders under usr/, which this unauthenticated endpoint may delete anyway. Nothing outside usr/ is reachable.

results.title: PUT /drop_sample `Name: ../CONFIG` overwrites CONFIG.JSN
results.reasoning: f_open("/usr/../CONFIG.RAW") at rest-api.c:1389 returns FR_INVALID_NAME because FF_FS_RPATH=0 (ffconf.h:171; ff.c:2869-2875 rejects dot segments). The handler then returns 500 "SD open failed" at lines 1391-1396, before any body is read and before writeJSONFile() at 1464 runs. Even if reached, writeJSONFile's VFS fopen on the `..` path would fail the same way. A '/' in the header only places the upload in a subfolder of usr/.

results.title: sample_resolve() stat sweep without sd_lock in /peaks, /files/raw, rename
results.claim: sample_resolve() does up to 28 stat() calls on the SD card and takes no sd_lock itself. /peaks (here), /files/raw (lines 527-531) and the post-rename sample_resolve_aux (line 482) call it without holding sd_lock. CLAUDE.md says every SD I/O burst must hold sd_lock, because the raw audio reader bypasses the VFS lock.
results.scenario: The web page fetches /peaks for each file in the list while Deck, Sampler or Keys stream from SD through raw FatFS reads. The unlocked stat() sweep from httpd races those reads on the SDMMC bus. This gives read errors or audio ring underruns, and the CLAUDE.md note says it can wedge the card.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 6.12, on the Watch list as low consequence, and it is still unfixed at lines 2590, 527-531 and 482. The Watch reasoning still holds: each VFS stat takes the vfs_fat lock, and FatFS itself is built with FF_FS_REENTRANT=1 (ffconf.h:287), so a stat cannot interleave with a raw f_read on the bus. The claimed card wedge or corruption is overstated; nothing new to add.

results.title: Upload finishing during an import scan is never converted
results.claim: The return value is ignored. samp_import_start() returns -1 while an import scan is running. An upload that finishes during a scan never gets converted, because the busy scan may already have passed its folder or skipped it because it was still open for write.
results.scenario: The web uploads several MP3s or 24-bit WAVs back to back. Upload 1 kicks the importer, which takes tens of seconds. Upload 2 arrives during the scan and is either skipped as locked or missed after the readdir has passed. Upload 2's own samp_import_start() returns -1 and is dropped. The MP3 bytes stay under a .RAW name, get a .JSN, and play as loud noise until some later upload or POST /import happens to rescan.
results.reasoning: samp_import_start() returns -1 while busy (sampimport.c:446) and there is no pending-rescan flag; the only other caller is POST /import. The web batch sends mp3/wav/aif as-is, back to back (index.html DEV_EXTS 'native'), so upload N+1 is open for write while upload N's scan runs. The scan's fopen of that file fails FR_LOCKED (FF_FS_LOCK=5) and it is skipped (sampimport.c:171-175, 352-354), or its dir slot is already behind the readdir cursor. If the upload then completes while the scan is still walking the other six folders, its own kick is dropped; an MP3 stays under .RAW, sampfile_probe falls back to headerless RAW (sampfile_int.h:151) and it plays as noise until a manual Rescan or a later upload.
results.fix_sketch: In sampimport.c add a volatile rescan-requested flag: samp_import_start() sets it and returns 0 when samp_import_busy is already true. import_task repeats the folder walk while the flag was set during the pass, and only then clears samp_import_busy.

results.title: POST /ota does not refuse while a recording is active
results.claim: POST /ota does not refuse while recording_is_active(). POST /reboot deliberately returns 409 in that case because a reboot destroys the PSRAM take. OTA ends in the same esp_restart().
results.scenario: A Sampler, Tape or bounce take is in progress (the recording writer is open) and someone runs tools/ota.sh. The handler mutes audio, flashes and restarts. The in-progress take is lost, or the WAV is left with a stale header for the probe to self-heal.
results.reasoning: ota_post_handler has no recording_is_active() check and ends in esp_restart() at line 2522, while reboot_post_handler refuses with 409 at 2539 for exactly this reason. tools/ota.sh only reads /ota/state before posting, so nothing outside the firmware guards it either. rec_writer_task never syncs during a take (recording.c:166-198; sampwav_finish and fclose run only at the end), so a restart mid-take leaves an unclosed file with no sidecar and the take is lost. It needs a flash while a take or bounce is running.
results.fix_sketch: Put the same recording_is_active() 409 block that reboot_post_handler uses at the top of ota_post_handler, before esp_ota_begin(). Consider also refusing when recording_is_prepared().

results.title: restartWifi aborts on rejected STA credentials, causing boot loop
results.reasoning: I disassembled IDF 4.3 libnet80211 wifi_set_config_process (dump written to the session scratchpad, outside the repo). The STA branch returns only ESP_ERR_INVALID_ARG for a NULL config or ESP_ERR_WIFI_MODE when the mode has no STA; the strnlen<8 check returning ESP_ERR_WIFI_PASSWORD (0x300b) is only in the AP-interface branch. Over-long values are truncated by strlcpy (rest-api.c:1221-1223, wifi.c:214-217) and restartWifi sets STA mode first when in AP fallback (wifi.c:329-333). A short or wrong password therefore just fails to connect and takes the 6.4 AP fallback; the garbage-config abort was 6.5, already fixed.

results.title: PUT /drop_ot ignores f_write result, publishes short .OT
results.claim: In PUT /drop_ot the f_write result is not checked, unlike the drop_sample and module upload paths. A failed or short write is still renamed into place as the .OT slice map.
results.scenario: The card is full or a write errors midway through the 832-byte body. The handler still f_unlinks the old <NAME>.OT, renames the truncated temp over it, and returns 200. The old good slice map is lost and the slicer applies a corrupt or partial one.
results.reasoning: Incomplete fix of 6.8: mod_upload (2102-2109) and drop_sample (1424-1438) now check the write, but drop_ot at line 2172 still ignores both the FRESULT and bw, and the f_close result at 2175. On a full card or write error the handler still unlinks the existing <NAME>.OT, renames the short temp into place and returns 200. The finder overstates one part: slicer_parse_ot rejects a file that is not 832 bytes (slicer_ot.c:62), so no corrupt map is applied. The real loss is the old good slice map, with a false success reported.
results.fix_sketch: Copy the mod_upload_handler check: on wr != FR_OK or bw != ret, f_close, f_unlink(OT_TMP) and return 500 "SD write failed". Also check the f_close result before f_unlink(path) and f_rename.

results.title: Web rename still enforces the 8-char uppercase rule after long filenames
results.claim: The web rename still enforces the stale 8.3 rule (1-8 characters, A-Z 0-9 _ only), although long filenames are on and SAMPLE_ID_LEN is 32. Valid ids such as lowercase names or 9-31 character names are refused.
results.scenario: A sample uploaded through the web as "Moog_Voyager_G3" (15 chars) can be listed and deleted but never renamed to another long or lowercase name. The rename returns 400 "Name must be 1-8 chars", while drop_sample accepts names up to 31 chars.
results.reasoning: files_rename_handler (rest-api.c:432-444) still rejects any target that is not 1-8 chars of A-Z 0-9 _, while drop_sample (rest-api.c:1350) and the page's upload/Freesound filters accept up to 31 chars of a-zA-Z0-9_-. plans/long-filenames-20260913.md step 5 says to relax /files/rename and the input maxlength, and neither was done; the 09-16 review does not record it (theme A covered only buffer sizes). The finder's scenario is slightly off: through the page the user never sees the 400, because libCommit (index.html:1248) uppercases, strips and slices to 8 before sending and the input has maxlength=8 (index.html:1171), so the name is silently shortened (e.g. a Keys note suffix is lost); the 400 only shows on a direct REST call. No memory risk: name[32]/to[32] and the 80-byte path buffers fit a 31-char id.
results.fix_sketch: In files_rename_handler size name/to as SAMPLE_ID_LEN, refuse tl >= SAMPLE_ID_LEN and allow the same charset the upload path uses (a-zA-Z0-9_-). In index.html set the rename input maxlength to 31 and make libCommit use the same filter and substring(0,31) as the batch-name code at line 1382 (the batch input at 1359 also still has maxlength 8), then run html/convert.sh. Note the 'target already exists' probe will refuse a case-only rename on FAT.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: components/rest-api/html/index.html, lines 1-3766. That covers the CSS (skimmed for anything behavioural), the whole static markup and the whole script. I cross-checked JS endpoints against the registered URIs and getElementById targets against the static markup, and read the firmware side of /settings and /files/rename. Nothing in scope was skipped.

Dropped or not reported:
- cvLast is declared twice (line 2704 and line 3693). It is harmless because the scope table #scopetb is absent and updateScope returns early.
- Cosmetic issues: the batch list shows the grey tail from character 8 although 31 are stored, and the batch rename input has maxlength=8.
- Concurrent loadFiles() responses can resurrect a just-deleted row, and any background loadFiles() resets an in-progress inline rename. Both are minor.
- Most rpSetCard re-renders discard typed but unsaved SSID and password text.
- glTz and similar controls compute from a stale rpGlob for 300 ms.
- The MIDI WebSocket reconnects every 3 s forever and ignores the WEB poll pause.
- Passwords travel in the query string on /ice/start.
- I did not read the firmware side of the remaining endpoints beyond the checks above, for example the body-size limits on /remote/params.

results.title: webPoll() throws on missing #ptag, so the Poll row never shows PAUSED
results.claim: webPoll() dereferences #ptag, but no element with id="ptag" exists in the page (only a .ptag CSS rule at line 87). getElementById returns null, so this throws a TypeError.
results.scenario: User clicks the WEB > Poll row. webPaused flips to true, then the throw skips webDraw() and pollStatus(). The row never changes to PAUSED and no paused tag appears. pollStatus() and sysPoll() now silently stop, so the page looks live but is frozen. Clicking again flips it back, but the throw still skips the catch-up pollStatus() and the row redraw. The 'quiet while judging audio' control has no visible state.
results.reasoning: No element with id="ptag" exists; only the .ptag CSS rule at line 87 survives (the element went with the header in 499b75e, 09-10). webPaused flips first, so pausing itself works (pollStatus :3724 and sysPoll :2515 both return), but the TypeError skips webDraw() and the catch-up pollStatus(). The row keeps reading LIVE until some other webDraw() runs, and no paused tag ever appears. index.html was excluded from the 09-16 review, so this is not recorded there.
results.fix_sketch: Either restore a PAUSED somewhere always visible (the CSS rule is still there), or null-guard the lookup the way webDraw() does with #webslot. Keep webDraw() and the resume pollStatus() after it.

results.title: rdState() throws on missing #rdnote; Radio card never renders state or stations
results.claim: rdState() first dereferences #rdnote, which does not exist in the markup. The .then callback throws before it renders anything, and the .catch handler (line 2774) dereferences the same missing element and throws again.
results.scenario: Switch to the Radio machine. machCardPoll starts rdState on a 1 s interval. Every call throws at its first line, so the NOW PLAYING state, title, buffer bar and the whole station button list (#rdstations) are never built. The Radio card is a dead form: you cannot pick a station from the list, and saved stations never appear. The interval keeps firing a GET /radio/state every second and leaks an unhandled rejection each time.
results.reasoning: #rdcard (lines 787-800) has rdstate/rdinfo/rdbuf/rdstations but no rdnote; it was dropped in 89be785 (09-10) when the tab became a card. The first statement of the .then throws, the .catch at :2774 dereferences the same null and throws again, so #rdstations is never built and the state/title/buffer never update. machCardPoll (:3303) still fires it every 1 s. Play-by-URL, Save and Stop are separate functions and still work, so the card is not entirely dead.
results.fix_sketch: Delete the two #rdnote lines (the card is only shown while Radio is active, so the 'switch to Radio' note has no job), leaving .catch(function(){}) as the other pollers do.

results.title: edState() throws on missing #ednote; Editor card never builds its op buttons
results.claim: edState() dereferences #ednote, which is not in the page. The success path throws before setting the state text, progress bar, range or op buttons, and the .catch (line 3259) throws again on the same element.
results.scenario: Switch to the Editor machine. #edops is only populated inside edState after this line, so no operation buttons (normalize, reverse, fade, ...) are ever created. The Editor card cannot start an operation. Progress and 'created XXX' are never shown. The 1 s interval keeps polling /edit/state.
results.reasoning: #edcard (lines 802-816) has edsel/edops/edrange/edstate/edout/edbar/edm but no ednote (removed in 89be785). The .then throws on its first line and the .catch at :3259 throws on the same null, so #edops is never populated and state, progress, range and 'created X' never show. edLoad() still fills the file select, but with no op buttons edApply() cannot be reached from the page.
results.fix_sketch: Delete the two #ednote lines, same as the Radio fix; the card only exists while Editor is active.

results.title: Library rename is still 8-char: an unchanged commit truncates a long name
results.claim: In-place rename still uses the old 8-char/8.3 rules (maxlength=8 on the input, slice(0,8), and a strip of everything except A-Z0-9_). Sample ids are now up to 31 chars and may contain '-' (Freesound names allow it). The rename box is pre-filled with the full current name, so an unchanged commit is not a no-op.
results.scenario: A file named KICK-01 or MOOG_C4_LONGNAME is listed. The user clicks the name and then OK (or Enter) without editing. The value is reduced to KICK01 or MOOG_C4_, which differs from name, so POST /files/rename renames the file. The long or hyphenated name is silently lost, and the truncated name can collide with or overwrite an existing sample. Any keys in presets that reference the old name are orphaned.
results.reasoning: The input at :1171 is pre-filled with the full name (maxlength=8 does not trim a scripted value), and libCommit strips to A-Z0-9_ and slice(0,8) before comparing with name, so OK/Enter on MOOG_C4_LONGNAME posts a rename to MOOG_C4_. The server has the same leftover: rest-api.c:432-437 refuses any target over 8 chars. The finder's overwrite claim is wrong: rest-api.c:449-454 refuses an existing target, so a collision gives an alert, not a clobber. No audio is lost; the long name is, and presets holding the old id are orphaned.
results.fix_sketch: Page: return early when el.value===name, and raise maxlength/slice to 31 with the same charset the upload uses. Server: change the 'tl > 8' check at rest-api.c:434 to 'tl >= SAMPLE_ID_LEN' and widen the charset to match; from_p/to_p[80] already fit 19+31+5.

results.title: A machine switch made on the panel leaves the old machine's cards and rpData in place
results.claim: The page never re-reads /remote/params, /remote/setup, the CV matrix or the FX card when the active machine changes. rpLoad() is only called from loadRemote, remMach (web-initiated), rpApply, clkApply and Reload. A machine switch made on the panel only toggles card visibility (capsApply) and leaves the old machine's forms and rpData in place.
results.scenario: The unit is on Synth and the page has loaded. The user switches to Keys or Tape with the encoder. The MATRIX, FX, Setup and ADVANCED cards still show Synth's data. Pressing Apply (or a matrix or FX Apply) posts the whole stale Synth preset (mxs/mxa/mxm arrays sized for Synth, fxsl, cut/res, ...) to POST /remote/params on the new machine. Shared key names are applied and arrays of the wrong length are loaded, which corrupts the new machine's settings and autosave. Setup row indices posted from the stale screen hit different rows.
results.reasoning: pollStatus only assigns curMach; capsApply (:3544) toggles visibility and nothing calls rpLoad on a change (callers are :1689, :2584, :2656, :2686, :3276 only). Synth, Keys and Tape share the MATRIX/FX/SETUP caps, so the stale cards stay visible, and Apply posts the old machine's full JSON to the new machine's preset_load (menu.c:618-627) with autosave. cvmtx_load bounds and clamps the arrays (cvmtx.c:290-313), so it is wrong routing and wrong shared keys, not memory corruption. A stale Setup click steps a different row once, then suLoad corrects the card.
results.fix_sketch: In pollStatus, compare d.machine with the previous curMach and call rpLoad() when it changed (it already re-runs suLoad/glLoad); remMach's 2.5 s timer then becomes a fallback. Optionally have rpApply refuse when rpData was loaded for a different machine.

results.title: rpApply posts the whole load-time snapshot, reverting device-side edits since
results.claim: Apply posts a full copy of the last-loaded snapshot (rpData) with only the DOM fields overlaid. The page keeps a private copy of device state that is refreshed only on rpLoad. Any parameter changed on the device, by a knob, the panel or autosave since the last load is sent back with its old value.
results.scenario: The page loads. The player turns K6 (cut), edits a Setup row or a preset key on the panel, or another browser tab applies. The user then presses Apply in the CV MATRIX or FX card. The whole stale snapshot is POSTed to /remote/params and reverts every untouched key to its value at load time. The CLAUDE.md note says knob-owned params reject remote writes only until the knob moves, so this also fights the knobs.
results.reasoning: rpData is set only in rpLoad (:2608) and after an Apply (:2656); nothing refreshes it from the 500 ms poll. rpApply clones it, overlays DOM fields that were themselves rendered at load, and posts every key, and each preset_load applies every key present (e.g. synth.c:353-357 cut/res, then cvmtx_load sets rearm=0xFFFF so the knob must move again to retake). A K6 turn or a panel Setup edit made after the page loaded is therefore rolled back by any matrix/FX/Advanced Apply. Same root as #4's Apply consequence, but #4's fix does not cover it.
results.fix_sketch: Keep a pristine copy taken at rpLoad (fxHarvest writes into rpData, so rpData cannot be the baseline) and post only keys that differ from it; preset_load already treats an absent key as keep, and cvmtx_load documents a node with no matrix as a partial update (cvmtx.c:287-289). Send mxs/mxa/mxm together when any of them changed.

results.title: Musical typing eats Cmd/Ctrl shortcuts and sticks notes on blur or octave change
results.claim: Musical typing ignores ctrl/meta/alt, and nothing releases held notes on window blur, tab hide or focus change. midiHeldClear() also drops the JS state without sending note-offs. The 2 s 'h' heartbeat (line 2937) keeps the device gate alive for as long as midiHeld is non-empty.
results.scenario: On macOS, press Cmd+C or Cmd+R while the page has focus. 'c' or 'r' fires midiOn and preventDefault, which also blocks the browser shortcut. keyup is never delivered for keys pressed while Cmd is held, so midiHeld keeps the note. The heartbeat refreshes the module's 5 s gate timeout every 2 s, and Synth or Keys drones until Space, Esc or Panic. The same happens if the user holds Z and Alt-Tabs away, because the keyup goes to another window. Changing octave with '-' or '=' while a key is down calls midiHeldClear() with no note-off, leaving up to 5 s of hung note.
results.reasoning: The keydown handler has no ctrl/meta/alt check and #midityping is checked by default (:728), on every machine, so Cmd+R/Cmd+C call preventDefault and midiOn. MIDI has only a pagehide handler (:2938); the blur/visibilitychange release at the end of the remHold block covers soft trigs only, so a keyup lost to another window leaves the note in midiHeld and the 2 s heartbeat (:2937) keeps refreshing the 5 s gate timeout (audio.c:147-155). midiOct calls midiHeldClear() with no note-off, so the device note hangs until the timeout. The Cmd case relies on macOS not delivering keyup while Meta is held, which is standard browser behaviour; the blur case needs nothing beyond the code.
results.fix_sketch: Return early in keydown when ev.metaKey||ev.ctrlKey||ev.altKey. Add midiSend('x');midiHeldClear() to the existing blur/visibilitychange listeners beside holdDropAll. In midiOct, release held notes with midiOff (as the Space branch does) before changing midiBase.

results.title: Batch upload names can collide after sanitise/truncate; later file overwrites earlier
results.claim: Upload names are derived from a lossy sanitize (strip non-[A-Za-z0-9_], truncate to 31, empty becomes FILE). There is no duplicate detection within the batch or against the library, and /drop_sample writes to usr/<NAME>.RAW verbatim.
results.scenario: Dropping a folder containing 'Vintage_Drum_Machine_Kick_Sample_01.wav' and '..._02.wav' (both truncate to the same 31 chars). Likewise 'Snare-1.wav' and 'Snare 1.wav' (both become Snare1), or several files whose base sanitizes to empty (all become FILE). Each later PUT silently overwrites the earlier upload, and the summary still reports 'N uploaded'. Files that match an existing library name are also overwritten without warning.
results.reasoning: fileMeta strips to [a-zA-Z0-9_] and nameOf cuts to 31 or falls back to FILE; stageBatch and doBatchUpload never compare names within the batch or against libFiles. The server opens usr/<NAME>.RAW with FA_CREATE_ALWAYS (rest-api.c:1389), so a second PUT with the same name replaces the first and the summary still counts both as uploaded. The staging list does show the names, but line 1365 appends base.substring(8) in grey after the full 31-char name (an 8.3 leftover, as is maxlength=8 at :1359), which garbles long names and hides a collision. Replacing an existing library sample by re-uploading its name may be intended; the intra-batch loss is not.
results.fix_sketch: In stageBatch/renderBatch, detect repeated nameOf() values in the batch and names already in libFiles; mark those rows and either block Upload or suffix _2, _3 within 31 chars. Fix the leftovers in the same pass: maxlength 31 at :1359 and the grey tail at :1365 to substring(31).

results.title: Drop/picker/row buttons mutate batchFiles during an upload; next() indexes it with stale i and N
results.claim: The dropzone and picker stay live during doBatchUpload, and stageBatch replaces the global batchFiles array while next() indexes it with a captured N and i. There is no busy guard.
results.scenario: An upload of 5 files is in progress. The user drops 1 more file. batchFiles is now length 1 while i=2 and N=5. On the next step next() reads batchFiles[i] as undefined, and nameOf(b) throws a TypeError inside a promise callback. finish() is never called. The Cancel button and progress bar stay on screen and Upload/Clear never return. Also, the 1.5 s clearBatch timer after a finished upload wipes any batch staged in that window.
results.reasoning: dz.ondrop and #fi onchange (1445, 890) call stageBatch unconditionally, and the per-row rename/remove buttons (1366-1367, removeBatch splice at 1386) also stay live; doBatchUpload only hides Upload/Clear. next() (1415) reads batchFiles[i] against the captured N, so a shorter array gives undefined and nameOf(b) throws inside okcb's promise callback; finish() never runs, Cancel finds curXhr null and never calls next(), and Upload/Clear stay hidden until reload. A longer replacement batch instead uploads from index i of the new list and skips its first i files. The unconditional setTimeout(clearBatch,1500) at 1404 also wipes a batch staged within 1.5 s of a finished upload.
results.fix_sketch: Add a batchBusy flag following the existing scrBusy pattern (2872-2897): set it in doBatchUpload, clear it in finish(), and have onFiles/removeBatch/renameBatch return while it is set. Let next() iterate a snapshot taken at start (var list=batchFiles.slice()), and keep the clearBatch timer id so stageBatch can clearTimeout it.

results.title: esc() does not escape ' or \ but names are placed in single-quoted JS inside onclick
results.claim: File and module names are put inside single-quoted JS string literals in onclick attributes (lines 1170-1180, 1197, 1101), but esc() does not escape ' or \. Names come from the SD card and can hold any FAT character, up to 31 chars.
results.scenario: A sample or module named e.g. Don't_stop.mod, or one copied from a Mac with an apostrophe, produces del('Don't_stop'), a JS syntax error. Delete, rename and move on that row silently do nothing. A crafted name such as x');fetch('/reboot',{method:'POST'});(' (31 chars) runs as script in the page when the row's rename or delete is clicked. Names arrive over an unauthenticated PUT /drop_sample or from a shared card.
results.reasoning: esc() (1260) handles only & < > ", and the names go into '...' JS literals at 1101, 1170, 1172, 1175, 1180 and 1197. /files emits the raw FatFS stem through cJSON (rest-api.c:288) with no character filter, and drop_sample's cleanStringSpace only touches spaces, backslashes and control chars, so a card loaded from a Mac or a raw PUT can hold an apostrophe; the handler then fails to parse and delete, rename and move are dead on that row (same for delMod on a module like Don't.mod). The finder's example payload cannot be a filename (FAT forbids / and :, and it is 39 chars, not 31), but a shorter one such as ');alert(1);(' would run; the LAN is unauthenticated anyway, so the practical defect is the dead row.
results.fix_sketch: Add one helper for JS-string context (escape \ and ' first, then esc()) and use it at every onclick site listed. Alternatively carry the name in a data-name attribute, as the canvas.wf rows already do at 1193, and read this.dataset.name in the handler.

results.title: pollStatus has no in-flight guard; polls queued behind a stalled httpd flush as a burst
results.claim: pollStatus has no in-flight guard, and each tick also fires bncPoll, bcastPoll (which calls icePoll) and possibly scrPoll. That is four unguarded requests per 500 ms tick. If the device answers slower than 500 ms, requests stack.
results.scenario: While the module is busy (SD-heavy work, a /files stream, an OTA or Freesound download, or radio starving internal RAM), responses take over 0.5 s. Each tick opens another 4 requests on top of the pending ones. Eight or more concurrent sockets from one tab fill the fixed lwip pool (10 sockets, httpd takes 9) and every outbound or other request fails. CLAUDE.md records that 4 Hz polling was already audible in peak block cost. The tab keeps piling on until it is closed.
results.reasoning: The guard is missing (3723-3752), but the stated consequence does not hold: browsers cap about 6 connections per host, httpd is capped at max_open_sockets=8 with LRU purge (rest-api.c:2694-2703) and CONFIG_LWIP_MAX_SOCKETS is 16, so one tab cannot fill the pool. The secondary polls (bncPoll, bcastPoll+icePoll, scrPoll) fire only from a /status response (3749), so during a stall only one /status per tick queues, not four. What remains is that httpd is a single task, so a long PUT /drop_sample or /files stream queues two /status per second in the browser, and when it ends they are served back to back, each spawning three more requests. Whether that burst is audible (CLAUDE.md: 4 Hz polling was) cannot be established by reading.
results.fix_sketch: Add a stBusy flag as scrShot does with scrBusy (2872-2897): return if set, set before the fetch, clear in both the then and catch paths. Or re-arm with setTimeout after each response instead of setInterval.

results.title: fsPoll (700 ms /fs/state) never stops unless a done/error response parses
results.claim: The download progress poll only stops when a response with phase done or error parses. A fetch failure is swallowed by .catch(function(){}), and machCardPoll never clears fsPoll when the Freesound machine is left.
results.scenario: Start a Freesound download, then switch machines from the panel (or the unit reboots or crashes mid-download). /fs/state now returns 404, so r.json() fails and the catch does nothing. The 700 ms interval polls forever. The progress bar stays visible with the last message, and each poll burns a socket while the unit is otherwise busy.
results.reasoning: fsPoll is cleared only at 1636 and 1639; machCardPoll('Freesound',false) clears only fsResPoll (3300-3301). After a machine switch /fs/state is an unregistered machine URI, so the 404 text fails r.json() and the empty catch (1645) keeps the interval running with the progress bar left visible. Switching back or rebooting does not end it either: fsnd_start resets phase to idle when no pipeline is busy (fs_machine.c:747-751), and the else branch at 1641 treats idle as progress, showing 'idle 0%' forever. The poll also ignores webPaused, so it keeps hitting httpd while audio is being judged.
results.fix_sketch: In machCardPoll's Freesound off branch also clear fsPoll and hide #fspr. In fsState treat !r.ok, phase==='idle' and a few consecutive fetch failures as terminal (clear the interval, hide the bar), and return early when webPaused.

results.title: saveSet always posts ssid; firmware stores an empty ssid and restarts WiFi with it
results.claim: g() returns '' when the row does not exist or was rendered blank. saveSet() always sends ssid, and the firmware replaces the stored ssid with any non-null string, including ''. Only passwd and apikey are guarded against empty.
results.scenario: The Save button lives outside the screen and is present before glLoad has rendered. Press Save before the GLOBAL screen exists, or after /settings failed so glLoad rendered {} with a blank SSID row, for example when only the hostname was meant to change. POST /settings sets ssid to '', and the unit loses its WiFi network on the next boot, so it comes up unreachable until the card's CONFIG.JSN is edited.
results.reasoning: g() returns '' when #gsSsid is absent, and the Save button is rendered by globCard (2435) even while rpGlob is null and the screen is an empty div (2430). glLoad's J() turns a failed /settings into {} (2354), so the SSID row then renders blank. settings_post_handler replaces ssid for any non-null string (rest-api.c:1097-1100), unlike the strlen guards on passwd (1102) and apikey (1110), sets wifiChanged and calls restartWifi with the empty SSID 500 ms later (1234-1238), so the unit drops off the LAN at once, not only on next boot. Recovery is less dire than claimed: the panel Settings page can re-enter the SSID and the 6.4 AP fallback exists.
results.fix_sketch: In settings_post_handler give ssid the same strlen(j->valuestring) > 0 guard that passwd and apikey have (rest-api.c:1102, 1110). In saveSet include only keys whose input element exists, and skip the POST when rpGlob is not loaded.

results.title: convertAudio closes its AudioContext only on successful decode
results.claim: The AudioContext is closed only in the success .then. If decodeAudioData rejects (unsupported or corrupt file), the context is never closed. The code's own comment notes browsers cap live contexts at about 6.
results.scenario: A batch or repeated drops contain files the browser cannot decode: FLAC on Safari, .m4a on Firefox, or truncated or renamed files. Each failure leaks one AudioContext. After about 6, new AC() throws or decodeAudioData stops working, so every later conversion in that tab fails (as 'error') until the page is reloaded, even for good files.
results.reasoning: ac.close() sits only in the success then (1303); a decodeAudioData rejection skips it and failcb just counts a failure. fileMeta (1340-1343) classes every unknown extension as 'audio', so any non-decodable file in a drop takes this path. Whether leaked contexts ever reach a cap depends on the browser (older Chrome capped at 6 and Safari has a low cap; current engines may garbage-collect or have no cap), which cannot be established by reading.
results.fix_sketch: Decode with an OfflineAudioContext, which the function already uses at 1306 and which holds no hardware context: new OfflineAudioContext(2,1,44100).decodeAudioData(ab). Or close ac in a rejection handler that rethrows.

results.title: fsChip escapes ' but not backslash in the onclick JS string
results.claim: Search-query chips escape ' but not backslash, and the query comes from the device's recents/saved store, which anyone on the LAN can fill through the unauthenticated POST /fs/query.
results.scenario: A stored query ending in a backslash, or of the form \');alert(1);// , gives fsChipGo('\') (syntax error, chip dead) or closes the string early and runs injected JS when the chip is clicked. The payload persists in the device's recents and executes for whoever next opens the Freesound card.
results.reasoning: fs_query_handler url-decodes q with no character filter (fs_web.c:160-173), a successful search stores it via fs_query_remember (fs_machine.c:591), and /fs/results returns it through cJSON (fs_web.c:210-213), so a backslash reaches fsChip intact. esc(q).replace(/'/g,"\\'") leaves it alone: a query ending in \ yields fsChipGo('...\') (parse error, chip dead), and \');alert(1);// yields fsChipGo('\\');alert(1);//') which runs on click. It needs an API key set and a search that returns 200, and the store persists in the preset. Given the unauthenticated LAN (OTA, reboot) the injection adds little; the practical defect is the dead chip.
results.fix_sketch: Escape backslashes before apostrophes (replace(/\\/g,'\\\\') then the existing ' replace), ideally through the same JS-string helper as finding 9. Or put the query in a data-q attribute and call fsChipGo(this.dataset.q).

results.title: wfCache is keyed by name only and never invalidated
results.claim: The waveform thumbnail cache is keyed by sample name only and is never invalidated on delete, overwrite, upload or edit. After a rename the old key stays cached too.
results.scenario: Delete KICK, upload a different KICK (or an Editor or Tape op re-creating the same id), or re-record over a REC name. The row draws the old file's waveform from wfCache until the page is reloaded.
results.reasoning: wfCache is touched only at 1205, 1223 and 1225; del(), libCommit(), finish() and pollImport() never drop entries. PUT /drop_sample opens with FA_CREATE_ALWAYS (rest-api.c:1389), so re-uploading a changed file under the same name, or delete then upload, leaves the row painting the old peaks until the page is reloaded. A 'native' upload can also be cached from its pre-conversion bytes if /peaks is fetched before the importer replaces the file. Display only.
results.fix_sketch: Delete wfCache[name] in del() on success, for both names in libCommit(), and for each uploaded name in doBatchUpload's okcb. Or key the cache on name+size+mtime, which /files already returns per entry.

chunks.coverage_notes:
I found no confirmed bugs in our own commits. The three findings above are low-confidence risks, not traced failures.

Read in full:
- The full diff `b1489d3..HEAD`, which covers 5 files (tftspi.c, tftspi.h, tft.c, spi_master_lobo.c, spi_master_lobo.h).
- tftspi.c from line 110 to the end, plus the diff hunks for lines 1-110.
- The tft.c glyph functions `printProportionalChar` and `printChar`, and the surrounding rotated-char code.
- The `spi_lobo_device_select` region of spi_master_lobo.c.
- The callers in ui.c (device config, `ui_ev_loop` lock, `ui_tft_set_clock_hz`) and rest-api.c (`/screenshot` shadow path and `tftread_pattern`).

What I checked and found correct:
- **`shadow_win` bounds:** The row-wise memcpy stays inside the window and stops at `len`. The `rowfill` chunking never reads past the filled part (`ww` at most 320, or 480 on other panels).
- **`trans_cline` reuse:** The `trans_cline_filled` and colour bookkeeping is correct, including a smaller fill after a larger one and after buffer growth. The buffer is only refilled after `disp_select` has waited for DMA to finish.
- **Glyph buffer reuse:** Each glyph blit is `send_data` then `disp_deselect`, which waits for the DMA transfer, so reusing the buffer is safe.
- **`NO_DUMMY`:** The flag bit does not collide with other flags. It is only honoured on the GPIO-matrix path at 40 MHz or more.
- **Lazy `tft_shadow_init`:** Publishing the pointer from httpd while the UI draws is benign (NULL to non-NULL only).

Not examined: the rest of tft.c (about 2,900 lines, mostly untouched upstream drawing code) and the touch and STMPE610 code, which is untouched upstream.

Dropped upstream issues, out of scope because we did not touch them:
- `printChar` can write past the end of the glyph buffer when `x_size` is not a multiple of 8 and padding bits are set.
- `read_data` returns after switching the clock without restoring it when `disp_select` fails.
- `send_data` can write to the display but not the shadow when `len` is larger than the window (the display wraps, the shadow stops).

results.title: Persistent glyph scratch buffer held in internal DMA RAM, never freed
results.reasoning: Deliberate and documented at tft.c:1545-1548 (replaces a DMA malloc/free per character; 'grows to the largest glyph in use and stays'). The largest font the firmware selects is DEJAVU24 (no 64x100 font is used outside the library demo), so the buffer tops out at roughly 30x30 px x 3 = under 3 KB, not 19 KB. Allocation failure is soft: glyph_scratch returns NULL and both callers fall through to the per-pixel path (tft.c:1578, 1663), and the old buffer is kept. The finder also states no reachable trigger.

results.title: Static rowfill / trans_cline / glyph buffer shared across drawing tasks
results.claim: `rowfill` in `shadow_win()`, the persistent `trans_cline` fill buffer and `s_glyph_buf` are all static and shared. Nothing protects them except the caller holding the display bus. The old code used a per-call malloc for the fill and glyph buffers.
results.scenario: If two tasks draw at once, one can overwrite the other's fill or glyph data. `s_glyph_buf` is filled and `_bg`/`_fg` are set BEFORE `disp_select()`, so the SPI select does not protect the fill loop. Only `ui_ev_loop` and the screenshot code take `disp_lock`. Any other task that calls `TFT_print` or a fill, such as boot code drawing the logo while the UI task starts, or a machine or worker task drawing progress, can corrupt glyphs or fills. I did not trace any concrete concurrent drawer.
results.reasoning: Recorded 09-16 in chunk 7 as 'Notes, not bugs: the glyph buffer is shared across tasks, which is safe while drawing is serialised', and that still holds. Every runtime draw goes through menuProcessEvent inside ui_ev_loop under disp_lock (ui.c:130-177); the only other drawers are httpd handlers, all under disp_lock (rest-api.c:612, 722, 842, 933). Boot draws (ui.c:252-259, initMenu menu.c:938-949) run in the main task before ui_ev_loop is created at ui.c:349, and timer callbacks only post events (menu.c:666-682). The finder's point that the glyph fill precedes disp_select is correct but moot: the guard is disp_lock, not the SPI mutex, and no unlocked drawer exists.
results.prior_ref: chunk 7 (TFT library) note: glyph buffer shared across tasks

results.title: NO_DUMMY removes read dummy cycle if reads ever ran at 40 MHz or more
results.claim: With `LB_SPI_DEVICE_NO_DUMMY` set for the display, reads at an effective clock of 40 MHz or more no longer get the dummy cycle that compensates the MISO delay. Reads are only safe while `max_rdclock` stays below 40 MHz.
results.scenario: `max_rdclock` is currently measured at the 8 MHz boot clock, so it is at most 8 MHz and the code is fine today. If `find_rd_speed()` were ever run after the write clock was raised to 40 MHz or more, the sweep and `read_data` would run at 40 MHz or more with no dummy cycle. GRAM reads and the `/tftread` and `/screenshot` GRAM path would then be shifted by one bit or clock, giving wrong pixels or a false pass.
results.reasoning: Recorded 09-16 in chunk 7 'Checked': LB_SPI_DEVICE_NO_DUMMY is set only on the display, whose reads run at 10 MHz or less; CLAUDE.md documents the same design (tftspi.c drops to max_rdclock for every read). Still holds: find_rd_speed has one caller, ui.c:229, run at the 8 MHz boot clock before the write clock is raised at ui.c:244, so max_rdclock is at most 8 MHz. /tftread drops to 1 MHz before reading (rest-api.c:860, 935) and its sweep stops at 16 MHz (rest-api.c:949), below the apbclk/2 threshold in spi_master_lobo.c:768-773. The scenario is hypothetical, as the finder says.

chunks.coverage_notes: Read in full: components/machine_sampler3/sampler3.c (1353 lines), sampler3_menu.c (679), sampler3_priv.h (220). I also read the worker.h helper, machine_core.c machine_activate, recording.c (poll_load, trig_func, set_trig_func) and the sampfile_t struct. I did not read machine_sampler3.h (the include/ dir), CMakeLists.txt, the cvmtx/cvsmooth internals, sampfile.c, or the body of recording.c beyond the parts above. The finding on reverse in-place reversal (line 107) is the highest-value one. I did not confirm recording_prepare()/writer behaviour, so a failed save may never set s3.save_failed. That flag is only ever cleared in sampler3.c and never set, so the SAVE FAILED banner is dead code. That is a missing feature, not a reported bug. I dropped minor torn-write races on pending/name strings, pos rewritten by the reader after head_valid = true, and lost seek_frame/retrig_req updates. These are low-severity ordering races with no clear reachable failure beyond a glitch.

results.title: Reverse mode: in-place chunk reversal (dst == stage) folds every chunk into a palindrome
results.claim: read_playback_frames() is always called with dst == stage (here, in the waveform pass, the loop-start cache build and the ring top-up). In reverse mode it reverses stage into dst in place: `dst[(got_total + i) * 2] = stage[(got - 1 - i) * 2];`. In-place reversal without a temp is wrong, because the first half is overwritten before the second half is read.
results.scenario: Set Reverse ON for a voice, or load a sample with rev:true in the preset. Every chunk that lands in head, ring or lsc comes out with its first half equal to the reversed second half and its second half left unreversed. The reverse-mode audio is a garbled mirror-fold repeating every 4096 frames (about 93 ms), so reverse playback is wrong audio. A clean fix needs a separate destination buffer or a swap loop.
results.reasoning: All four callers (107, 126, 325, 375) pass stage as both dst and stage, and the reverse loop at 76-80 copies stage[got-1-i] to stage[i] with no temp. For i >= got/2 the source frame was already overwritten, so the result is the reversed second half followed by the unreversed second half; the first half of each file chunk is never heard. Present since the first commit 3a6298c (07-12); reachable from the Setup Reverse row (sampler3_menu.c:460) and preset rev (now via s3_set_reverse after 8.4). Head, ring, loop-start cache and thumbnail are all affected.
results.fix_sketch: In read_playback_frames reverse branch, swap frame pairs in place (i < got/2, two-ended swap of L and R) instead of the one-way copy; the dst parameter can then be dropped since every caller memcpy's out of stage anyway.

results.title: Reader's 16 KB DMA stage buffer is never NULL-checked
results.claim: The 16 KB internal DMA staging buffer is never checked for NULL. Internal RAM is the scarce pool, and the largest free block is what fails.
results.scenario: If the internal heap is fragmented or low at machine start (for example after a long web or OTA session, or with Radio or broadcast active earlier), stage is NULL. The first load_req then calls sampfile_read()/fread into NULL (via rebuild_head and read_playback_frames), or reverses into it, and the unit panics.
results.reasoning: heap_caps_malloc(16384, MALLOC_CAP_DMA) at 142 is used unchecked by rebuild_head, the lsc build and the ring top-up; sampfile_read (sampfile.c:29-35) passes it straight to fread, so a NULL stage is a store to address 0 on the first load. s3_start cannot see the failure because the alloc happens inside the task. The 09-16 bench notes already record the internal largest block dipping to 10 KB, so a failed 16 KB contiguous alloc is a realistic low-RAM case. Not recorded on 09-16 (6.10 covers rest-api mallocs only).
results.fix_sketch: Allocate stage in s3_start before worker_spawn and hand it to the reader as the task arg; on NULL take the existing free-all path and return ESP_ERR_NO_MEM so machine_activate's Stub fallback applies. Free it after worker_stop succeeds (leak on timeout, same rule as the PSRAM buffers).

results.title: Seek sets wpos = tgt, so never-streamed ring frames below the seek point pass s3_frame_ok
results.claim: A retrig/seek sets wpos = tgt. Because wpos means "ring frames [head_frames..wpos) are valid", every ring frame between head_frames (or the last-valid point) and tgt is now declared valid even though it was never streamed. Those slots hold stale data: the previous sample's frames, or frames from the old stream position. The consumer's s3_frame_ok() only checks f < wpos and wpos - f <= RING - CHUNK.
results.scenario: (a) A sample of 5 s or less is triggered with crop start beyond 1 s before the initial ring fill has finished. The seek jumps the stream ahead and skips frames. Once wpos reaches play_len, `resident` becomes true, so loop wraps and reverse play into the skipped region play stale ring contents (old sample or old position) as if they were audio. (b) A speed CV below zero on a streamed sample after a heal or seek reads stale frames behind the seek point, because ring frames below tgt pass frame_ok(). The ring is not cleared on load.
results.reasoning: After a retrig the reader sets stream_p = wpos = tgt (347-348) and s3_frame_ok (552-560) has no lower bound except head_frames and the RING-CHUNK margin (skipped entirely when resident). Traced: long sample, 1 s loop at start 10 s, gate seeks to tgt = cs-3072; turning Crop Start (K5 by default) back 1.5 s makes the wrap at 946-960 accept f_cs because wpos - f_cs <= RING-CHUNK, and s3_fetch reads ring slots that still hold the initial fill or the previous sample. The loop then plays wrong audio on every pass (only the 0.5 s loop-start cache part is right) and no starve/heal fires because the frames count as valid. Same hole for a <=5 s sample seeked forward during its initial fill: once wpos reaches play_len, resident makes the skipped span permanently valid.
results.fix_sketch: Add a reader-published ring low bound (set to head_frames in rebuild_head, to tgt in the retrig branch, written before wpos) and have s3_frame_ok reject ring frames below it; resident must also require that bound == head_frames. The existing wrap/snap seek protocol then refills instead of reading stale slots.

results.title: s3_stop leaves the recording service armed / a take running across a machine switch
results.claim: Neither stop() nor start() resets the recording service's global trig_func[] (or stops an active take). It is process-global in recording.c and only Sampler3 code disarms it. s3_start() memsets s3, so arm_target goes to -1, but recording_get_trig_func(vid) still reads RECORD.
results.scenario: Arm V1 (gate hold, or Record page), then switch machine away and back to Sampler (or arm and let the reader stop). On return the UI shows nothing armed (arm_target = -1), but process() sees armed: `pass_input` is true, the line-in is monitored to the output, and with arm_mutes the voice is muted. The next gate press on that voice starts a take instead of playing, with no banner shown. If a take was active at switch time, recording continues into the next machine.
results.reasoning: trig_func[] is a static in recording.c:37 and only Sampler3 resets it; s3_stop (519-528) neither disarms, cancels the parked writer nor stops an active take, while s3_start's memset puts arm_target back to -1. On return the banner and Record rows show nothing armed, the Live encoder-turn disarm (menu:400) no longer fires, but process() (723-743) still monitors the input, mutes the voice and a gate press records. An active take keeps recording line-in in every other machine (audio.c:643) until the card fills, and the parked writer blocks /bounce (audio.c:168). Arm on the Record page then switch machine (panel or web remote) reaches it; tape_stop (tape.c:1032-1033) shows the intended cleanup.
results.fix_sketch: In s3_stop, before worker_stop: recording_finish() if a take is active, recording_set_trig_func(0/1, TRIG_FUNC_VOICE), recording_cancel_prepared() - the same pair tape_stop already uses. Optionally have s3_start re-sync arm_target from recording_get_trig_func.

results.title: s_discard_next (and the arm/abort request flags) outlive the session and can eat the next good take
results.claim: The file-static request flags s_arm_req, s_rec_abort_req and s_discard_next live outside s3 and are never reset in s3_start()/s3_stop().
results.scenario: Abort a take with a gate hold (s_discard_next = true) and switch machines before the reader consumes the pickup. Alternatively the abort's finished take never signals rec_load_pending. The flag stays true, and after returning to Sampler the next genuine recording is silently discarded as an "aborted take" ("discarded aborted take REC_xxxx") and never loaded. A stale s_arm_req likewise arms a voice at start.
results.reasoning: s_discard_next is set on abort (164) and cleared only when a pickup arrives (185-186); neither s3_start nor s3_stop resets the three file-static flags. If the aborted take never signals a pickup - writer write/close error (recording.c:203-207), or Tape's tape_card_service (tape.c:934) consuming the flag after a quick switch - the flag stays true and the next genuine take is logged as 'discarded aborted take', not loaded and its tempo stamp dropped. The take file itself stays in usr/REC, so this is wrong behaviour, not data loss. The trigger is narrow (a write error on the aborted take's final flush, or a switch to Tape inside the writer's finalize window).
results.fix_sketch: Clear s_arm_req, s_rec_abort_req and s_discard_next in s3_start right after worker_idle/memset, and clear s_discard_next in the arm branch of s3_toggle_arm so a fresh arm can never inherit an old discard.

results.title: Loop-start cache build that reads 0 frames retries every loop with no delay (busy-spin)
results.claim: When the loop-start cache read returns 0 frames, the build sets lsc_valid = false with lsc_start = lw and reports worked = true. The next reader iteration sees !lsc_valid and retries the same read immediately. There is no delay: worked = true skips the vTaskDelay(1), and the failed path exits before the courtesy delay.
results.scenario: The file is truncated relative to its header frame count (power-cut take, or a card glitch) or the card is removed, and lsc_want lies past the real data. The reader (priority 6, unpinned) spins forever hammering sd_lock and fseek/fread. It starves lower-priority tasks (httpd, WiFi, UI), and it also starves the other voice's fill except for its share of the loop.
results.reasoning: When the first read returns 0 the block leaves lsc_valid false, sets lsc_start = lw and still sets worked = true (332-335), so the vTaskDelay(1) at 396 is skipped and the same fseek/read is retried immediately, forever, at priority 6. The ring top-up next to it only sets worked when got > 0, so this is the one path that breaks the 'sleep at least one tick' rule. The truncated-file trigger in the scenario is wrong: sampfile probe clamps frames to the real file size (sampfile_int.h:66-68, 123-124, 155), so it needs a card read error or removal while a long loop with start past the head is loaded. Task WDT does not watch idle tasks here, so no reboot: httpd (prio 5) and lower tasks are starved on that core until the machine is switched.
results.fix_sketch: Set worked only when got > 0 in the lsc build (as the ring path at 376-385 does), so a failed build falls through to the loop's vTaskDelay(1).

results.title: Waveform thumbnail: a -32768 sample gives peak 32768, (uint8_t)(32768>>7) wraps to 0
results.claim: peak can be 32768, because abs(-32768) is computed as an int. 32768 >> 7 = 256, and the uint8_t cast wraps it to 0.
results.scenario: A hard-clipped recording or file containing sample value -32768 in a 144-column waveform bucket makes that column the quietest on the thumbnail. It renders as the minimum-height stub instead of full height, so the loudest peaks show as gaps in the waveform on the panel.
results.reasoning: s is an int, so -(-32768) = 32768, 32768 >> 7 = 256 and the uint8_t cast stores 0. The draw code (sampler3_menu.c:154-157) then renders that column at the 2 px minimum. Any column whose 128 peeked frames contain one full-scale negative sample (a clipped take, or clipped imported material) shows as a gap instead of full height. Display only; nothing reads wf[] for audio.
results.fix_sketch: Clamp before the shift: if (peak > 32767) peak = 32767; then wf[c] = peak >> 7.

results.title: s3_reader 4096-byte stack overflow on the tempo-stamp / JSON path
results.reasoning: The heavy items the finder lists are on the heap, not the stack: FatFS LFN buffer (sdkconfig:625 CONFIG_FATFS_LFN_HEAP), the JSON file buffer (fileio.c:245), cJSON nodes and print buffer. Frame sizes read from the existing build ELF (entry a1,N) sum to about 1.6-1.8 KB on the deepest chains: reader_task <=368 + esp_log_write/writev/vprintf 176 + _vfprintf_r 784 + _dtoa_r 160, or cJSON_Print + sprintf 192 + _svfprintf_r 784 + _dtoa_r 160, or resolve_aux 128 + resolve 96 + f_stat 112 + sdmmc ~300; even with the unbuffered __sbprintf detour it is about 2.7 KB. rec_writer (recording.c:261) runs the same cJSON_Print/writeJSONFile/log chain from a 560-byte frame in the same 4096 stack on every take, with the canary check on. A high-water log would be cheap hardening but no overflow is shown.

chunks.coverage_notes:
I read all six files in scope in full: slicer.c, slicer_menu.c, slicer_ot.c, slicer_web.c, slicer_priv.h. machine_slicer.h is not in components/machine_slicer/ (only an `include` directory is there), so I did not read it. I also read the parts of worker.h, sampfile.h and sampfile.c (resolve paths and the path-buffer sizes), reverb.c (init/free/set_mode), svf.c and setup_menu.c (value buffer sizes) that the traced paths needed.

I checked these and found no bug: path and header buffer sizes against SAMPLE_ID_LEN 32 (worst case about 57 bytes into 64/80-byte buffers); the OT slice-count and index bounds; the slice_pt, head_len and heads-slab indexing; the ring wrap and lead maths; the generation handshake (stale-generation reads are ignored by the voice); and the display snprintf buffers.

I dropped these because they are minor or not reachable in a harmful way:
- Small windows where the UI or httpd task reads slice_pt or n_slices while the reader rewrites them. These give display glitches only.
- A reverse toggle takes about one tick to mute, so the tail can be read in the wrong direction for a few milliseconds.
- Two rapid reverse toggles during a head build could leave the heads in the wrong direction.
- After a failed load, sl.sample keeps the old name, and resl_req and loading can stay stale until the next load.
- A voice waiting on a tail that never arrives (SD read error) stays silent until the next fire.
- A sidecar bpm that is huge or NaN overflows the float-to-uint32 conversion in slicer_build_ot.

I did not build or run anything, and I did not touch the device or the plans/ folder.

results.title: Slicer reverse heads are flipped in place (dst == stage) and come out as palindromes
results.claim: read_slice_frames() is called with dst and stage as the same buffer. In reverse mode its flip loop (`dst[(got_total+i)*2] = stage[(got-1-i)*2]`) then reverses IN PLACE, which destroys the data. The same call is made for the tail ring at line 295-296.
results.scenario: Set Reverse ON (or load a preset with reverse:true). For each slice the loop overwrites stage[i] for i < got/2 before it is read back as stage[got-1-i'] for the mirrored index. The first half of every head and tail chunk comes out reversed and the second half comes out FORWARD. Every reverse trigger plays a splice of reversed and forward audio at 1.5 chunk boundaries, and the tail has the same fault each 4096-frame chunk. Forward mode is unaffected, because memcpy with dst==src at got_total==0 is a no-op in practice.
results.reasoning: build_heads passes stage as both dst and stage (slicer.c:201-202); hl <= SL_HEAD_FRAMES 3528 < SL_CHUNK 4096, so got_total is 0 and the flip loop at slicer.c:130-133 reads and writes the same buffer. For i < got/2 it writes orig[got-1-i]; for i >= got/2 it reads back what it already overwrote, so the second half stays forward: each reverse head is the last ~40 ms reversed followed by the same 40 ms forward, and the first half of the chunk is lost. Forward mode is fine (memcpy onto itself at offset 0). Not in the 09-16 review; the same pattern sits in sampler3.c:76-80 with callers at 107/126/326/375, in the code since 419344b.
results.fix_sketch: In read_slice_frames, reverse the just-read chunk in stage with a two-ended swap over got/2 frames, then memcpy to dst only when dst != stage. One change there fixes both call sites; apply the same change to sampler3's read_playback_frames.

results.title: Slicer reverse tail chunks are flipped in place (same root cause as #0)
results.claim: The tail-stream read passes stage as both destination and staging buffer, so reverse mode flips each chunk in place and corrupts it (see the finding at line 202). The reader then copies the corrupted chunk into the ring.
results.scenario: With sl.reverse set, every tail chunk of up to 4096 frames is half-reversed and half-forward before the memcpy into sl.ring. This is audible as garbage in the body of every reversed slice longer than the 80 ms head.
results.reasoning: Same defect as #0 at the tail call site: slicer.c:295-296 passes stage, stage with want <= SL_CHUNK, so the flip at slicer.c:130-133 aliases and every 1024/4096-frame chunk copied into sl.ring (302-304) is reversed-upper-half followed by forward-upper-half. With Reverse ON (menu row 5, slicer_menu.c:355, or preset 'reverse') the body of every slice longer than the head is garbled. Not a separate bug; it is fixed by the #0 fix.
results.fix_sketch: Covered by the #0 fix in read_slice_frames (in-place swap reversal in stage, memcpy only when dst != stage); no change needed at this call site.

results.title: Slicer reader's 16 KB DMA staging buffer is not NULL-checked
results.claim: The 16 KB internal DMA staging buffer is never checked for NULL. The reader passes it straight to sampfile_read()/memcpy on the first load request. The reader is spawned after several PSRAM slabs and the reverb are allocated, and CLAUDE.md says internal RAM is the scarce pool.
results.scenario: If the largest free internal DMA block is under 16 KB when the Slicer starts (Radio, web or broadcast active, or a fragmented heap), stage is NULL. The first slicer_load makes scan_file() call sampfile_read(f, sf, NULL, ...), which writes to a NULL pointer and panics the module. The free at exit is harmless, but the load crashes.
results.reasoning: heap_caps_malloc(16384, MALLOC_CAP_DMA) at slicer.c:219 is used unchecked; slicer_start auto-loads the first sample (slicer.c:423), so scan_file calls sampfile_read(f, sf, NULL, 4096) at slicer.c:164, which is fread into address 0 (sampfile.c:32) and panics. The 09-16 triage itself records the largest internal block dipping to 10 KB, so a failing 16 KB internal alloc is a realistic low-RAM state. Deck (deck.c:124) and Sampler3 (sampler3.c:142) have the same unchecked pattern; none of these is recorded in the 09-16 review (6.10 was rest-api only).
results.fix_sketch: Allocate stage in slicer_start beside the PSRAM slabs and fail with ESP_ERR_NO_MEM (the Stub fallback from 1.1/1.2 then takes over); pass it as the worker_spawn arg and free it in slicer_stop only after worker_stop succeeds. Same treatment fits deck.c:124 and sampler3.c:142.

results.title: sl_reader 4096-byte stack may overflow in the .OT probe
results.reasoning: Frame sizes read from the existing build/ctag-straempler.elf: reader_task 240, slicer_parse_ot 992, pick_transients 2112 (a leaf called from the reader, never stacked with parse_ot, slicer.c:58/78), _vfprintf_r 784, sample_resolve_aux 128 + sample_resolve 96, f_stat/f_open 112, sdmmc_read_sectors_dma 112. The deepest chains sum to about 2.3-2.6 KB (parse_ot + ESP_LOGI, parse_ot + stat walk, pick_transients), roughly 3.0 KB with task-top and interrupt-frame overhead, against 4096; FatFS LFN buffers are on the heap (CONFIG_FATFS_LFN_HEAP=y). The parse_ot + stat/fopen chain also runs on every Slicer start (slicer.c:423 -> 243) without a canary panic. Margin is about 1 KB by arithmetic and not measured on the unit, but no overflow path exists.

results.title: GET /slicer/ot exports without checking sl.loading: stale or torn slice table
results.claim: The httpd handler reads sl.n_slices, sl.slice_pt[] and sl.sample (through slicer_build_ot and sidecar_bpm) without checking sl.loading. The reader rewrites these concurrently during a load or reslice.
results.scenario: A GET /slicer/ot request lands while the reader is inside recompute_slices() or pick_transients() (for example while the user turns the Sensitivity dial, which reslices on every detent). The handler exports a torn slice table: mixed old and new slice_pt entries, or a sample name that was only partly copied. The downloaded .OT file has non-monotonic or wrong slice points and a valid checksum, so it silently misleads the Octatrack.
results.reasoning: The handler (slicer_web.c:29-42) and slicer_build_ot (slicer_ot.c:114-143) never test sl.loading. On a load the reader sets sl.len and sl.sample first (slicer.c:240-241), then scans for seconds to ~1.5 min before recompute_slices (slicer.c:246), so a download in that window returns the PREVIOUS sample's slice points (or 16 zero-length slices on first load) under the new name and trimEnd, with a valid checksum; the web link is shown whenever the machine is Slicer (index.html:3742). The finder's reslice tear is the same missing gate with a microsecond window; additionally the loop at slicer_ot.c:137 re-reads volatile n_slices, so a reslice from <=64 to 128 mid-loop would write past the 832-byte httpd stack buffer (very narrow race). Consequence is a wrong export file, not data loss.
results.fix_sketch: In slicer_ot_get_handler return 409/503 while sl.loading or !sl.heads_valid, and in slicer_build_ot snapshot n_slices into a local once (bound-checked against SL_OT_SLICES) and loop on the local. Re-check sl.loading after the build and fail the request if it went true.

chunks.coverage_notes: Files read in full: components/machine_instsampler/instsampler.c (852 lines), isampler_menu.c (1232), instsampler_priv.h (231), include/machine_instsampler.h. I also read the paths they call into: util/lfo.c (div and shape indices are clamped, so not a bug), machine_core.c (the machine_block_wait and machine_activate order is sound), sample_ram.c sample_load, sampfile.c sample_resolve, preset_store.c (save takes ownership of the cJSON; patch id buffers are adequate), the cvmtx_abs, cvmtx_val and cvmtx_cv01 excerpts of cvmtx.c, and the pitch_detect_buf head (it mallocs its scratch; not stack). Traced with no finding: SAMPLE_ID_LEN string buffers (tag[32] and the snprintf calls truncate safely, strlcpy into the 32-byte zone sample), the arena bump allocator accounting on append, in-place reload and failure paths, cubic_read bounds, the loop and xfade math (aside from the LoopMov finding), and gate and zone latching.
