Findings dropped as too speculative or too minor: the nanosecond-wide race in which keys_clear_zones zeroes frames between process()'s `pos < frames` guard and cubic_read's reload of it (buf is still valid, so at worst one stray read); a reload that only glitches audio while sample_load overwrites the last zone's buffer in place; KR_LOOPEND on a zone shorter than loop_start+64 frames leaving loop_end > frames, which process() clamps; a saved patch overwriting PAT_999 after the 1000th save (preset_store.c, out of scope); and concurrent preset_load from httpd racing the UI task's loads (a cross-cutting pattern, not Keys-specific).

results.title: keys_snap_zero always snaps against zone[0], not the zone being edited
results.claim: keys_snap_zero always snaps against zone[0]'s buffer and length, but its callers (Live loop-edge drag and the Setup Loop Start/End rows) pass frames that belong to the edit or sounding zone, which may be any zone.
results.scenario: Multisample with zone 0 = 20000 frames and zone 2 = 500000 frames. Edit zone 2's Loop End in Setup or by dragging on Live. keys_snap_zero clamps the requested frame to zone 0's length minus 1 and returns a crossing from zone 0's audio. Zone 2's loop_end is then pinned at or below 20000, or bumped to loop_start+64, so the loop cannot be set past zone 0's length. The snap also lands on zero crossings of the wrong audio, which defeats the declick. The call sites are isampler_menu.c lines 669, 677, 956 and 963. Fix by passing the zone index to keys_snap_zero.
results.reasoning: keys_snap_zero hardcodes &inst.zone[0] (instsampler.c:366-368) and clamps frame to zone 0's length, but all four callers pass frames of kl_z() (isampler_menu.c:669, 677: sounding or edit zone) or ks_z() (956, 963: edit zone). For a zone longer than zone 0, any Loop Start/End edit past zone 0's length is pulled back to about zone0.frames-1; the callers' post-clamps only guard against frames and loop_start, so the wrong value is stored. For frames inside zone 0's length the snap lands on zone 0's zero crossings, up to 512 frames away from the intended spot and not a crossing in the edited audio. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Change the signature to keys_snap_zero(const is_zone_t *z, uint32_t frame) (instsampler_priv.h:225) and pass kl_z() at isampler_menu.c:669/677 and ks_z() at 956/963. No other change needed; the body already works on z.

results.title: LoopMov can push the loop window past the sample end; voice goes silent and stays stuck
results.claim: The LoopMov matrix offset can push the loop window's start to or past the end of the sample. The fix-up then sets le = ls + 64, which is greater than frames. The voice cursor is never wrapped and stops advancing once it reaches frames.
results.scenario: Sample with loop_start > 0 and LoopMov patched with a full-scale CV (ABS bipolar knob, or an amount of +1). mov = m_lmov * frames >= frames - loop_start, so ls >= frames and le is forced to ls + 64, past frames. The cursor advances until pos >= frames, where wrap never triggers because le > frames. The sample read is guarded by `v->pos < (double)z->frames`, so nothing advances pos any more. The voice stays active with the envelope held and is silent until the next note-on. It does not recover when the CV returns, because pos is stuck at or beyond frames.
results.reasoning: m_lmov reaches +1.0 (cvmtx_val = amt*cv01, or the ABS bipolar knob (kk-0.5)*2, instsampler.c:483-484), so mov = m_lmov*frames gives ls >= frames whenever m_lmov >= 1 - loop_start/frames; line 523 clamps le to frames, then line 524 sets le = ls+64 > frames. The wrap at 606 needs pos >= le, which cannot happen because the read and the pos advance are both inside the pos < frames guard at 577, so pos parks at >= frames with the voice active and sig = 0. When the CV drops back, le is valid again but pos never advances, so the note stays silent until the next gate. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: In the loop-window block (514-525) clamp ls to [0, frames-64] (floor 0) before computing le = ls + len, then clamp le to frames, so le never exceeds frames. Optionally also wrap a cursor found at pos >= frames back to ls in LOOP_FWD so an already-parked voice recovers.

results.title: Zones preset load leaves peaks of the last zone while edit_zone is reset to 0
results.claim: After a zones-array preset load, edit_zone is reset to 0 but inst.peaks still holds the waveform of the last zone appended, because keys_load_zone_at rebuilt peaks for edit_zone = zi. No keys_build_peaks follows. The Live page's kl_sync_peaks only rebuilds when the shown zone index differs from the cached s_peaks_zone.
results.scenario: Keys is on Live showing zone 0, so s_peaks_zone is 0. The user picks a 5-zone patch (Setup > Load Patch), or a /remote/params POST carries a zones array. keys_preset_load ends with edit_zone = 0 and peaks belonging to zone 5. On return to Live, kl_zone_idx() is 0 and equals s_peaks_zone, so there is no rebuild. The strip shows zone 5's audio under zone 0's loop box. The same stale strip appears after a machine switch away and back, because the menu static s_peaks_zone survives keys_start. Call keys_build_peaks() after edit_zone = 0.
results.reasoning: Each keys_load_zone_at sets edit_zone = zi and calls keys_build_peaks() (153, 187), so after the loop inst.peaks holds the last zone; line 774 then sets edit_zone = 0 with no rebuild, and keys_patch_handler (isampler_menu.c:1187) does not rebuild either. kl_sync_peaks (isampler_menu.c:61-65) only rebuilds when kl_zone_idx() differs from the static s_peaks_zone, which is never reset, so if Live last showed zone 0 the strip keeps the last zone's waveform under zone 0's loop box until a note in another zone changes the shown zone. The web Apply posts the whole preset including the zones array (index.html rpApply), so every Apply on a multisample hits this too. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Call keys_build_peaks() right after inst.edit_zone = 0 at instsampler.c:774 (it builds for edit_zone, which matches the s_peaks_zone == 0 case). That also makes the first Live paint after boot or a machine switch correct.

results.title: sample_resolve stat walk runs without sd_lock in sample_load
results.claim: sample_resolve performs up to SF_N_DIRS x SF_N_EXTS stat() calls on the SD card without holding sd_lock. sample_load takes the lock only around fopen, probe and read, not around the resolve. This breaks the rule that every SD I/O burst must hold sd_lock.
results.scenario: Keys (and every other sample_load caller) loads a sample from the UI or httpd task while a streaming machine's reader is doing raw-FatFS reads, or the recorder is writing. The stat walk runs with no lock, up to about 28 stats when the file sits in a late folder or is missing. It races the raw audio read path, which bypasses the VFS lock. The documented consequence is card wedge or corruption and audio dropouts. Wrap the resolve in sd_lock_take/give; the mutex is recursive.
results.reasoning: True as written: sample_resolve (sampfile.c:85-96) does up to 7 dirs x N exts stat() calls with no sd_lock, and sample_load only locks fopen/probe/read; the same unlocked call is in every other caller (deck.c:135, sampler3.c:248, slicer.c:231, dualdeck.c:112, sampplay.c:152, tape.c:610, rest-api.c:529-531, 2590), only rest-api.c:448 wraps it. It breaks the CLAUDE.md sd_lock rule and is the same class as 09-16 finding 6.12 (Watch, low), which listed only the rest-api sites. The corruption claim is not established: IDF 4.3 ffconf.h has FF_FS_REENTRANT 1, so each FatFS call is serialised by the volume mutex, and the current streaming readers use VFS fopen/fread, not raw FatFS. What is missing is any evidence that a bare stat interleaving between another task's locked calls does harm; consequence corrected from corruption to none shown.
results.fix_sketch: Fix it once inside sample_resolve (sampfile.c:91): sd_lock_take()/sd_lock_give() around each stat, not around the whole walk, so a streaming reader is not held off for up to 28 stats. The mutex is recursive, so the existing wrap at rest-api.c:448 keeps working and every caller is covered.

results.title: Legacy flat 'root' is cast to uint8_t unclamped; zones 'fn' is not clamped
results.claim: The legacy flat-key root is cast to uint8_t without clamping, unlike the zones path (clampi 0..127) and the UI (12..108). The zones-path "fn" value is also not clamped to -1..1, although the flat path clamps it.
results.scenario: POST /remote/params {"root":300} or a hand-edited patch gives root = 44, and {"root":-1} gives 255. The zone plays at the wrong pitch, and the inc clamp of 0.25..4 hides the error. Zone selection by nearest root is skewed, since keys_zone_for_note compares against the wrapped value. A zones entry with "fn":5.0 detunes that zone by five semitones, which the Setup Fine row cannot express.
results.reasoning: Line 785 stores (uint8_t)j->valueint with no clamp (300 -> 44, -1 -> 255) while the zones path clamps 0..127 (760); line 762 stores zones 'fn' unclamped while the flat path clamps to +/-1 (786). Nothing downstream is unsafe: inc is clamped 0.25..4 (560) and note_name_midi caps at 127, so the effect is only a wrong root or an over-wide fine tune from invalid input. The flat path runs only when the node has no zones array; the web Apply always sends zones (index.html rpApply), so root needs a hand-edited legacy patch or a crafted POST, while fn out of range can be typed in the web raw table. Same class as 09-16 finding 12.6 (Glitch, Watch) but not recorded for Keys.
results.fix_sketch: Use the existing helpers: clampi(j->valueint, 0, 127) at line 785 and clampf((float)q->valuedouble, -1.0f, 1.0f) at line 762, matching the other path in each case.

results.title: Keys preset load stores sus, cut and the other voice params without range clamps
results.claim: Envelope, cutoff, level, glide and LFO values from preset or REST are stored without range clamps. The UI clamps each of them (for example sus 0..1). process() trusts sus, cutoff_base, res01, env_to_cut and lfo_depth as given.
results.scenario: POST /remote/params {"sus":50}: dec_inc is negative, so ENV_DEC first holds env at 1 and then jumps it to 50. The amplitude is multiplied by 50 (clipped hard at 32000) and the filter cutoff offset env*e2c*5000 goes far out of range. {"sus":-1} gives a negative envelope, which inverts polarity. The same applies to a negative "cut", which makes logf NaN in the Live dial (NaN reaches sinf and an int cast, so pointer and focus-ring geometry is garbage).
results.reasoning: Lines 707-721 store atk/dec/sus/rel/e2c/cut/res/gld/lvl/lfo values as given. process() clamps cutoff, res, e2c and level (498-501) and floors the times (539-541), but sus is used raw: with sus = 50 dec_inc is negative (543) and ENV_DEC jumps env straight to 50 (570), so sig = lp*50 hits the hard clip at 620; a negative sus inverts polarity. A negative cut makes logf NaN in draw_dial (isampler_menu.c:431), and clampf passes NaN through (priv.h:185), so the dial pointer is drawn from NaN; lfo_div and lfo_shape are safe, lfo.c clamps both. Reachable from the web: the raw preset table renders every number as a free type=number input with no min/max (index.html:2410), so typing 80 for sus (the panel shows it as 80%) is enough.
results.fix_sketch: Clamp on load with the existing clampf/clampi and the same ranges ks_adj uses (isampler_menu.c:969-993): sus, e2c, res, lfd, lvl to 0..1, cut to 30..12000, atk/dec/rel/gld to their Setup ranges, lfx/lfv/lfw to their enum ranges. One clamp per line in keys_preset_load; no change in process().

chunks.coverage_notes:
Files read in full: components/machine_drumsampler/drum.c, drum_menu.c, drum_priv.h, include/machine_drumsampler.h. I also read the audio_task loop in components/audio/audio.c, machine_activate in components/machine/machine_core.c, sample_load in components/util/sample_ram.c, beatlisten_out_render, and the MI_ADD macro in machine.h. Everything in scope was read. I did not read the internals of cvmtx, fxrack, reverb or svf, so any claim that depends on them (for example that cvmtx_abs returns 0..1, or that reverb_send_i32 is safe) was taken on trust.

Checked and found safe, so not reported:
- Display and name buffers (nm[10] with %.8s, tag[20], val[32] and raw[24], t[32]) all fit or truncate through snprintf.
- The lazy-buffer free in drum_clear_layer is guarded by len=0 plus a one-tick delay.
- The layer flip in the mixer re-runs voice_setup, so a shorter B buffer is not overrun.
- Loop and interpolation indices stay inside len because st+ll <= len.
- Pitch LUT index is clamped to 0..24.
- All preset values used as indices are masked or clamped: sel_src, trig_src, pitch_src, sens, reps, lvl, rvs, dec, pit.
- The soft-clip and mixing arithmetic does not overflow int32.

Dropped or unconfirmed: preset_load never clears a layer when 's' is empty or absent (state not reset on reload, low value). A machine_activate stop racing an httpd-driven drum_load_layer was judged too exotic to report.

results.title: drum_process early-out leaves out[] stale; audio task re-sends the last block
results.claim: drum_process returns without writing `out` when no pad is playing and the filter, reverb and FX rack are all idle. The audio task's `out[]` is a persistent stack array that is never cleared between blocks. Glitch, granular, radio and slicer all memset(out) on their early-out paths. Drums does not.
results.scenario: Default state: filter off, reverb off, FX slots off. A pad plays and ends. Every later block returns early, so audio_task re-sends the last block written, which holds the sample's tail, forever. It is audible as a ~1.4 kHz buzz of the tail at low level, or full-level garbage if Drums is the first machine active after boot (`out` is uninitialised stack). With any tail-producing stage live (filter, reverb or FX) the path is not taken, so the bug shows only in the plain dry configuration. Fix: memset(out, 0, MACHINE_BLOCK*sizeof(int32_t)) before returning.
results.reasoning: drum_process never writes out before the return at 553, and audio_task (audio.c:601, 676, 740) keeps one persistent out[] that is only zeroed when no machine is active, so the last written 32-frame block repeats at ~1378 Hz until a pad sounds again. After a natural sample end the stale block is only the rem<256 tail ramp (at most 12% of the last 31 frames, silent for clean one-shots, audible for samples cut at the 2 s cap). It is full level when drum_load_layer/drum_clear_layer clear p->playing under a sounding pad (660, 698), or when an FX slot or the filter is switched off while its tail rings with no pad playing. The boot-garbage part is wrong: initAudio runs before machine_activate (ui.c:344, main.c:16), so NULL-machine blocks zero out first. Not in the 09-16 review (Drums: nothing to report).
results.fix_sketch: memset(out, 0, MACHINE_BLOCK * sizeof(int32_t)) before the return at drum.c:553, the same early-out pattern as glitch.c:86, granular.c:148 and slicer.c:460.

results.title: POST-filter reverb send uses a per-sample send/dry ratio that blows up
results.claim: The POST-filter reverb send is rebuilt per sample as send * filtered_out / dry_in. The SVF is not a memoryless gain: its output is phase-shifted and resonant, so this ratio is meaningless per sample. It goes to +/-infinity as the dry sample approaches zero, and it flips sign wherever the filtered and dry signals have opposite polarity.
results.scenario: Send Tap = post-filter, filter engaged (LP or HP), reverb on, a pad with rv_send > 0 playing. At every dry zero-crossing, dl is about +/-1 while lo32 is thousands. sndL*lo32/dl is enormous and clamps to +/-32767 in the send buffer, so the reverb receives full-scale spikes and polarity flips, heard as harsh noise or distortion in the tail. The same thing happens on the right channel at line 609.
results.reasoning: snd*lo32/dl equals the filtered send only when snd/dl is constant, i.e. one dry-routed pad; that single-pad case is bounded (ratio <= 1), so the finder's single-pad blow-up is overstated. With two overlapping pads at different rv_send the ratio is (w1*x1+w2*x2)/(x1+x2), unbounded wherever the sum crosses zero; the same happens with one pad on the FX bus (fx_on defaults true) once a slot is live, because accL then holds FX output while sndL holds the raw pad. The int64 result clamps to +/-32767 at 620-621, so the tank gets full-scale spikes and sign flips; dl==0 also drops the send to 0 for that sample. Needs non-default Send Tap = post-filter (drum_menu.c:969) with the filter engaged and reverb on; after that every overlapping hit triggers it.
results.fix_sketch: Drop the ratio and filter the send bus itself: add a second svf_t pair to dr_state_t and run svf_step on sndL/sndR with the same dr.flt_f/dr.flt_q and mode tap when rv_post && flt_live && flt_mode, svf_park otherwise. Reset the pair alongside flt_l/flt_r (drum_start and the NaN guard).

results.title: Retrigger/choke queued near the sample end is dropped
results.claim: This check runs before the retrig/choke fade handling. If a retrigger or choke was queued (p->retrig set) and the cursor reaches the end of the sample during the ~32-frame fade, the voice stops with retrig still true and the queued hit is never started.
results.scenario: A pad is hit again, or the other layer is hit, within roughly the last 32 frames (about 0.7 ms) of the playing sample, or 128 frames for a choke (fade step 2). The pad goes silent and the new trigger is lost, although p->hit was set so the UI flashed. This is most likely with very short samples and fast rolls. The window is narrow.
results.reasoning: trigger_pad on a playing pad only sets retrig/fade (61-68); the new hit starts only when fade reaches 0 at 452. If pos reaches len first, line 473 sets playing=false and breaks with retrig still set, so next_layer never starts, though p->hit already flashed the UI. The window is the last 32 frames for a same-layer retrig and the last 128 for a cross-layer choke (DR_RETRIG_STEP 8, DR_CHOKE_STEP 2), doubled at +12 pitch. The decay and loop-rep ends sit in the non-retrig branch and are not affected.
results.fix_sketch: At line 473, when p->retrig is set, do not stop the voice: set p->fade = 0 and continue, so the next frame's fade check at 451-452 lands the queued layer through the existing voice_setup path.

results.title: Preset pan is cast to uint8, not clamped
results.claim: Preset pan is masked into uint8 instead of clamped, unlike the neighbouring lvl/rvs/dec fields. The house rule 'clamp, don't mask' is not followed here.
results.scenario: A preset, or a POST /remote/params body, with pan 300 or -1 wraps to 44 or 255. The pad jumps to the wrong side of the stereo field instead of pinning at the extreme.
results.reasoning: The line is a bare (uint8_t) cast, so pan 300 becomes 44 and -1 becomes 255, while lvl/rvs/dec right beside it clamp. The effect is only a wrong stereo position; pan is used as a 0..255 multiplier (535-536), so nothing reads out of range. No shipped path produces such a value: the web slider is min 0 max 255 (index.html:2201) and the panel row clamps (drum_menu.c:745-748), so it needs a hand-made POST /remote/params or a hand-edited AUTOSAVE/preset. Same class as 12.6 in the 09-16 Watch list, but this site was not recorded.
results.fix_sketch: Clamp like the rvs line below it: int pn = j->valueint; dr.pad[i].pan = (uint8_t)(pn < 0 ? 0 : (pn > 255 ? 255 : pn)).

results.title: Negative preset cw gives cw_mode 251..255 via signed %
results.claim: C's % keeps the sign of the dividend, so a negative preset value gives a negative remainder that is cast to uint8, e.g. -1 gives 255. cw_mode then lies outside 0..DR_CW_MODES-1.
results.scenario: A preset or remote params with cw:-1 sets cw_mode = 255. The knob7 clockwise handler matches none of the modes, so the CW half of the knob silently does nothing, and the Pads row shows 'retrig'. The next press of the row wraps it to 1 (attack).
results.reasoning: valueint % 5 is negative for a negative value and the uint8 cast turns -1 into 255. With cw_mode 255 none of the branches at 286-301 match, so knob7 CW does nothing; the Pads row falls through to 'retrig' (drum_menu.c:652-663), and the next row press wraps to 1 (drum_menu.c:762). There is no array index on cw_mode, so no memory risk. The web Drums form does not expose cw and the panel only cycles 0..4, so it needs a hand-made POST or a hand-edited file.
results.fix_sketch: Range-check instead of modulo: int cw = j->valueint; if (cw < 0 || cw >= DR_CW_MODES) cw = DR_CW_LOOP; dr.pad[i].cw_mode = (uint8_t)cw.

results.title: drum_load_layer raced by UI browser and httpd preset_load
results.reasoning: httpd never calls preset_load: remote_params_post_handler only queues EV_REMOTE_PRESET to the UI queue (rest-api.c:1888-1889), and preset_load runs on the UI task in menu.c:618-624. The browser confirm (drum_menu.c:866) and the autosave restore at bind (menu.c:913-916) are on that same UI task, and Drums has no web URI that loads a layer. All callers of drum_load_layer are serialized on one task, so the double malloc and interleaved load cannot happen.

results.title: Deck reader busy-spins without a tick when sampfile_read returns 0
results.claim: When sampfile_read returns 0 (file shorter than its probed frame count, or an SD read error), the fill branch still ends in `continue`, skipping the vTaskDelay(1) at the bottom of the loop. cur_ff and wpos do not advance, so the same read repeats forever.
results.scenario: A WAV whose header data-chunk size is larger than the bytes actually present (truncated upload), or a card read error mid-track: sfl.frames > real frames, so ff < file_frames but fread returns 0. The reader task (prio 6, unpinned) spins on sd_lock/fread with no sleep and starves lower-priority tasks on its core (httpd, analysis). dk.loading never clears, so the deck sits in BUF and never recovers until the track is reloaded.
results.reasoning: With got==0 neither wpos nor cur_ff advance and the fill branch still ends in `continue` (deck.c:224-233), skipping vTaskDelay(1) at :260, so the prio-6 unpinned reader spins on sd_lock/fread; FatFS keeps fp->err sticky so every later read fails at once. The truncated-WAV trigger is wrong: frames are clamped to the real file size at probe (sampfile_int.h:66-68, :123-124, RAW = fsize/4), so only a card read error or pulled card gets here. httpd is prio 5 pinned to core 0 (rest-api.c:2687) and can starve; the deck stays silent until a new track load or machine switch (run flag is still checked). Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: On got==0 do not `continue`: treat it as end of data (reader owns file_frames, so set dk.file_frames = ff and clear dk.loading, log once) and fall through to the existing vTaskDelay(1). That ends playback cleanly through the existing EOF path instead of spinning.

results.title: Deck reader chunk/tail DMA buffers are never NULL-checked
results.claim: The chunk and tail buffers are allocated from scarce internal DMA RAM and never NULL-checked. The first fill passes `chunk` straight to sampfile_read and memcpy; `tail` is used in the seam crossfade.
results.scenario: Internal RAM is fragmented or exhausted (16 KB for chunk plus 2 KB for tail; the notes say largest free block is what fails, for example with Radio/HTTPS/broadcast active or a Deck start after other machines). The malloc returns NULL, the first successful track open then reads into NULL and panics. `tail` NULL crashes the first loop seam.
results.reasoning: reader_task allocates 16 KB + 1 KB MALLOC_CAP_DMA and uses both unchecked: chunk goes to sampfile_read at :204 and :247, tail at :213. deck_start only checks the PSRAM ring and worker_spawn (4 KB stack), so a start where 4 KB fits but a 16 KB block does not leaves a live reader with chunk NULL and the first track load writes through NULL. The 09-16 bench notes record the internal largest block dipping to 10 KB and a Deck start landing on Stub after a 22 KB leak, so the regime is real. Not recorded as a finding on 09-16 (6.10 was rest-api only).
results.fix_sketch: Allocate chunk and tail in deck_start next to the ring, where a failure already returns ESP_ERR_NO_MEM and the core falls back to Stub; hand them to the task and free them in deck_stop only after worker_stop() succeeds (leak otherwise, per worker.h).

results.title: deck_loop_remap schedules at wpos against an in-flight chunk and the committed mapping
results.claim: deck_loop_remap (audio task) snapshots dk.wpos and schedules the new window at that frame, but the reader task may already be in the middle of filling a chunk at wpos using the OLD mapping. It also computes the carried phase with the committed loop_start/loop_len_fr/map_p0 even when an earlier scheduled move (rm_at) is still pending and the reader frontier is already under that pending mapping.
results.scenario: Turn CV6 or CV7 while looping. The reader has already read up to 4096 frames past `at` under the old window. When the cursor reaches rm_at, dk_map switches to the new window for slots that hold old-window audio, so up to ~93 ms of the wrong material plays and ui_fpos/PLL phase disagree with what is heard. A second knob move before the first commits overwrites rm_start/rm_len/rm_p0/rm_at. Frames between the old and new `at` were written under the first pending window but are mapped under the old loop. The phase offset is computed from the wrong mapping, so the loop slips against the clock.
results.reasoning: The mismatch is real: the reader computes ff at :193 before the SD read, so a remap during the read leaves up to 4096 old-window frames at [rm_at, rm_at+got); and a second remap before the first commits computes off from map_p0/loop_len_fr (:559) and moves rm_at forward, so frames written under the first pending window are mapped as the committed one. The claimed clock slip does not follow: every window start is grid + k*len and every length is a whole number of pulses (dk_min_q :436, :502-504, :782, :828), so all mappings agree modulo one pulse and p_trk is unchanged. What remains is a window cut landing up to 93 ms late, an intermediate window heard for up to the 0.5 s lead during a sweep, and ui_fpos showing the old window meanwhile. Consequence downgraded to display.
results.fix_sketch: The in-flight half is covered by the reader revalidation in #4 (drop the chunk if dk_map(w0) no longer equals ff). For the second-move half, when rm_at is pending compute off from rm_p0/rm_len (the dk_live_start/dk_live_len pattern) instead of the committed pair. Low priority.

results.title: Freeze-mode loop release ignores a pending scheduled window
results.claim: Loop release assumes everything the reader buffered up to the next seam of the committed window is valid under the new linear mapping. It ignores a pending scheduled window (rm_at). Ring data at counters >= rm_at was written under the rm_* mapping, and rm_at is then zeroed.
results.scenario: Move the loop window (CV6/CV7), then release the loop (TR2) within the read-ahead time (~0.5 s) before the cursor commits the move. The reader has already filled [rm_at, wpos) with the new window's audio, but release rebases to linear from the OLD window's file position and only truncates wpos to the old window's seam. The cursor plays the new window's material where the linear mapping says old-window continuation, so wrong audio is heard until the truncated wpos is reached, and ui_fpos/PLL phase are then computed from a mapping that does not match the audio.
results.reasoning: Release rebases to linear from loop_start/loop_len_fr/map_p0, zeroes rm_at and only truncates wpos to the committed window's next seam (:455-463). With a move pending, ring frames [rm_at, min(wpos, valid_to)) hold the rm_* window's audio but are now mapped as the old window's linear continuation, so up to ~0.5 s of the other window plays with two hard cuts. Only freeze mode is affected: the default (loop_freeze false) issues a seek at :478-482 and the reader rebases onto fresh slots. It also needs rm_at < valid_to, i.e. a loop longer than the remaining lead.
results.fix_sketch: Before clearing rm_at in the release branch, clamp the keep point: if (dk.rm_at && dk.rm_at < valid_to) valid_to = dk.rm_at; so the reader refills linear from the scheduled switch. Route the truncation through the same reader-side handshake as #4.

results.title: process() truncates dk.wpos under the reader with no handshake
results.claim: The audio task truncates dk.wpos (here, and again at line 534 on engage) while the reader task does a non-atomic read-modify-write `dk.wpos += got` (line 230). There is no handshake between them.
results.scenario: The reader has copied a chunk read under the loop mapping (or the linear mapping, on engage) and is about to do `dk.wpos += got` when process() truncates wpos to valid_to. The reader then writes old_wpos+got, overwriting the truncation and re-marking as valid the frames written under the OLD mapping beyond the seam. After release or engage, playback runs into up to 4096 frames of audio from the wrong file position, which is audible as a repeated or wrong-content stretch. The same race applies to deck_loop_remap reading wpos.
results.reasoning: wpos is written by the audio task at :463 and :534 and by the reader at :230 with no protocol, unlike rpos ("reader is the ONLY seek-writer", :165). Beyond the narrow load/store race the finder describes there is a much wider one: ff is computed at :193 before sd_lock_take and the read, and the ring slot is taken from a fresh dk.wpos at :225, so a truncation during the read (ms, longer while analysis holds sd_lock) drops a chunk read for the old frontier at valid_to. On engage the read-ahead is ~7 s, so nearly every engage truncates; when a read is in flight the first loop wrap plays up to 93 ms from seconds ahead in the file. A few percent of engages by reader duty cycle; freeze-mode release has the same hole.
results.fix_sketch: Make the reader the only writer of wpos, mirroring the seek protocol: process() publishes the keep point (a volatile cap plus flag, with can_play bounded by it) and the reader applies it at the top of its loop. After each read the reader snapshots w0 before the read and drops the chunk (cur_ff = -1) if dk.wpos != w0 or dk_map(w0) != ff.

results.title: Resume from pause inside a KO-II loop lands at the window start
results.claim: deck_toggle_play() resumes via the seek protocol but does not exit the KO-II loop or rebase the loop mapping. The reader's seek only rewrites map_p0/map_f0, so under a still-active loop the resume position `to` is ignored: dk_map uses loop_start + ((p - map_p0) % loop_len_fr) with map_p0 = the new base.
results.scenario: Loop engaged mid-window, TR1 tap to pause, TR1 tap to resume. seek_to = the cursor's file frame inside the window, but with loop_active still true the reader reads from loop_start, so playback resumes at the window start rather than where it paused. If a scheduled move (rm_at, rm_p0) was pending, stale rm_p0 is used against the new counter base, giving an arbitrary phase within the new window. The PLL then fights the discontinuity.
results.reasoning: deck_toggle_play (TR1 tap, :745) leaves loop_active set and requests a seek to dk_map(rpos_i). The reader's seek only writes map_p0 = base and map_f0 = to (:162-167), and with loop_active dk_map ignores map_f0: dk_map(base) = loop_start + 0 (:63-64). So the resume position is the window start, contrary to the comment at :336-340. With a move pending (rm_at is never committed while paused, since rpos does not advance) the stale rm_p0 gives an arbitrary offset in the new window. deck_restart, deck_seek_beats and deck_load_track all clear loop_active first, so only this path has it.
results.fix_sketch: In the reader's seek block, when dk.loop_active and `to` lies inside [loop_start, loop_start+loop_len_fr), set dk.map_p0 = base - (to - dk.loop_start), the same form engage uses at :529. Commit or clear a pending rm_* in deck_toggle_play before computing `to`.

results.title: deck_seek_beats divides by beat_tf with no zero guard
results.claim: beat_tf is computed as (uint32_t)(60*44100/track_bpm) when track_bpm > 20 with no `!beat_tf` guard here, unlike every other caller. A track_bpm above ~132300 gives beat_tf == 0 and an integer divide-by-zero. track_bpm comes unclamped from the sidecar 'bpm' (deck_load_track).
results.scenario: A hand-edited or corrupt .JSN sidecar with "bpm": 200000 (or a value that becomes huge after feel x2) is loaded. Turning the encoder while unsynced (EV_FWD/EV_BWD -> deck_seek_beats) divides by zero and the UI task panics.
results.reasoning: Every other user guards beat_tf (:94, :490, :586, :888, dk_len_for :444); this one does not, and the int64 divide by zero traps in the UI task on EV_FWD/EV_BWD when not locked+synced (deck_menu.c:346/352). The finder's threshold is wrong: beat_tf = 2646000/bpm is zero only above 2,646,000 BPM (1,323,000 with feel x2), so "bpm": 200000 gives beat_tf 13 and no crash. The only unclamped source is the sidecar at :292-293; analysis is bounded and the Setup row clamps 40..240 (deck_menu.c:418-419). So it needs an absurd hand-edited or corrupt sidecar.
results.fix_sketch: Clamp at the source in deck_load_track: treat a sidecar bpm outside a sane range (say 20..1000) as 0 = unknown, which also lets auto-analysis repair it. Add `if (!beat_tf) beat_tf = DK_RATE;` in deck_seek_beats to match the other callers.

results.title: sample_resolve stat() walk runs without sd_lock
results.claim: sample_resolve() does up to SF_N_DIRS x SF_N_EXTS stat() calls on the SD card without sd_lock. deck_load_track's sample_resolve_aux calls do the same from the UI or httpd task. The project rule is that every SD I/O burst holds sd_lock.
results.scenario: The reader resolves a new track while the analysis task or another machine's reader is doing raw FatFS reads. The stat walks bypass the lock and can interleave on the SD bus, which the notes say wedges or corrupts the card (glitches and read errors under load).
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 6.12 (Low, on the Watch list): its files_raw_handler lines are the sample_resolve calls, i.e. this same unlocked stat loop. It is not Deck-specific: all ~30 callers (sampler3, slicer, dualdeck, tape, sample_ram, rest-api) call it outside sd_lock. The corruption claim is not supported: FF_FS_REENTRANT is 1 in IDF 4.3 (ffconf.h:287, 10 s timeout), so f_stat and the raw f_read path are serialized by FatFS's own volume lock. Nothing new beyond noting the fix belongs in the helper.
results.fix_sketch: If 6.12 is ever picked up, take sd_lock inside sample_resolve around the stat loop (the mutex is recursive, so callers that already hold it are fine) rather than at each call site.

results.title: Deck playback counters wrap at 2^32: deck mutes until the next seek or track load
results.claim: wpos and rpos_i are monotonic 32-bit playback counters that grow by 8 s of frames on every seek, plus continuously while playing. At wrap (~27 h of playback, or ~12k seeks) the slot mapping p % DK_RING_FRAMES breaks (2^32 is not a multiple of 352800). Comparisons such as `rpos_i + 1 < wpos`, `p >= rm_at` and `wpos < map_p0 + ...` also break.
results.scenario: Deck left playing for over a day, or heavily scrubbed. When wpos wraps before rpos, can_play is false until rpos wraps as well. The slots the reader fills after the wrap are not contiguous with the slots the cursor is reading, so garbage or stale audio plays for up to the read-ahead (~7 s) at each wrap.
results.reasoning: wpos/rpos_i are uint32 and reset only on track load (deck.c:145); every seek adds DK_RING_FRAMES (deck.c:162). The finder understated the result: once wpos wraps, `dk.rpos_i + 1 < dk.wpos` (deck.c:955) is false, and rpos_i only advances when can_play is true, so rpos never wraps and the deck stays silent with playing=true; the reader's signed slead stays positive, so its self-heal (deck.c:176) never fires. Also 2^32 % 352800 = 332896, so the chunk crossing the wrap lands in the wrong slots, and the linear have_room test (deck.c:195) fails when map_p0 + remaining wraps. Needs about 27 h looped on one track load at 1x (10.8 h at the 2.5x cap) or about 12k seeks; not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Make the compares modular like the reader's existing `slead`: can_play as `(int32_t)(dk.wpos - dk.rpos_i) > 1`, the rm_at tests as signed differences, linear have_room as `(wpos - map_p0) < (file_frames - map_f0)`. In the seek handler use a small base with the same slot (`dk.wpos % DK_RING_FRAMES + DK_RING_FRAMES`) so seeks stop consuming counter space. For continuous play, have the reader rebase once through the existing seek protocol when wpos passes about 0xC0000000, or make DK_RING_FRAMES a power of two.

results.title: Deck sidecar read-modify-write is not atomic between analysis commit and deck_set_feel
results.claim: The sidecar update is an unsynchronised read-modify-write of the same JSN file, run in the analysis task here and in the UI task in deck_set_feel (deck.c 386-392). The two can interleave, and the later writer drops the other's key.
results.scenario: The user cycles Feel in Setup just as an analysis finishes. Both read the old JSON. deck_set_feel writes {feel}, then commit writes {bpm,grid,dver,conf} from its stale copy without the new feel (or the reverse order drops the fresh bpm/grid). The per-track feel silently reverts on the next load, or the analysed tempo is lost and the track is re-analysed.
results.reasoning: readJSONFileAsCJSON and writeJSONFile each take sd_lock on their own (fileio.c:225, 318); nothing holds it across the read-modify-write in deck_analysis_commit (deck_analysis.c:54-69, analysis task prio 4) or deck_set_feel (deck.c:386-392, UI task prio 11, from deck_menu.c:434). If the Feel edit arrives while commit is in or just past its read, the UI task blocks on sd_lock, wakes when the read releases it, writes {old + feel}, then commit writes its stale root and drops "feel". The window is tens of ms once per analysis, so only that direction is realistic; the lost-bpm order would need the analysis task to fit two lock acquisitions into the UI task's microsecond gap. Loss is the per-track feel reverting to x1 on the next load; not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Hold sd_lock (recursive) across the whole read-modify-write in both deck_analysis_commit and deck_set_feel: sd_lock_take() before readJSONFileAsCJSON, sd_lock_give() after writeJSONFile. The nested takes inside the fileio helpers are fine with the recursive mutex.

chunks.coverage_notes: Read in full: components/machine_dualdeck/dualdeck.c (1386 lines), dualdeck_menu.c (689), dualdeck_priv.h (237), include/machine_dualdeck.h (4 lines), CMakeLists.txt. Cross-read for call paths: util/include/worker.h, util/sampfile.c (sampfile_read, sample_resolve, sample_resolve_aux), util/include/svf.h, machine/include/clock.h (clockin_ppb_eff), parts of machine/clock.c (octave fold), menu/clock_ui.c (ppq ladder), menu/cvmtx.c (src/override/abs/track), menu/sample_browser.c (sample_browser_selected), machine/machine_core.c (start/stop/failure fallback), audio.c (audio_status_set_voices), fileio.c readJSONFileAsCJSON, and bpm_analysis.c busy hook. I did NOT read components/machine_deck/deck_analysis.c or the body of bpm_analyze, and I did not read cvmtx_load/save or writeJSONFile. Dropped as speculation or too minor: torn `pending` name on rapid double-loads; uint32 playback-counter wrap after ~27 h (ring slot discontinuity); (uint32_t) casts of out-of-range JSON grid/bpm doubles; the legacy CV-map migration `valueint & 7` turning -1 (off) into CV8; a two-pending-remap mapping mismatch that only affects UI and PLL fine phase; stale ui_fpos against a shorter new file_frames (display only, transient); an empty-name load leaving stale file_frames (not reachable from the browser).

results.title: bar_edge never true when per_bar clamps to 1 (slow clock at PPQ 1): armed start/stop never fire
results.claim: When per_bar is clamped to 1, `dd.pulses % 1` is always 0, so the test `== 1` never passes and bar_edge is never true. Every quantized start and stop then stays armed forever while the clock is locked.
results.scenario: per_bar = (uint32_t)(DD_PPB_EFF()*4+0.5). The effective ppb is the clock_ui ladder {1,2,4,8} times the detector octave fold, which runs 0.25..4 (clock.c ~L240). A slow pulse train (about one pulse per bar) lets the fold drop to oct 0.25, so ppb_eff = 0.25 and per_bar = (uint32_t)1.5 = 1. With `pulses % 1 == 1` never true, deck_fire() is only reached when the clock is unlocked. TR1 tap/hold on a locked clock arms the deck and nothing ever fires. The UI shows the amber ARM state indefinitely.
results.reasoning: ppb_eff = ppb*oct (clock.h:71-75); at PPQ 1 a pulse train under 38/min folds oct to 0.25 (clock.c:240-243) and still locks down to 15/min (clock.c:180), so per_bar = (uint32_t)(0.25*4+0.5) = 1 and `pulses % 1 == 1` is always false. deck_fire() is then only reached via `!locked` (L918), so TR1 tap/hold arms stay pending for as long as the clock is locked. One pulse per bar at 60-150 BPM is exactly this case, and the 1.10 fix deliberately made such slow jack clocks lockable. Not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: Make the test hold for per_bar 1: `bar_edge = pulse && locked && (per_bar <= 1 || (dd.pulses % per_bar) == 1)`. No other change needed.

results.title: Waveform peak of 32768 wraps to 0 in the uint8 thumbnail column
results.claim: The waveform thumbnail peak is the absolute value of an int16, which can be 32768 for a -32768 sample. 32768>>7 = 256, and the cast to uint8_t wraps it to 0. The loudest column is drawn as silence.
results.scenario: Line 229 in reader_serve: `v->wf[v->wf_col] = (uint8_t)(peak >> 7);`. A track containing a full-scale negative sample (-32768) in a 128-frame slice, as clipped or normalized material commonly does, stores 0 for that column. The stacked layout (v_paint_slice) and the side-by-side layout (h_bar_slice) both draw it at the minimum height of 2 px, leaving a hole exactly where the track is loudest.
results.reasoning: `sv = -sv` on an int gives 32768 for a -32768 sample, 32768>>7 = 256, and the uint8_t cast stores 0; every other value tops out at 255. Both painters (dualdeck_menu.c:179-181 and :346-348) then draw that column at the 2 px minimum. Only an exact -32768 inside the 128-frame slice sampled for that column triggers it, so it needs hard-clipped material. The same line exists in deck.c:256 and sampler3.c:133; not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: Clamp before the shift: `if (peak > 32767) peak = 32767;` at L229, and the same one-liner in deck.c:256 and sampler3.c:133.

results.title: Reader task's two MALLOC_CAP_DMA buffers are never NULL-checked
results.claim: The two internal-DMA buffers for the reader task (16 KB and 1 KB) are never checked for NULL. The task then passes them to sampfile_read/fread and to the seam blend.
results.scenario: Internal RAM is the scarce pool (CLAUDE.md notes the largest free block is what fails). If either malloc returns NULL, for example after a machine switch from Radio or Tracker or while the web page holds sockets, the reader gets NULL for `chunk` on the first track load and fread() writes to address 0. That is a LoadProhibited panic and a reboot. start() reports ESP_OK because the worker spawned fine.
results.reasoning: chunk (16 KB) and tail (1 KB) go straight into reader_serve; sampfile_read (sampfile.c:29-35) passes dst to fread with no check, so a NULL chunk is written through on the first fill, which the autosaved ta/tb load triggers right after start. dualdeck_start has already returned ESP_OK because worker_spawn succeeded, so the Stub fallback never engages. It needs a 16 KB internal-DMA allocation to fail at task entry, which is an OOM condition I cannot establish as normal. deck.c:124-125 and sampler3.c:142 have the same unchecked pattern; not recorded on 09-16 (6.10 is rest-api only).
results.fix_sketch: Allocate chunk and tail in dualdeck_start() before worker_spawn (file-statics, as the rings are), return ESP_ERR_NO_MEM on failure so the core's Stub fallback takes over, and free them in dualdeck_stop() only after worker_stop succeeds. Apply the same to deck.c and sampler3.c.

results.title: Failed track open leaves loading (and seek_req) set forever, stalling later analyses
results.claim: When a track fails to open or probe (missing file, 24-bit or 48k WAV, etc.), `loading` set by dualdeck_load_track is never cleared. Its only clear sites are inside `if (*fp && ...)`.
results.scenario: Load an unsupported or unopenable track onto deck A. Deck A keeps loading==true and seek_req==true forever. dd_busy() returns true forever because it ORs in `loading`. dd_maybe_analyze() has already started the analysis task for that load, and bpm_analyze() spins in its busy() wait at bpm_analysis.c:41. dd.an_running stays true and the panel shows 'analyzing N%' indefinitely. Every later unstamped-track load on either deck only queues in an_pending, so the deck never gets a grid and cannot loop. The task only ends at machine stop.
results.reasoning: `loading` is set in dualdeck_load_track (L377) and only cleared at L208/L211, both inside `if (*fp && ...)`; after a failed fopen/probe nothing clears it, and L131 also leaves seek_req set. The finder's hang on the failed track itself is wrong: bpm_analyze returns -1 at once when resolve/probe fails (bpm_analysis.c:71-104). The real effect is that dd_busy() (L262) stays true, so any later analysis of an unstamped track on the OTHER deck sits in wait_idle (bpm_analysis.c:41) at "analyzing 0%" until the failed deck gets a good track or the machine stops. Reached by an autosaved ta/tb naming a file since deleted from the card, or a file the probe rejects; not a hang of the unit.
results.fix_sketch: In the failure branch at L121 also clear `v->loading = false; v->seek_req = false;` (and skip setting seek_req at L131 when *fp is NULL). Optionally blank v->track so the header shows the deck as empty.

results.title: dualdeck_load_track does not clear loop_active/rm_at; old loop window maps the new track
results.claim: Loading a track does not clear loop_active, rm_at, loop_start or loop_len_fr. Only deck_fire (start/stop) clears them. A loop from the previous track therefore keeps applying to the new track's reader mapping.
results.scenario: The load is reachable while a deck is looping through preset_load: POST /remote/params with a new "ta" or "tb", or the autosave path. Deck A is looping a window at 3:00-3:10 of a long track, and a shorter track is loaded. The reader still maps through loop_start+(p-map_p0)%loop_len_fr, and the new map_p0=0/map_f0 are ignored while loop_active. `limit = win_st+win_len-ff` then exceeds the new file's end. The reader pre-fills the ring with the wrong or past-EOF window (short reads), and the loading-clear at L211 is skipped because lp is true. The UI draws a loop box from ui_lstart/ui_llen beyond the new file_frames. The wrong audio is only healed when the user starts the deck.
results.reasoning: deck_load_track clears the loop first (deck.c:271); the dualdeck copy does not, so after a load the reader's dd_window/dd_map (L63-66, L80) still use the old loop_start/loop_len_fr on the new file. If loop_start is past the new file end nothing fills and L211 is skipped (lp true), so loading sticks until a start; if it is inside, the ring is pre-filled from the old window position and deck_fire (L718) sees map==grid_offset and !loading, skips the seek, and the start plays up to 0.5 s of the wrong position before cutting to the cue. The panel blocks loads on a playing deck only at browser entry (dualdeck_menu.c:525), so it needs a `ta`/`tb` change via /remote/params on a looping deck, or starting and looping the deck with the browser already open.
results.fix_sketch: Mirror deck_load_track: set `v->loop_active = false; v->rm_at = 0;` at the top of dualdeck_load_track before `playing = false`.

results.title: Loop engage/release truncates wpos under an in-flight reader chunk
results.claim: The reader does a read-modify-write on wpos with no handshake, while the audio task rewrites the same variable in dualdeck_loop_toggle and dualdeck_loop_remap.
results.scenario: On loop release or engage (dualdeck_loop_toggle L595/L661), the audio task truncates `v->wpos = valid_to` so that ring data mapped by the old window is discarded. If the reader is inside its SD read (sd_lock held, up to 4096 frames) at that moment, it finishes and does `wpos += got` on the truncated value. The ring slots [valid_to, valid_to+got) then hold data written under the old mapping for a different file position, and they are marked valid. Playback crosses the seam and plays up to ~93 ms of audio from the wrong file position, an audible glitch or jump, and it corrupts the PLL phase. dd_loop_remap has the same race: it reads `at = v->wpos` before the reader's in-flight chunk lands, so that chunk is mapped by the old window.
results.reasoning: The reader computes ff from wpos at L168, blocks in the SD read, then writes the chunk at the CURRENT wpos and does `wpos += got` (L201-206) with no check that wpos moved. dualdeck_loop_toggle runs in the audio task (L902) and sets `wpos = valid_to` at L595/L661, so a toggle during a read lands a chunk read under the old mapping (on engage, several seconds ahead in the track) at the seam, marked valid, with no seam blend: up to 4096 frames (93 ms) of wrong audio at the first wrap. The reader does one such read per ~93 ms per playing deck, so a fraction of ordinary TR2 presses hit it; I could not measure that fraction. The PLL claim is overstated (the mapping is unaffected) and the dd_loop_remap variant only delays the window switch by one chunk; deck.c:230/463/534 has the same race, not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: In reader_serve snapshot `w0 = v->wpos` before the read and commit `wpos = w0 + got` only if wpos still equals w0, otherwise drop the chunk and set `*cur_ff = (uint32_t)-1`. Put that compare-and-advance and the two truncations in dualdeck_loop_toggle under a short portMUX, as s_an_mux is used. Port the same to deck.c.

results.title: Trailing `an_running = false` outside s_an_mux can clobber a hand-off
results.claim: The task's final `dd.an_running = false` runs outside s_an_mux after the queue-empty decision. It can clobber an `an_running = true` set by dd_maybe_analyze in the gap. The comment at dd_maybe_analyze says this hand-off is protected.
results.scenario: The analysis task empties the queue under the lock (an_running=false) and breaks. Before it reaches L336, the UI task loads an unstamped track. dd_maybe_analyze sees an_running==false, sets an_running=true/an_deck/an_track, then waits in worker_idle. The old task executes L336 and resets an_running=false, then exits. The new task is spawned with an_running==false, so a further load on the other deck starts a second 'first' run. That overwrites dd.an_deck/an_track while the first analysis is still reading them, and worker_spawn fails ('analyze task start failed') and leaves an_deck=-1. The window is very narrow.
results.reasoning: The task clears an_running under the lock at L327, leaves the critical section, then stores false again at L336 unlocked; a dd_maybe_analyze that sets an_running = true in between (L355) and waits in worker_idle has its flag overwritten before the new task spawns. A later load during that run then takes the non-queued path, overwrites dd.an_track, fails worker_spawn, and the running analysis writes its result under the other track's name at L315. The defect is in the code, but the window is the few instructions between L333 and L336 and the UI/httpd task must run its critical section inside it; I could not establish that this happens in practice. The lock came from the 10.4/10.5 fix (cb19915), which left this one store outside it.
results.fix_sketch: Delete L336 and clear the flag only on the abort path, under the lock: at L313 take s_an_mux, set `dd.an_running = false; dd.an_deck = -1;`, release, then break. The queue-empty path already clears it under the lock at L327.

results.title: deck_rate has no beat_tf==0 guard; a huge sidecar bpm makes rate_sm NaN until restart
results.claim: deck_rate has no beat_tf==0 guard, unlike the loop and resync paths. A sidecar bpm above about 2.6e6 gives beat_tf 0, seg_tf 0 and fmodf(x, 0) = NaN. The NaN then becomes sticky in rate_sm.
results.scenario: A hand-edited or garbage sidecar "bpm" (only checked for `> 20`) with a locked clock gives err = NaN, phase_int = NaN and rate = NaN. The clamps `rate<0.25`/`rate>2.5` do not catch NaN, so rate_sm becomes NaN. Because `rate_sm += 0.08*(rate - rate_sm)` stays NaN even after a good track is loaded, rpos_f becomes NaN and the deck freezes. NaN samples then reach `(int32_t)mix_l`, which is UB and outputs noise or full-scale. Only a machine restart clears it.
results.reasoning: The sidecar bpm is only tested `> 20` (L393, L754); above about 2.65e6 (or inf) beat_tf is 0, seg_tf is 0, fmodf(x,0)/0 is NaN, and the clamps at L773-782 do not catch NaN, so rate_sm (reset only in start(), L810) stays NaN. rpos_f and s_last_out then go NaN, and NaN*gain poisons the mix for both decks before the float-to-int cast at L1258, until the machine restarts. Every writer of "bpm" in the tree (analysis, sampler3, looper) produces sane values, so it needs a hand-edited or corrupt sidecar and a locked clock. The loop and resync paths already guard `!beat_tf` (L613, L675, L990); not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: Reject the value at the source: in dualdeck_load_track accept the sidecar bpm only inside a sane range (e.g. 20..1000), else leave track_bpm 0 so the track is re-analysed. Also add `&& beat_tf` to the lock condition in deck_rate, matching the guards at L613/L675.

results.title: sample_resolve() stat() probes run outside sd_lock (dualdeck reader + load_track)
results.claim: The reader task calls sample_resolve() (up to 28 stat() calls over 7 folders x 4 extensions) before taking sd_lock. dualdeck_load_track does the same with sample_resolve_aux on the UI task.
results.scenario: The card is shared with the other deck's stream and with httpd/recording bursts that hold sd_lock, and the stat() calls hit FatFS/SDMMC on the same bus without the lock, contrary to the CLAUDE.md rule that every SD burst holds sd_lock. Loading a track while the other deck is streaming or another task is doing raw or VFS I/O can contend on the bus and cause card errors or a stalled ring.
results.reasoning: The code is as quoted (dualdeck.c:112 and :389; the unlocked stat() is sampfile.c:91), but it is the same defect as 09-16 finding 6.12 (stat() without sd_lock, Low, on the Watch list): 6.12's peaks_handler/files_raw_handler sites are this same sample_resolve-before-sd_lock_take call (rest-api.c:2590, 527-531), and Deck, Sampler3, Slicer, sampplay and sample_load do it identically. The Watch reason still holds: IDF 4.3 FatFS is built FF_FS_REENTRANT=1, so each f_stat takes the volume mutex that the raw f_read path also takes, and SDMMC transactions are serialized by s_request_mutex, so the claimed bus contention / card errors / stalled ring do not follow. Worst case is a stat waiting behind another task's burst; the 10 s FATFS timeout is not realistically reached. Nothing new beyond 6.12 except that the root is the shared resolver, not the dualdeck call site.
results.fix_sketch: If 6.12 is ever taken off Watch, fix it once at the root: take sd_lock per stat() inside sample_resolve() in sampfile.c (the mutex is recursive, so the rename handler that already holds it is fine, and per-probe locking lets the other deck's refills interleave as sample_next_index does). The same goes for sample_resolve_f in sampfile_f.c. No change is needed in dualdeck.c.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: components/machine_tape/tape.c (1130 lines), tape_menu.c (1038), tape_priv.h (286). machine_core.c (machine_activate / block_wait) and recording_poll_load were read to confirm the stop() handshake and the fname buffer size. I did not read machine_tape.h (it does not exist in the directory; only include/ and CMakeLists.txt are there).

Not traced: the internals of fxrack, cvmtx, sample_next_index, sampfile_read and the recording_* functions called from the audio task. The card-record path was reviewed only at the call level. I dropped these as low value or unreachable:
- preset_load rdest/rsrc changing while the transport is rolling.
- tape_eff_window with len<64 after a heavy cut.
- Cosmetic playhead stale pixel.
- The take_num double increment.
- The small autosave_req versus crop save_a/save_b overwrite window.
- restore_id repointed before the file exists.

results.title: rec_stop_target is never cleared by tape_rec_stop / tape_erase / a fresh punch-in
results.claim: tape_rec_stop() and tape_rec_stop_request() never clear tp.rec_stop_target. A pending quantized stop that is cancelled by a second punch-out press, or overtaken by tape-full, leaves a stale target behind.
results.scenario: Rec Quant = beat or bar. Record a fresh take and press TR2 to punch out. rec_stop_target is set and recording continues to the beat. Press TR2 again before the beat: tape_rec_stop_request sees rec_stop_target already set and falls through to tape_rec_stop() (line 226), which stops immediately and leaves the target set. Later, punch in on the playing loop (overdub) or start a new fresh take. The frame loop test at lines 531-532 (recording && rec_stop_target && pos >= target) fires when pos crosses the stale target. tape_rec_stop_at then rewrites in_pt=0 and out_pt=target, and it stashes a save. The loop is truncated or the take is cut short at an arbitrary point. TR1 press clears the target (line 388), but no other path does. The same stale target survives a tape-full stop and a tape_erase.
results.reasoning: rec_stop_target is cleared only at tape.c:202 (tape_rec_stop_at) and :388 (TR1 stop); a second TR2 press falls through :214 to tape_rec_stop() (:226) and leaves it set. The finder's overdub case cannot fire (the cancelled take has len < target and an overdub keeps pos < len), but the next FRESH take without a TR1 stop in between (hold-erase at :423-427, one-shot end, tape-full) is auto-finalised at the stale target by :531-532, or its quantised punch-out stops immediately. New beyond 11.6 (Watch, tape-full/erase only): in MOMENTARY mode :404 calls tape_rec_stop_request() every block while the gate is released, so the block after the target is set it falls through to the immediate stop - Rec Quant never quantises in momentary mode and every take leaves a stale target.
results.fix_sketch: Clear tp.rec_stop_target in tape_rec_stop(), tape_erase() and the fresh branch of tape_rec_start(). In the momentary branch (:404) only call tape_rec_stop_request() when !tp.rec_stop_target, so a pending beat-stop is allowed to run to the target.

results.title: TR1 'plays' a blank tape; TR2 then starts an overdub that writes nothing
results.claim: TR1 is allowed to start playback on an empty tape when rec_src is INPUT (line 390: `else if (tp.len || tp.rec_src == TPS_INPUT)`). A TR2 press while playing is then treated as an overdub, with rec_extend=false. Nothing is written when len==0.
results.scenario: Blank tape. Press TR1 to play, so playing=true and len=0. Press TR2 to record. tape_rec_start takes the overdub branch (playing is true) with rec_extend=false. In the frame loop the write plan uses `!empty_rec && w < tp.len`, and len is 0, so wdo is never set. The UI shows REC in red and take_dirty is set, but no audio is captured. Punching out does nothing because rec_extend is false, so there is no stash and no save. The take is silently lost. The momentary-mode path at lines 399-402 has the same flaw.
results.reasoning: tape.c:390 lets TR1 set playing=true with len==0 when rec_src is INPUT (the default, and the Live hint says 'TR1:play TR2:rec' on a blank tape). TR2 (punch :409 or momentary :401) then takes tape_rec_start's overdub branch (:170, rec_extend=false), and the write plan at :515 needs w < tp.len, which is 0, so no frame is ever stored while the header shows REC. Punch-out via tape_rec_stop does nothing (no rec_extend, len 0), so nothing is saved; playing an empty tape also mutes the monitor (:483-485). Not in the 09-16 review; only the 0.7 s hold-erase gesture escapes it.
results.fix_sketch: In tape_rec_start() take the fresh-take branch when `!tp.playing || tp.len == 0` (covers punch and momentary), and/or drop the `|| tp.rec_src == TPS_INPUT` clause at :390 so TR1 does not roll an empty tape.

results.title: tape_cut deletes the full crop when the clipboard alloc was trimmed
results.claim: tape_copy() returns 0 when the clipboard alloc was only partly satisfied: bank_alloc returns 1 for trimmed, and `if (tp.clip.cap < n) n = tp.clip.cap` shrinks the copy. tape_cut() then deletes the FULL crop length regardless of how much was copied.
results.scenario: The tape takes most of PSRAM (40 s is about 3.5 MB of the 4 MB pool, plus FX slabs). A Cut of a 10 s crop only gets a few 128 KB clip banks, so the clipboard holds a fraction of it. tape_cut still closes the gap for the whole crop (lines 723-727) and shrinks len by n. The audio outside the clipboard is destroyed and cannot be pasted back. The Copy row shows a shorter 'held' time but Cut gives no warning.
results.reasoning: bank_alloc returns 1 for a trimmed allocation (:81) but tape_copy only tests < 0 (:713), shrinks n to clip.cap (:714) and returns 0; tape_cut then recomputes n = out_pt - in_pt (:723) and closes the gap for the whole crop. Arithmetic: a 40 s tape is 3.53 MB of the 4.00 MB pool (tape.c:29-33), leaving at most 3 clip banks (about 4.4 s); 30 s plus delay and reverb slabs leaves about the same, so any longer Cut loses the remainder with no message. If zero banks are obtained the path is safe (-2), so only the partial case loses audio.
results.fix_sketch: Have tape_copy() pass bank_alloc's 1 (trimmed) through as its return value, and make tape_cut() bail without touching the tape when the return is non-zero or tp.clip_len < out_pt - in_pt. The Setup row can show the refusal the way stopped_or() does.

results.title: tape_set_len_sel and the buffer edits run while save_task is still reading the banks
results.claim: The destructive edits (tape_set_len_sel, tape_norm, tape_reverse, tape_fade, tape_cut, tape_paste, tape_clear) and tape_load check only tp_stopped(). They do not check tp.save_busy, so they run while save_task is still streaming the same banks from the card.
results.scenario: Record a fresh take and punch out. The autosave writer starts, and a 30-40 s take takes seconds to write. Press TR1 to stop, then Rev, Cut or Paste. save_task keeps reading with tp_rd() and writes a blend of old and new samples to the file. drop_spoiled is only set by audio-task writes, so nothing flags it. Worse, Setup > Tape Len (or a /remote/params preset load with a different `lsel`) calls tape_set_len_sel, which calls bank_free. bank_free sets blk[i]=NULL and frees the slabs while save_task is mid-loop. tp_rd then dereferences NULL or freed PSRAM, which is a crash or garbage in the file.
results.reasoning: tape_set_len_sel (:580), tape_norm/reverse/fade/cut/paste/clear and tape_load_inner (:608, waits only when take_dirty) gate on tp_stopped() alone, while tape_stop (:1034) is the only place that waits for save_busy before bank_free. Setup > Tape Len (tape_menu.c:870) or a preset `lsel` (:1079) during the multi-second autosave runs bank_free, which frees and NULLs blk[] under save_task's tp_rd loop (:793); shrinking 30 s to 15 s leaves the upper blk[] NULL for good, so the writer dereferences NULL (LoadProhibited), otherwise the file gets freed or reallocated memory. The edit ops instead produce a blended file that drop_spoiled (audio-task only, :560) never flags and that save_task then marks clean (:820). Distinct from 11.3, which fixed the audio-task side of the same free with machine_block_wait.
results.fix_sketch: In tape_set_len_sel() wait for the writer exactly as tape_stop does (`while (tp.save_busy) vTaskDelay(pdMS_TO_TICKS(20));`, also clearing autosave_req) before bank_alloc. Make the destructive edits and tape_load_inner refuse (or wait) while tp.save_busy, with the Setup rows showing 'saving...' as row 19 already does.

results.title: tape_drop_adopt_kick forces playing=false without checking tp.recording
results.claim: tape_drop_adopt_kick() forces playing=false but does not check tp.recording. A crop pressed while playing leaves adopt_id pending for the duration of the file write. Punching TR2 in during that window makes the kick run with recording=true.
results.scenario: Press Crop while the loop plays, then press TR2 (overdub) within the few seconds the writer runs. When save_busy clears, adopt_kick sets playing=false while recording is still true. tape_load then refuses because !tp_stopped(). The engine is left with recording=true, playing=false and a frozen playhead. pos no longer advances (it only advances when playing), so the record head overwrites one frame position over and over. The user sees REC with a stuck playhead, and TR1 press takes the not-playing branch and restarts playback instead of stopping the record.
results.reasoning: The finder's overdub scenario is normally caught: overdub writes land inside [save_a,save_b), set drop_spoiled (:560) and the kick returns at :897. The guard misses a FRESH take: Crop with the window not at the tape start (save_a > 0), then TR2 from stop records from frame 0 and the short crop file closes before the head reaches save_a, so drop_spoiled stays false, :901 clears playing and tape_load refuses at :608. That leaves recording=true, playing=false, rec_extend=true with pos frozen: the head rewrites one frame (:511-513), the take stops growing under a REC header, and TR1 then restarts at pos 0 still recording over it. The same happens for any punch-in between save_busy clearing and the next menu tick; this pre-load window is not the one 11.4 closed (tp.loading only covers the load itself).
results.fix_sketch: In tape_drop_adopt_kick(), after clearing adopt_id, skip the adoption (log and return) when tp.recording is set, before touching tp.playing. To close the remaining gap, raise tp.loading and call machine_block_wait() before that check so the gates are already held.

results.title: In-place edits never mark the take dirty, so they are dropped on leave or reboot
results.claim: The in-place edits (tape_paste, tape_cut, tape_norm, tape_reverse, tape_fade) never set take_dirty or repoint restore_id. After an autosave or a load, take_dirty is false, so edits made to the buffer are never persisted.
results.scenario: Record a take. The autosave finishes and clears take_dirty. Reverse or Normalize the crop, or Cut a section, then switch machines or reboot. tape_stop checks `tp.take_dirty && tp.len > 1`, which is false, so nothing is saved. tapelast still points at the pre-edit file. The user returns to the unedited take, and the header still shows the saved check. The same applies to edits on a loaded sample.
results.reasoning: tape_norm/reverse/fade/cut/paste (:669-754) never touch take_dirty, dirty_gen or restore_id. Since the 11.5 fix, save_task clears take_dirty after the autosave (:820-821), so tape_stop (:1035) skips the save and writes the pre-edit id to tapelast (:1040), and tape_restore_last reloads the unedited file while the header keeps its saved check (tape_menu.c:189). Before 11.5 a recorded take stayed dirty forever and its edits were saved on leave, so for recorded takes this is a side effect of that fix; for loaded samples it was always so (:653). Nothing in CLAUDE.md documents edits as session-only; the only way to keep them today is the Crop button.
results.fix_sketch: In each edit that actually changed the buffer set tp.take_dirty = true, bump tp.dirty_gen (so an in-flight save cannot mark it clean) and clear tp.restore_id[0] (drops the saved check). The existing tape_stop / tape_load_inner save path then persists the edited buffer as a new CUT_ take.

results.title: tape_snap divide by zero when the clock source is OFF
results.reasoning: tape_snap's only callers are in nudge() (tape_menu.c:629, :635), and nudge calls tape_beat_frames() first (tape_menu.c:620), which zeroes tp.disp_bpm when the source is OFF (tape.c:88-89), so disp_bpm is never stale at the guard. clock_core_set_src drops the lock and bpm in the same call (clock.c:328-331, cc_relock) and clockin_beat_bpm returns 0 when unlocked (clock.h:127), so both guard terms at tape.c:127 are 0 and the zero-cross branch runs. What remains is a web clk_src POST landing between two adjacent statements of the UI task, which is not a practical trigger; a `b == 0` fallthrough in tape_snap would still be a cheap hardening.

results.title: Crop Beats with clock source OFF collapses the crop to 64 frames
results.claim: tape_crop_beats() does not handle b==0 (clock source OFF). out becomes in_pt, and crop_clamp then forces a 64-frame window.
results.scenario: Set Setup > Clock Src to OFF, then turn the 'Crop Beats' row. tape_beat_frames returns 0, so out_pt = in_pt. crop_clamp sees in_pt >= out_pt and sets in_pt = out_pt-64, leaving a 64-frame (1.5 ms) loop. The user's crop is destroyed, and the loop chops or clicks at about 690 Hz.
results.reasoning: With Clock Src OFF tape_beat_frames returns 0 (:88-90); tape_crop_beats has no b==0 guard, so out_pt = in_pt (:760-761) and crop_clamp (:575) pulls in_pt back 64 frames (or leaves 0/0, which tape_eff_window widens to 64). The Setup row calls it on every detent with no transport or clock check (tape_menu.c:855-857), so it also fires while playing, turning the loop into a ~689 Hz buzz. Only the crop points are lost, not audio; tape_rec_stop_request guards the same value with `beat >= 64` (:216), so the missing guard here is an oversight. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Return early from tape_crop_beats() when tape_beat_frames() is 0 (same `beat >= 64` test tape_rec_stop_request uses), and have tape_val case 0 show 'no clock' in that state.

results.title: Momentary rec: tape-full with gate still held restarts a fresh take over the one just finished
results.claim: In MOMENTARY mode, when the tape fills while the gate is still held, tape_rec_stop() sets recording=false and playing=false. The very next block sees gate && !recording and calls tape_begin_fresh(), which wipes len and restarts a fresh take. The autosave for the take that just filled has only been queued.
results.scenario: Rec Mode = momentary. Hold TR2 past the tape capacity. At tape-full, tape_stash_and_save queues autosave_req and the transport stops. Next block, tape_begin_fresh resets len=0 and records over bank 0 while the writer spawns and reads the same banks. The saved CUT_ file is a blend or truncated, and the finished take is gone from the buffer.
results.reasoning: At tape-full (tape.c:514) tape_rec_stop() queues autosave_req and sets recording=false, then playing=false; the next block's momentary branch (400-402) sees gate && !recording && !playing and calls tape_begin_fresh(), which zeroes len and records from frame 0 with no release required. The writer is only spawned by tape_autosave_kick on the UI tick (300 ms fast / 1 s slow, tape_menu.c:719/738/1012), so up to ~13k frames are overwritten before save_busy is set and the drop_spoiled check at 560 cannot see them; after the spawn it does flag the file as a blend, but only as a log line. Result: the CUT_ file has the new audio at its head (not truncated, save_b stays at the old len), the buffer take is gone, and holding on repeats this every tape length. Not in the 09-16 review (11.6 is the rec_stop_target leftover at the same line, a different defect).
results.fix_sketch: Make the momentary punch-in need a fresh gate edge after a tape-full stop: set a latch in the tape-full branch at tape.c:514, test it in the `gate && !tp.recording` condition, and clear it when the gate is released (same shape as the existing tr2_recgest/tr2_armed handling). Clear rec_stop_target there too (11.6).

results.title: Crop adopt runs after a failed or short save: playback stops, or a truncated loop replaces the tape
results.claim: adopt_id is left set when save_task fails (fopen or alloc failure) or writes a short file. The kick then unconditionally sets playing=false before tape_load, and the load fails with -2 or -4 because the file is missing or invalid.
results.scenario: Press Crop while a loop plays and the card is full or the fopen fails. save_task clears save_busy but leaves adopt_id set, and drop_spoiled is false. tape_drop_adopt_kick then stops playback (line 901). tape_load fails, and the loop simply stops with only a log line. For a short write (card full), the truncated file is adopted and the tape is replaced by a partial loop.
results.reasoning: save_task's fopen/alloc failure path (782-787) and its short-write path (810-811, `ok` only gates take_dirty) leave adopt_id set and drop_spoiled false, so tape_drop_adopt_kick passes its only check (897), sets playing=false (901) and calls tape_load. With fopen failed, sample_resolve returns -2 and the loop just stops, resume not honoured, while the drop note stays green (tape_menu.c:462 only turns amber on drop_spoiled). With a short write the file is finalised at its truncated size, so tape_load_inner first writes the dirty take whole to the same full card (612, also short, and repoints tapelast), then overwrites the bank head with the partial loop and sets len and take_dirty=false (651-653). Not recorded on 09-16 (11.4 covers the load-back race, not save failure).
results.fix_sketch: Have save_task publish its result (a tp.save_ok flag, or clear tp.adopt_id on the fopen/alloc and !ok paths) and make tape_drop_adopt_kick return before `tp.playing = false` when the write failed, next to the existing drop_spoiled bail. On a tape_load failure restore `tp.playing = resume`, and let the drop note's amber `bad` state in tape_menu.c:462 cover a failed save as well.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Files read in full: machine_looper/looper.c, looper_menu.c, looper_web.c, looper_priv.h; machine_glitch/glitch.c, glitch_menu.c, glitch_priv.h. I did not open the machine_looper.h and machine_glitch.h wrappers or the CMakeLists.

Outside these files I only read what was needed: sd_lock.h, sampfile.c (sample_next_index, sampwav_*), svf.h, and cvmtx_abs. I did not read the activate()/stop ordering in machine.c or the audio task, so I did not confirm that process() cannot run after stop().

I did not read cvmtx.c beyond cvmtx_abs, so I did not check whether pos01 is clamped to 0..1. If it is not, vol, pan and cutoff could be out of range. I did not verify that writeJSONFile takes sd_lock internally; it appears to, at util/fileio.c:225.

I did not chase the float-to-int paths in the SVF (a NaN bp cast to int).

I dropped nothing for the 15-finding cap.

results.title: looper_save_track writes the WAV with no sd_lock
results.claim: looper_save_track does all its SD I/O (mkdir, fopen, every 512-frame fwrite, sampwav_finish's fseek/fwrite, fclose) without ever taking sd_lock. Only the readdir inside sample_next_index and writeJSONFile lock. The sd_lock.h rule requires the lock around every I/O burst.
results.scenario: The user presses Save Trk, or POSTs /looper/save. A ~2.8 MB WAV is written in 512-frame bursts on the same SD bus that the sampler/tape reader tasks, REST file serving and recording use. Those paths use raw f_read/f_lseek that bypass the VFS lock, so the bursts can interleave. This is the race sd_lock.h says can wedge the bus and corrupt the FAT or directory, or give noisy reads.
results.reasoning: machine_looper never includes or takes sd_lock: mkdir (309), fopen (316), sampwav_start, every fwrite (333), sampwav_finish and fclose (337-338) run unlocked; only sample_next_index and writeJSONFile lock internally. CLAUDE.md says every SD burst must hold it, and the sibling Tape save does (tape.c:778-808). No reader task runs under Looper, so the collision needs other SD traffic during the save: a web upload or /files listing (raw f_open/f_opendir in httpd, rest-api.c:227/1389) during a panel save, or the /bounce recording writer or import task during either. I did not trace actual corruption (FatFS has FF_FS_REENTRANT=1); the rule violation itself is certain. Max file is 1.4 MB, not 2.8 MB.
results.fix_sketch: Mirror tape.c:778-808: sd_lock_take/give around mkdir+fopen+sampwav_start, around each 512-frame fwrite, and around sampwav_finish+fclose. Check the fwrite return while there (card full currently reports SAVED).

results.title: Save reads a track buffer the audio task can re-record during the write
results.claim: looper_save_track reads t->buf for many seconds while the audio task can still change that track. len is captured once and the state is never checked again. Re-arming a STOP track sets len=0 and starts recording over the buffer; punch, clear and TR triggers also act on the track mid-save.
results.scenario: The user POSTs /looper/save?trk=1 on a STOPPED or PLAYING track, or presses Save in the menu. While the write runs, TR1 or the encoder press re-arms and records on that track, and the audio task overwrites t->buf[0..]. The saved WAV holds the old loop head and then new live audio, and the sidecar still reports the old length.
results.reasoning: len is captured once at line 326 and state is never rechecked through the multi-second write. The panel save blocks the UI task, but TR1 is handled in the audio task (looper.c:158 -> apply_cmd): a TR1 edge on a STOP track (or two on a PLAY track) re-arms and records over buf[0..]; a web save of trk=N is also open to panel encoder presses. Reads stay in bounds (captured len <= LP_BUF_FRAMES), so no crash; the saved WAV is old loop plus new input. The sidecar carries no length, so that part of the claim is wrong; cmd_clear is never set anywhere.
results.fix_sketch: Add one volatile per-track busy flag in lp_state_t that apply_cmd and the TR handlers honour (ignore action on a track being saved or bounced); save sets it, calls machine_block_wait(), writes, clears. Alternatively recheck t->len/state per chunk and abort + remove() the partial file, returning the existing -2 'STOP REC' style code.

results.title: Panel and web saves can pick the same LOOPnnnn index
results.claim: The save number comes from a directory scan and the file is only created later. The UI-task Save row and the web /looper/save worker do not exclude each other: s_sv_done only guards web against web.
results.scenario: A web save is running on the lp_save worker. The user presses Save Trk on the panel, or a second save starts before the first has created its file. Both calls compute the same LOOPnnnn index and fopen("wb") the same path. The two writers interleave or truncate each other, giving a garbled WAV and a JSN describing the wrong track.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 11.8, placed on the Watch list. The code is unchanged: s_sv_done (looper_web.c:20) only guards web against web, and the UI-task Save row calls looper_save_track directly. The window is only between one caller's readdir pass and its fopen (milliseconds), since a created file is seen by the next scan, so the watch rating still holds.

results.title: Bounce re-reads volatile len between the zero check and the modulo
