results.claim: looper_bounce re-reads the volatile t->len on every sample. The check t->len == 0 just above can go stale: the audio task on the other core applies cmd_clear, which sets len=0, or a re-arm from STOP, which also sets len=0, during the roughly second-long bounce loop.
results.scenario: During the long bounce loop (up to 8 s x 4 tracks of float SVF), a TR1 gate re-arms a STOP track, or a cmd_clear lands. len becomes 0 between the check and the modulo, so j % 0 raises an integer divide-by-zero exception and panics the chip. Even without that timing, a re-arm makes the audio task start recording over a buffer the bounce is reading.
results.reasoning: lp_track_t.len is volatile (looper_priv.h:26), so line 400's t->len==0 test and line 401's j % t->len are two separate loads. The bounce blocks the UI task, but a TR1 edge is handled in the audio task: on a selected STOP track apply_cmd sets len=0 (looper.c:131, or :52). If that lands between the two loads the remainder traps (IntegerDivideByZero panic); the window is a few instructions per iteration over up to 352800x4 iterations. cmd_clear is dead code (no writer), so only the TR1 re-arm path is real; TR1 is a button unless it is the clock source (core default is CV4).
results.fix_sketch: Snapshot each contributing track's len (and eligibility) into locals in the gather loop at 380-386 and use only the snapshots in the mix loop. Better, share the busy flag from #1 so apply_cmd/TR ignore actions for the duration, which also stops a re-arm recording over a source being read.

results.title: TR1 on empty track 1 during the bounce swap records under the memcpy
results.claim: The bounce swap-in sets all lanes to LP_EMPTY and waits one tick, but the audio task keeps running apply_cmd and TR handling. A pending cmd_action or a TR1 edge on the now-EMPTY track 0 starts a record into d->buf while the memcpy is writing it. The function then forces state=LP_PLAY, over the state the audio task set.
results.scenario: A TR1 pulse arrives, or the user pressed the encoder just before pressing Bounce. Track 0 is EMPTY during the swap, so it arms or records at once. The audio task writes live input into d->buf[0..] while the memcpy writes the bounce, and the result is a bounced loop with live audio mixed into its head. The record state is then overwritten.
results.reasoning: Between lines 417 and 430 (one 10 ms tick plus a PSRAM memcpy of up to 700 KB) track 0 is LP_EMPTY and nothing stops the audio task acting on it. With lp.sel==0 and sync off or unlocked, a TR1 edge goes EMPTY -> track_start_record and writes live input at buf[0..] while memcpy writes the same buffer; line 430 then forces LP_PLAY. Result is a few ms of live input at the head of the bounced loop (a click) and a dropped TR1 action; with sync locked it only arms and is overwritten harmlessly. A pending encoder cmd_action is not realistic (consumed within one block before the UI reaches Bounce). Window is ~10-40 ms, so low severity.
results.fix_sketch: Same busy flag as #1/#3 held across the swap so apply_cmd and the TR handler ignore actions, and replace the vTaskDelay(1) at line 420 with machine_block_wait() (the 09-16 convention) before the memcpy.

results.title: Lane thumbnail stays stale after a same-length bounce
results.reasoning: looper_bounce is only called from the Setup page action (looper_menu.c:389), and lanes are never drawn there. Lanes are drawn only on Live and the main screen, and both call lanes_reset_cache() on EV_ENTERED_MENU (looper_menu.c:278 via live_full_redraw, and :433), which zeroes s_wf_for[] so wf_build runs again for every track. The user cannot see a lane after a bounce without passing through one of those resets.

results.title: looper_stop leaks the four track slabs when the web save wait times out
results.claim: When the wait for the web save times out, stop() returns without freeing. The pointers stay in lp.tr[] and the next looper_start memsets lp, which drops them, so four 700 KB PSRAM slabs are permanently lost. Meanwhile the worker keeps reading the buffers (safe, but they are never freed).
results.scenario: The user switches machine while a slow /looper/save is still running. That is possible on a card under load, and the handler's own wait is 30 s while the stop wait is only 10 s. After the save ends and the looper is started again, about 2.8 MB of PSRAM is unreachable for the rest of uptime.
results.reasoning: This is the deliberate outcome of the 09-16 fix for 11.7 (theme B: on timeout 'the caller leaks, never frees'; 'Looper: stop waits for a web save'), and the log line says so. It needs a single-track save (max 1.4 MB) to take over 10 s, i.e. a badly stalled card. Only addition: the leak could be reclaimed cheaply, since looper_start already refuses while the save runs (line 72) and could free any non-NULL lp.tr[i].buf before its memset.

results.title: glitch_start leaks one slab when only one of two PSRAM allocs succeeds
results.claim: If exactly one of the two PSRAM allocations succeeds, start returns an error without freeing the other. The looper comments confirm that activate() does not call stop() on a failed start, and the next start memsets gl and drops the pointer.
results.scenario: PSRAM is fragmented or low. The 352 KB ring allocates but the 88 KB window fails, or the reverse. The machine fails to start, the slab stays allocated, and repeated attempts leak it each time.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 12.5, left on the Watch list (its Looper twin 11.9 was fixed, this one was not). The code is unchanged: line 57 returns without freeing, machine_activate falls back to Stub without calling stop (machine_core.c:72-84), and the next start's memset at line 54 drops the pointer. It needs PSRAM exhaustion, so the watch rating still holds.

results.title: Glitch ring is never zeroed; an early stutter loops uninitialised PSRAM
results.claim: The ring is heap_caps_malloc'd and never zeroed, and wpos starts at 0. capture_window copies the last wl frames ending at wpos, which wrap into the not-yet-written tail of the ring.
results.scenario: Glitch is selected. Within the first 2 s the user holds TR1 or latches TR2. The captured window includes uninitialised PSRAM, which holds leftover data from a previous machine (audio, code or random). It loops at full level, so the output is a burst of noise or stale audio.
results.reasoning: glitch_start (line 55) allocates the ring with heap_caps_malloc and never clears it, and wpos starts at 0 after the memset. capture_window (36-41) wraps to the unwritten tail whenever wpos < wl, and nothing tracks how much has been written. The exposure is the first win_ms after start (120 ms default, 500 ms max), not 2 s as the finder said. But `want` (line 111) is level-based, so a gate already low on TR1 when Glitch starts or boots captures a fully uninitialised window on the first block and loops it at level 255 until released. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Allocate gl.ring with heap_caps_calloc(..., MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM) in glitch_start (start runs on the UI task, so a 706 KB clear is fine). gl.win needs no clear: it is always written up to win_len before it is read.

results.title: Glitch preset division (and win_ms) loaded without a range check
results.claim: division is loaded from the preset without clamping. window_frames uses it as a shift count, and the menu's div_name and Setup cycle assume 0..3. win_ms is also unclamped, at line 165.
results.scenario: A preset or hand-edited CONFIG.JSN has division=-1 or 40. `1u << gl.division` is undefined behaviour (in practice a wrapped shift count), so the synced window length is wrong (for example 1/2^8 of a beat, or shifted by a negative count). Setup shows 1/32, and the first encoder step jumps back to 0 or 3 (Setup's wrap tests are `< 0` and `> 3`), so the bad value silently sticks until adjusted.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 12.6, triaged under Watch (low consequence), and the code is unchanged. The reason still holds: capture_window clamps wl to 64..GL_MAX_WIN (glitch.c:32-33), so a bad shift count or an out-of-range win_ms (line 165) only gives a wrong but bounded window length. `1u << n` cannot be zero on Xtensa, so there is no divide-by-zero. gl_adj (glitch_menu.c:118) wraps the value back to 0..3 on the first encoder step.

results.title: Looper preset bars loaded unclamped; bar_frames can wrap in uint32
results.claim: bars is loaded unclamped. bar_frames multiplies period*4*ppb*bars in uint32 and can wrap. Setup only steps 1,2,4,8.
results.scenario: A preset has bars=100000000. bar_frames wraps to a small non-zero value. Synced recording then auto-stops after a tiny or arbitrary number of frames, so loops are cut wrongly with no error. bars=3 or 5 is also accepted and shows in Setup as an unreachable value.
results.reasoning: looper_preset_load takes any int, and bar_frames (line 46) multiplies period*4*ppb*bars in uint32, so a huge value wraps. Severity is lower than claimed: track_start_record (line 55) caps target at LP_BUF_FRAMES, so there is no overrun, and a wrapped product almost always lands above the cap and records to buffer-full, like any over-long setting. The wrap needs bars above roughly 48,000 at 120 BPM / PPQ 4, which only a hand-edited AUTOSAVE.JSN or a crafted /remote/params post gives; bars=3 or 5 simply records 3 or 5 bars. Not recorded on 09-16; it is the same class as the Watch item 12.6.
results.fix_sketch: Clamp in looper_preset_load to 1..8 (optionally snap to 1/2/4/8, which is what the Setup row at looper_menu.c:371-372 steps through).

results.title: looper_save_track ignores write errors and reports SAVED for a truncated loop
results.claim: looper_save_track ignores the fwrite return, sampwav_finish and fclose results, and returns 0 (menu shows SAVED) even if the card is full. writeJSONFile is also unchecked, so there can be a WAV with no sidecar.
results.scenario: The SD card is full or write-protected mid-save. fwrite short-writes, the header is patched to the truncated size, the function returns 0, and the UI or web reports success although the loop is truncated or the sidecar is missing.
results.reasoning: The fwrite at 333, sampwav_start (318), sampwav_finish (337) and fclose (338) results are all dropped and the function returns 0 unconditionally (360). The menu then shows SAVED (looper_menu.c:387) and /looper/save returns 200 (looper_web.c:66-78). On a full card sampwav_finish patches the header to the truncated size, so the file probes as a valid shorter WAV; writeJSONFile is void (fileio.c:311), so a missing sidecar is also silent. The e327f6f fix for 6.8/13.8 covered Editor, upload and Freesound but not this writer; the looper save was not a 09-16 finding. The function also does its fopen/fwrite/fclose without sd_lock.
results.fix_sketch: Follow the Editor pattern from e327f6f (editor.c:99, 283): set an io_err flag when fwrite != nfr or sampwav_start/sampwav_finish/fclose fail, break out of the loop, remove() the partial file and return a distinct negative code. Show FAILED instead of EMPTY on the menu row for that code; the web handler already reports any non-zero rc. Wrap the write bursts in sd_lock_take/give while there.

results.title: Radio never checks HTTP status; any body bytes reset the retry counter, so 30x/404 reconnects forever
results.claim: The HTTP status code is never checked, and `attempts` is reset to 0 whenever any body bytes arrive (line 308). A 301/302/404/403 response with a small HTML body is fed to the decoder as if it were audio. The retry counter then never reaches its limit.
results.scenario: The user picks a station URL that answers with a redirect or an error page, for example http://host/stream returning 302 with a short body. esp_http_client_open() does not follow redirects, so the task reads the body (r>0, attempts=0), sees the close, and reconnects after 0.8 s. Each pass resets attempts, so `++attempts > 8` is never true and set_err() is never called. The machine sits in BUFFERING forever with no error text. It reconnects about once a second and burns one of the ~10 lwIP sockets each time, until the user presses stop.
results.reasoning: No status check follows esp_http_client_fetch_headers (297), and the open/read API in IDF 4.3 does not follow redirects. A 30x/404 with a small body gives r>0 once, so attempts=0 (308); the next read returns 0, attempts becomes 1, and the task reconnects after 0.8 s. `++attempts > 8` (347) is never reached, so state stays BUFFERING with no error text until the user stops. The socket-burn part of the claim is wrong: each pass runs close+cleanup (340-341), so nothing leaks; an empty-body redirect does end in 'stream lost'.
results.fix_sketch: After fetch_headers read esp_http_client_get_status_code(cl) (as fs_machine.c:106 does): on 301/302/307 call esp_http_client_set_redirection(cl) and reopen, on any other non-200 call set_err("HTTP %d") and break. Move `attempts = 0` from line 308 to the MP3Decode err==0 branch so only decoded audio resets the backoff.

results.title: Radio rd.sel can exceed rd_n_stations (preset clamp uses RADIO_MAX_ST; delete never adjusts sel)
results.claim: The preset `sel` is clamped to RADIO_MAX_ST (24), not to rd_n_stations. radio_play_station() silently ignores idx >= rd_n_stations. radio_station_del() also never adjusts rd.sel.
results.scenario: The user saves a favourite (index 6 or higher) and selects it, so autosave stores sel=7. The favourite is then deleted through /radio/station/del, or usr/radio.jsn is missing after a card swap. On the next start rd.sel=7 while rd_n_stations=6. The Live page shows rd_stations[7 % 6], which is a different station, but pressing to play calls radio_play_station(7), which returns without doing anything. Nothing happens and no error is shown until the user turns the encoder.
results.reasoning: preset_load runs at bind, after radio_start has loaded the stations (menu.c:912-916), yet it clamps sel to RADIO_MAX_ST (24), not rd_n_stations. radio_station_del (87-94) leaves rd.sel alone. With sel >= rd_n_stations the Live page shows rd_stations[sel % n] (radio_menu.c:67), but a press calls radio_play_station(sel), which returns silently at radio.c:405. Easiest trigger: play the last favourite, stop, delete it from the web.
results.fix_sketch: In radio_preset_load clamp against rd_n_stations (already loaded by radio_start). In radio_station_del decrement rd.sel when idx < rd.sel and reset it to 0 when rd.sel >= rd_n_stations.

results.title: Tracker browser truncates module names over 39 chars into entries that cannot be opened
results.claim: With long filenames enabled, module names over 39 characters are truncated in the browser list. The extension is lost and the truncated string is later used as the file name. TRK_NAME_LEN is 40, while a card copied from a Mac can hold names up to 255 characters.
results.scenario: A card holds 'My Long Song Name Remix Version 2 final.xm' (over 39 characters). has_mod_ext() accepts it on the full name. The list stores the first 39 characters, without '.xm'. Selecting it calls tracker_request_load() with the truncated name, and fopen fails with 'open failed'. Two long names sharing the first 39 characters collapse into one entry. The module cannot be loaded from the panel, and if the truncated name is saved as trk.file it fails again on every boot.
results.reasoning: has_mod_ext tests the full d_name, then lines 68-70 cut it to 39 chars; tracker_request_load passes that to fopen and load_file_psram fails with 'open failed' (131). sdkconfig has CONFIG_FATFS_MAX_LFN=64, so the affected range is 40-64 chars, not 255; longer names arrive as 8.3 aliases and load. Only card-copied files hit it, since /trk/upload clamps names to 8 chars (rest-api.c:2052). The 09-16 'Checked OK: Tracker filenames 40 chars' note covered 24-char leftovers only, not this truncation.
results.fix_sketch: In tracker_list_modules skip names that do not fit (`if (L > TRK_NAME_LEN - 1) continue;`), the refuse-not-truncate rule drop_sample already uses. Alternative: raise TRK_NAME_LEN to FATFS_MAX_LFN+1, move s_list to PSRAM and widen path[80] in load_file_psram.

results.title: radio_play_url zeroes ring counters while process() is still draining (state PLAYING)
results.claim: radio_play_url() zeroes the ring counters from the httpd or UI task while rd.state is still RADIO_PLAYING (state is only set to BUFFERING at line 394). process() in the audio task keeps doing rd.rpos++ in that window, so a lost update can leave rpos above wpos.
results.scenario: A station change happens while the old station is playing. The audio task has read rpos=N and passed `rd.rpos < rd.wpos`. On the other core, radio_play_url writes wpos=rpos=0. The audio task then stores rpos=N+1. Now wpos-rpos wraps to about 4 billion. The new stream task's ring_write sees the ring as full (`>= RADIO_RING_FRAMES-2`) and spins in vTaskDelay forever, and process() outputs silence. The machine is wedged in BUFFERING until the user hits stop. The window is tiny but exists on every station change. Setting state=BUFFERING before the reset would close it.
results.reasoning: The web calls /radio/play while playing with no stop first (index.html:2776). Line 387 zeroes rpos/wpos while state is still PLAYING (BUFFERING is set at 394), so a process() iteration that passed `rpos < wpos` (452) stores rpos++ (456) after the zeroing, leaving rpos >= 1 and wpos = 0. ring_write (121) then sees wpos-rpos as ~4e9 and sleeps in vTaskDelay until s_stop, so the machine sits in BUFFERING until the user stops. Not established: the hit rate; the window is the ~32-frame drain loop out of each 1.45 ms block, my estimate well under 1% per station change. It is a stuck stream, not a system hang: stop/play recovers.
results.fix_sketch: In radio_play_url set rd.state = RADIO_BUFFERING first, call machine_block_wait() (machine.h), then zero wpos/rpos.

results.title: xmp_start_player() return ignored; a failed start still publishes TRK_READY
results.claim: The return value of xmp_start_player() is ignored. If it fails (mixer or voice allocation), do_load() still publishes TRK_READY, sets s_have_module and turns playing on.
results.scenario: Internal RAM is fragmented after a large load, and xmp_start_player returns a negative error. The UI shows the title and READY. xmp_play_buffer then returns an error (-XMP_ERROR_STATE), which the render loop treats as 'module ended' (`if (r < 0) trk.playing = false`). The module silently stops right after loading, with no FAIL and no reason shown.
results.reasoning: The return is ignored; on failure libxmp stays in LOADED, xmp_play_buffer returns -XMP_ERROR_STATE (player.c:2194) and line 537 reads that as 'module ended', so the track shows READY and silently stops. No crash: xmp_get_frame_info guards xc_data (player.c:2341). Not established: a way for start to fail. libxmp allocations are PSRAM-first with internal fallback (libxmp/xmp_mem.c), not internal as the finder says, and the module file buffer was freed just before (196), so PSRAM has at least that much free.
results.fix_sketch: Check the return: on < 0 call xmp_release_module(s_ctx), snprintf trk.fail_why "start err %d", set trk.state = TRK_FAIL and return, the same shape as the load-error branch at 197-201.

results.title: Order-step map stops at the first skip marker, so S3M/IT orders after '+++' are unmapped
results.claim: The order-step map stops at the first '+++' (skip) marker. IT and S3M files can have skip markers in the middle of the order list, so all later orders are unmapped (n_orders and total_steps come out too short). fi.pos for those later orders is >= n_orders.
results.scenario: An IT module has orders 0-9, a '+++' at order 10, and orders 11-20. While playing order 12, loop mode computes `cur_abs = (fi.pos < n_orders) ? ... : 0`, which gives 0. Then `cur_abs < lstart` is true on every row boundary, so the render task repeatedly calls xmp_set_row/xmp_set_position. The play bar and the loop window are wrong for the whole later part of the song, and scrub/nudge cannot reach it.
results.reasoning: The loaders keep 0xFE in xxo, and libxmp steps over skip markers and ends only on 0xFF (scan.c:181-205, control.c:90-97), so playback continues past a '+++' that line 240 treats as the end. Beyond it fi.pos >= n_orders: engaging the loop gives loop_anchor_abs 0 (342-343) and the first resync jumps to order 0 row 0; CV6 cannot reach the later part; nudges are dropped (569). The finder overstated two details: the relocation happens once, not on every row, and scrub still works because it uses num_pat = mod->len (tracker_menu.c:353). The play bar falls back to time.
results.fix_sketch: Break only on XMP_MARK_END. For XMP_MARK_SKIP (or pat >= m->pat) record order_rows[o]=0, order_step0[o]=acc, count the order and continue; abs_to_or and the seek code already tolerate zero-row orders.

results.title: xmp_create_context() NULL result unchecked in render_task
results.claim: The result of xmp_create_context() is not checked for NULL. Every later xmp_* call (do_load, apply_sound_mode, xmp_play_buffer) dereferences it.
results.scenario: Internal RAM is tight when the tracker starts (the code already documents this with the trimmed-stack fallback). The render task spawns, but xmp_create_context() returns NULL. The first load_req calls xmp_load_module_from_memory(NULL, ...) and the task crashes with a NULL dereference, which reboots the module. It should set TRK_FAIL and exit instead.
results.reasoning: xmp_create_context returns NULL on calloc failure (libxmp/src/control.c:36-39) and s_ctx is never checked. A NULL s_ctx is dereferenced by xmp_free_context (reads ctx->state) at line 604 on every tracker_stop, and by xmp_load_module_from_memory (load.c:427) on a load. The finder's trigger is off: the calloc is PSRAM-first with internal fallback (xmp_mem.c), so it needs PSRAM nearly empty right after the 352 KB ring allocation and no internal block big enough. In that state the file-buffer alloc usually fails first, so the certain crash is on leaving Tracker.
results.fix_sketch: On NULL set trk.fail_why ("no RAM for player") and trk.state = TRK_FAIL, then stay in the s_rd.run loop answering load_req with TRK_FAIL so worker_stop still works. Guard the xmp_free_context call at exit with `if (s_ctx)`.

chunks.coverage_notes:
I read every line of these files in full: components/machine_synth/synth.c, synth_menu.c and synth_priv.h, and components/machine_granular/granular.c, granular_menu.c and granular_priv.h. I did not open the include/machine_synth.h and machine_granular.h headers, which are one-line public headers. I also read the related code in components/machine/machine_core.c (machine_block_wait, machine_activate), util/lfo.c, util/svf.{h,c}, util/preset_store.c, util/sample_ram.c (sample_load), sampfile.c (sample_resolve) and the cvmtx.h API. I did not read the bodies of cvmtx.c, fxrack, reverb, flanger or fxdelay, or the sample_browser internals, so bugs inside them are not covered.

Things I checked and found safe:
- Grain pool indexing, window LUT indexing, gr_cubic bounds, and the maxp/glen clamps.
- The wavetable read path (wl is read once and clamped, and sample_load is capped at SY_WT_MAX).
- The block-handshake ordering for load, and for stop()/machine_activate.
- Preset and remote loads run on the UI task, so the httpd-vs-stop race does not arise.
- The LFO div and shape indices are clamped inside lfo.c.
- The name and string buffers (wave_name[SAMPLE_ID_LEN], htag[28], the granular info line s[96]).

Dropped as too minor: the preset_store id truncation to 11 characters for long file names (that file is in the util area, and the failure is only a silent load failure), and preset_store_save clamping the index at 999 (unrealistic).

No crash-class or use-after-free findings survived in scope."}

results.title: Granular preset load takes density unclamped; spawn loop has no per-sample cap
results.claim: gr.density is loaded from preset JSON with no clamp (line 255: gr.density = j->valueint), and the spawn loop runs once per whole grain owed, with no cap.
results.scenario: A preset or POST /remote/params with density around 1e8 to 2e9 (cJSON saturates valueint to INT_MAX), or the same value in AUTOSAVE.JSN, gives spawn_per_sample of thousands. That is tens of thousands of spawn_grain() calls per sample in the audio task, so the block overruns and the task watchdog fires. If the value is persisted in AUTOSAVE.JSN it re-triggers on every boot with Granular active, until the card is edited. A negative density (also accepted) sends spawn_phase steadily negative, so after the value is fixed no grains spawn for a long time.
results.reasoning: granular_preset_load (granular.c:254-257) stores valueint with no range check, while the panel clamps density to 1..120 (granular_menu.c:133); the web machine form is a free number input (index.html:1737) that reaches it via POST /remote/params -> EV_REMOTE_PRESET -> preset_load, then autosaves. At INT_MAX that is ~48,700 spawn_grain() calls per sample (~1.5M per block, with soft-double math), so the audio task (prio 23, pinned core 1) effectively stops producing blocks; roughly 1e6 and up already overruns the 1.45 ms budget. The finder's watchdog claim is wrong: idle-task WDT checks and WDT panic are off (sdkconfig:417-420), so there is no reset, just dead audio that returns on every boot until K8 or the Setup Density row (which re-clamps) is touched. Negative density is also accepted and drives spawn_phase negative; a large one sticks through float absorption until the machine restarts.
results.prior_ref: 12.6 (same class in Glitch, Watch; Granular not recorded)
results.fix_sketch: Clamp in granular_preset_load to the ranges granular_menu.c:132-135 already uses (grain_ms 10..500, density 1..120, spray/spread 0..100). In process(), floor spawn_phase at 0 so a bad value cannot leave a standing deficit.

results.title: Synth preset load leaves sus/shape/fmr unclamped; hot clipped voice and stray Live drawing
results.claim: synth_preset_load does not clamp several parameters that the UI does clamp: sus, atk/dec/rel, shape (line 337), fmr (line 333), fmi, gld and e2c. The process() clamps only some of them, and the Live drawing code clamps none.
results.scenario: (a) A preset with sus=5 gives dec_inc<0, and ENV_DEC immediately sets env=5, so the voice is 5x hot into the hard int16 clamp. In draw_adsr, ys = yb - sus*(h-4) is far outside the cleared rect, so the ADSR polyline is drawn over other screen areas and leaves stale pixels. (b) shape=50 makes draw_osc compute yv=(1-50)*saw+50*sq, so py is hundreds of pixels off and vertical lines are drawn far outside the strip. process() clamps shape_eff, so the audio is fine but the display is corrupted. (c) fmr=1e999 parses to inf, so mdt=inf and sy.mphase becomes inf permanently. sinf(inf)=NaN gives NaN osc every block, and the SVF reset guard only recovers one block at a time, so the voice stays silent until fm_ratio is edited. All of this is reachable through POST /remote/params, a patch file, or AUTOSAVE.JSN.
results.reasoning: synth_preset_load clamps only cut/res/fold (synth.c:353-364); sus, shape, fmr, atk/dec/rel, gld are stored raw, and the web form offers them as free number inputs showing raw 0..1 values the panel displays as percent (typing 50 for shape is a plausible slip). sus=5: dec_inc is negative and ENV_DEC at synth.c:228 sets env=5 on the first sample, so the voice hits the int16 hard clamp at 5x (negative sus inverts the envelope); draw_adsr (synth_menu.c:256) puts ys ~180 px above its cleared rect, drawing over the dials and osc strip. shape=50: process() clamps shape_eff so audio is fine, but draw_osc (synth_menu.c:133-141) computes py ~+-700 px and the TFT library clips only to dispWin, giving full-height vertical lines left as stale pixels. The fmr=inf case needs a crafted non-finite JSON number and is worse than stated: sy.mphase stays inf after fm_ratio is corrected, until Synth restarts; fmi/e2c/lvl/lfo_div are already clamped at use.
results.prior_ref: 12.6 (same class in Glitch, Watch; Synth not recorded)
results.fix_sketch: Clamp in synth_preset_load with the ranges the Setup rows already use (synth_menu.c:595-603: shape 0..1, fmr 0.25..16, fmi 0..12, atk/dec 0.0005..2, sus 0..1, rel ..3, e2c 0..1, gld 0..2), the same way cut/res/fold are clamped a few lines below, and reject non-finite values.

results.title: sample_resolve() stat probes run without sd_lock (shared resolver, most callers unlocked)
results.claim: sample_resolve() runs a stat() probe loop over every folder and extension on the SD card without holding sd_lock. sample_load() calls it before its first sd_lock_take(), and both granular_load and synth_load_wave go through sample_load.
results.scenario: Loading a wave in Synth or a sample in Granular (UI task) issues up to about 7 dirs x N exts VFS stat calls on the FAT volume. If the SD reader tasks are streaming at the same time (raw FatFS reads under sd_lock, or REST file serving), the unlocked stat races them. CLAUDE.md says all SD I/O must hold sd_lock, because the raw audio path bypasses the VFS lock and can wedge or corrupt the card.
results.reasoning: True as code: up to 28 stat() calls with no sd_lock, and sample_load calls it before its first sd_lock_take (sample_ram.c:112-113); only rest-api.c:448-450 wraps it. Corruption is overstated: vfs_fat_stat takes the esp_vfs_fat ctx lock and FatFS is built FF_FS_REENTRANT=1, so each call is serialised at volume level, and the sd_lock origin commit 48e69a7 says the symptom was audio noise, never on-disk damage. In the stated Synth/Granular scenario no raw-FatFS streaming reader is running (RAM machines), and the concurrent users (httpd, rec_writer) are VFS, so I could not establish any harm there; the exposure is the same line reached from httpd while a streaming machine plays, which is the class recorded as 6.12 (Low, Watch). What is missing is evidence that a VFS stat interleaving inside a raw reader's locked burst does more than add latency.
results.fix_sketch: Take and give sd_lock around each stat() inside sample_resolve, per probe as sample_next_index does per readdir, so all callers comply at once; the mutex is recursive, so rest-api.c:448 which already holds it is unaffected.

results.title: WT engine with no wave loaded plays the VA oscillator
results.reasoning: The code does fall through to VA, but WT-with-no-wave is a designed state, not a missed error path: the panel lets the engine be cycled to WT with nothing loaded (synth_menu.c:391-393, :592) and the header has a dedicated red engine tag for exactly this condition (synth_menu.c:94). Sound-plus-indicator instead of silence is a design choice, and 09-16 finding 12.2 treated this fallback as the visible symptom and fixed its cause (wave_name is now SAMPLE_ID_LEN, synth_priv.h:56). No state is corrupted and the preset keeps eng=2.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Files read in full: machine_freesound/fs_machine.c, fs_menu.c, fs_web.c, fs_auth.c, fs_auth.h, fs_priv.h; machine_editor/editor.c, editor_menu.c, editor_web.c, editor_priv.h. I did not open machine_freesound.h or machine_editor.h, or the two CMakeLists. To confirm paths I also read util/sampplay.c and sampplay.h, sampfile.c (resolve and next_index), sampfile_int.h (sf_parse), sampimport.c (samp_import_file and imp_publish), machine_core.c (activate, block_wait), wave_edit.c and .h, and parts of fileio.c and wifi.c.

Checked and found safe: the SAMPLE_ID_LEN buffers in fs_pool_name, fs_safe_name, the pipeline paths and the sidecar buffers; the machine-switch stop() handshake (machine_activate detaches before stop); and the double f_close on a FIL, which FatFS rejects harmlessly.

Dropped, all borderline: PSRAM-source f_write bounce-buffer pressure; the sampplay in_pt/out_pt non-atomic update in util (transient only); the clipboard staying 'full' after a failed copy; Editor Trim discarding material outside a selected range; and fs_query_remember/UI races on the recents arrays (benign). CJ_SLICE does not write the .OT sidecar its comment promises; that is a missing feature, not a bug, so I did not report it. I did not verify whether IDF 4.3's esp_http_client follows redirects on open/fetch_headers for direct-URL imports.

results.title: Editor job_task leaks the source FILE when the file probes OK with zero frames
results.claim: When the source opens and probes OK but reports zero frames, job_task jumps to `done`, which skips `close_src`. The FILE* is never closed. clip_task has the same pattern at line 483.
results.scenario: sf_parse returns 0 with frames == 0 for a header-only 44-byte WAV (an aborted recording, since a zero data size self-heals to fsize-52 = 0) and for any RAW under 4 bytes. POST /edit/apply?name=<that id>&op=0 skips editor_probe, so the job opens the file, probes rc 0 with 0 frames, and leaks a VFS FILE and fd on every attempt. The FatFS/VFS open-file table is small, so a few repeats stop every other fopen on the card (recording, uploads, loaders) from working. The panel path is guarded by editor_load's F==0 check, but the web path and copy/cut/paste/slice on an already-loaded file are not.
results.reasoning: open_src() returns an open FILE when sampfile_probe returns 0, and sf_parse does return 0 with frames==0 for a 44-byte WAV (sampfile_int.h:66-73) or a RAW under 4 bytes; line 210 then jumps to `done`, past the fclose at close_src. editor_apply (web /edit/apply, editor_web.c:42) never probes, and /files lists such takes; the Editor's own default-range Cut writes a 44-byte CR_ WAV (13.9, still present). Each attempt pins one of the 10 VFS fds (components/drivers/storage.c:32), so after at most 10 repeats every fopen on the card fails until reboot, and the file stays FatFS-locked. Not recorded on 09-16 (13.9 is only the junk file).
results.fix_sketch: Send the `sf.frames == 0` case to close_src when src is non-NULL, the way scan_task (editor.c:369) and sampplay_open (sampplay.c:158-160) already close on zero frames. Optionally have editor_apply reject a name whose editor_probe() returns 0.

results.title: Editor clip_task leaks the source FILE on a zero-frame source
results.claim: Same leak in clip_task. A zero-frame source jumps to `done` past `close_src`, so `fclose(src)` never runs.
results.scenario: Copy, Cut, Paste or Slice on a source whose file has become zero-frame (truncated or replaced while loaded) leaks the FILE and fd on each press.
results.reasoning: Same pattern as job_task: open_src succeeds with frames==0, line 483 jumps to `done` and skips fclose(src) at close_src (546-549). start_clip only checks ed.src[0]; editor_load guards F==0 for the panel, but a web /edit/apply sets ed.src to any name without probing (editor.c:304), after which panel Copy/Cut/Paste/Slice each leak one VFS fd. Same defect as finding #0 at a second site; not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: Same fix as job_task: when src is non-NULL and frames is 0, set the error and goto close_src instead of done. One shared open-or-fail helper in open_src (close and return NULL on zero frames, as sampplay_open does) fixes both sites.

results.title: Setup > Drop Last deletes an existing pool sample after a failed or colliding /fs/fetch
results.claim: Setup > Drop Last auditions and then deletes whatever pool sample is named `fsm.cur_name`. `cur_name` is set at start_job even when the job FAILED. /fs/fetch only sanitises the name (fs_safe_name) and never checks for a collision.
results.scenario: The user has KICK.WAV in the pool. POST /fs/fetch?url=...&name=KICK downloads usr/KICK.mp3, and samp_import_file refuses to overwrite the existing KICK.WAV (imp_publish 'exists'), so the job ends FS_ERROR 'convert failed' with cur_name = "KICK". The user then opens Setup, where the Drop Last row shows KICK, and presses it. fs_audition("KICK") opens the user's real sample and fs_audition_drop() removes KICK.WAV and KICK.JSN.
results.reasoning: start_job sets fsm.cur_name before the job runs (fs_machine.c:399) and neither set_err nor fsnd_start clears it; fs_fetch_handler only runs fs_safe_name (fs_web.c:148), with no sample_resolve check. With KICK.WAV in the pool, a fetch named KICK fails (imp_publish 'exists', sampimport.c:274, or any network error) and leaves cur_name=KICK; Drop Last then auditions the user's KICK successfully and fs_audition_drop removes its audio and .JSN. The 13.4 fix (fs_pool_name) covers the panel and /fs/get only, not this path.
results.fix_sketch: In fs_setup_action/fs_setup_val fall back to fsm.cur_name only when fsm.phase == FS_DONE (the job actually installed it). In fs_fetch_handler return 409 when sample_resolve(name) == 0, the same test fs_pool_name uses.

results.title: /fs/fetch onto a name held by X.RAW installs a shadowed X.WAV and overwrites X.JSN
results.claim: The direct-URL import uses the plain sanitised name with no collision check, unlike /fs/get (fs_pool_name). It can hit an existing sample under a different container.
results.scenario: name=X where X.RAW already exists. The download converts to X.WAV (it does not exist, so imp_publish succeeds). fs_write_sidecar then overwrites X.JSN, which sample_resolve_aux maps to the existing RAW's sidecar. sample_resolve prefers .RAW, so the new sound is invisible and the old sample's metadata is silently replaced.
results.reasoning: fs_fetch_handler uses fs_safe_name with no collision check; imp_publish only stats the .WAV destination (sampimport.c:274), so with usr/X.RAW present (web uploads land as .RAW) usr/X.WAV publishes and fs_write_sidecar rewrites /sdcard/usr/X.JSN (fs_machine.c:150). sample_resolve tries .RAW first (sampfile.c:72), so the job reports 'installed' but id X still plays the old file with the new sidecar. Drop Last after that DONE then removes the user's X.RAW, so data-loss stands. Not recorded on 09-16; 3.3 and 13.4 fixed neighbouring cases.
results.fix_sketch: In fs_fetch_handler refuse with 409 'name taken' when sample_resolve(name) == 0, mirroring the test in fs_pool_name. No id exists to suffix on this path, so refusing is the simple option.

results.title: Web /edit/apply repoints ed.src/in/out without updating ed.frames or ed.peaks
results.claim: editor_apply, also called by POST /edit/apply, overwrites ed.src, in_pt and out_pt without touching ed.frames or ed.peaks. Omitted in/out become 0/0.
results.scenario: The panel has sample A loaded (frames = F_A, peaks scanned). A web client posts /edit/apply?name=B&op=0. ed.src becomes B and ed.out_pt becomes 0, while ed.frames and ed.peaks still describe A. The panel now draws A's waveform against B's name, and the crop points are 0/0. TR1/Audition calls sampplay_window(0,0), which clamps to a 64-frame (1.4 ms) loop, so the audition is a buzz. Grabbing IN or OUT in wave_edit works from out_pt = 0. A later panel Apply runs on B with A's peaks and range assumptions.
results.reasoning: editor_apply writes ed.src, in_pt and out_pt (304-308) but only editor_load sets ed.frames and starts the peak scan. The web card sends the dropdown's name with the device's mirrored in/out (index.html edApply), or none when nothing is loaded, so the panel then shows B's name over A's waveform and length, or 0.00 s with out_pt=0. A TR1 or Setup audition then calls sampplay_window(0,0), which clamps to a 64-frame loop (sampplay.c:210-211), and A's crop range is applied to B. Not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: In editor_apply, when src differs from ed.src, call editor_probe(src), set ed.frames, clamp in/out to the file with out==0 meaning F, and clear ed.peaks (or chain scan_task when the job ends). A zero probe should set_err and return, which also closes the web trigger for the fd leak.

results.title: Freesound pipeline runs samp_import_file without claiming samp_import_busy
results.claim: The pipeline calls samp_import_file directly. It never checks or claims samp_import_busy, so it can overlap the pool-scan importer task. Both use the fixed scratch names IMPMP3.TMP and IMPNEW.TMP in usr/. The importer's directory scan also sees the pipeline's usr/<name>.mp3 while it is being written.
results.scenario: The user uploads a file or POSTs /import, which auto-kicks import_task, while a Freesound download is in its write or decode phase. Two decoders write and read the same usr/IMPMP3.TMP and IMPNEW.TMP. The result is a corrupt or mixed take, a failed rename, or the importer converting and deleting the half-written NAME.mp3 out from under the pipeline.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 3.4: it is listed under themes G and H but appears in no fix tier and not in the Watch list, and the code is unchanged (samp_import_file never reads samp_import_busy). Same-folder temp clashes are fenced by CONFIG_FATFS_FS_LOCK=5 in the local sdkconfig (the second f_open of IMPMP3.TMP/IMPNEW.TMP gets FR_LOCKED), so those end as a spurious 'convert failed' or an importer fail. When the pool scan is decoding an MP3 in another folder (own usr/DRUMS/IMPMP3.TMP), two decodeMP3FileSync calls share the globals `input`/`readPtr` (mp3.c:29-30, 296, 305): garbage decode and a double free. The scan is kicked by every upload (rest-api.c:1478) and POST /import.
results.fix_sketch: Add a test-and-set claim on samp_import_busy (portMUX, like ed_claim in editor.c) used by both samp_import_start and the pipeline around its samp_import_file call; the pipeline waits or fails with 'importer busy'. Also make `input`/`readPtr` in mp3.c locals passed into decode().

results.title: fsm.busy is cleared before the pipeline task has finished its cleanup
results.claim: set_err clears `busy` while the pipeline task is still alive and about to run its cleanup (f_close, f_unlink(pool_path), TLS cleanup, free, vTaskDelete).
results.scenario: A download errors and the user immediately re-presses the same result. start_job passes the busy check and a second 40 KB task and TLS client start, or fails with 'no RAM for the download task' because the old stack is still held. The second job f_opens usr/<name>.mp3 with CREATE_ALWAYS. The first task then reaches `out:`, sees fsm.phase != FS_DONE (the new job's phase) and runs f_unlink(pool_path), deleting the new job's file mid-write. It can also stomp fsm.err and fsm.phase.
results.reasoning: The defect is real: set_err (74) and the success path (372) drop busy while the task still has to close, unlink, tear down TLS and free its 40 KB stack. The finder's consequences are overstated: after set_err the old task never writes fsm.err/phase again, and its f_unlink cannot hit the new job's file (that file is opened seconds later, after the download, and FS_LOCK refuses unlinking an open file). What remains is a millisecond window in which a second start_job either gets 'no RAM for the download task' or briefly runs two 40 KB tasks. Missing: a press or POST landing inside that window, which I could not establish as realistic.
results.fix_sketch: Have set_err set only err and phase, and clear fsm.busy once at `out:` after all cleanup, just before vTaskDelete. Or put the pipeline on worker.h (worker_spawn refuses while the old task is alive, worker_exit as the last line).

results.title: start_job ignores s_searching; shared s_http_status; non-atomic busy check
results.claim: start_job does not check `s_searching`, though fs_search_start refuses when a download is busy. Search and download can therefore run together, sharing the static s_http_status/s_http_err and two TLS sessions. The check-then-set on `busy` and `s_searching` is also not atomic across the UI and httpd tasks.
results.scenario: POST /fs/get, or a panel press, arrives while a page search is running. The download's error text then reads the other request's s_http_status/s_http_err ('freesound HTTP 429' shown for a network failure). Two TLS handshakes need roughly 2x32 KB contiguous internal RAM, so one of them fails or the allocator is starved. Two near-simultaneous callers can both pass the busy check and start two pipelines writing the same fsm state.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 findings 13.10 (shared static s_http_status/s_http_err, start_job ignores s_searching, two TLS sessions compete for internal RAM) and 13.12 (fsm.busy check-and-set not atomic). Both are on the Watch list (13.9-13.12, low consequence). The code is unchanged (fs_machine.c:83-84, 392, 606) and the Watch reasoning still holds; nothing new to add.

results.title: Editor job re-reads live ed.op/ed.param after snapshotting x.op
results.claim: job_task snapshots `ed.op` into x.op at the start but re-reads the live `ed.op` for open_out(ed.op) and the branch chain, and ed.param later. The Setup > Op and Param rows can be changed while a job is running, since ed_setup_adj has no running guard.
results.scenario: The user presses Apply for REVERSE and, during the source open and output create window, rotates the Op row. The branch runs on the new op (for example FADEIN) while the output was named and prefixed for the old op. With x.op still OP_REVERSE, frame_gain returns 1.0, so the take is an unmodified copy labelled as an edit. NORMALIZE with a changed op runs a branch that never sets x.gain.
results.reasoning: job_task snapshots x.op at :216 but uses the live ed.op for open_out (:221), the branch chain (:224-258) and ed.param (:249, :259). ed_setup_adj (editor_menu.c:252) has no running guard and Op is a click-toggle row, so a change during open_out (one readdir pass over 7 folders plus file create) runs another op's branch with x.op still the old one, giving an unmodified copy under the old prefix. Not established: whether that sub-second window is reachable from the panel (two detents back plus a press) or via setup_menu_remote_adjust on a real card. A change before :216 just runs the new op consistently.
results.fix_sketch: Use x.op for open_out() and the whole branch chain, and snapshot ed.param into a local beside x at :216. Nothing new is needed; ed_xf_t already carries the op.

results.title: span_rev accepts a partial read and silently drops the unread frames
results.claim: span_rev treats only got == 0 as an error. A partial read (0 < got < n) is flipped and written short, then pos jumps to `start`. The unread frames are dropped and s_io_err is not set.
results.scenario: A transient short fread on a chunk during Reverse (card hiccup, or the file shorter than its header claims) leaves a gap of (n-got) frames. The job finishes ED_DONE 'wrote RV_xxxx' with a shorter, mis-ordered take. span_fwd tolerates short reads because it continues from the file position, but span_rev re-seeks every chunk.
results.reasoning: Incomplete fix of 13.8: only got == 0 sets s_io_err. With 0 < got < n, span_rev flips and writes got frames, then sets pos = start (:195), so n-got frames vanish and the job ends ED_DONE. sf_parse clamps frames to the file size (sampfile_int.h:66-72, :121), so an intact file never reads short; this needs a card read error. After the per-chunk fseek, newlib fread can return already-buffered bytes before the failing read, so a partial count is a likely shape of that error.
results.fix_sketch: In span_rev, treat any short chunk as an error: `if (got != n) { s_io_err = true; break; }`. The existing fail_output() then deletes the take.

results.title: editor_start wipes ed while a job that outlived editor_stop still runs
results.claim: editor_start wipes the shared `ed` struct. editor_stop only waits 3 s (300 ticks) for a running job or scan, so on re-entry a still-running job continues writing ed.* into the freshly reset struct.
results.scenario: Normalize on a multi-minute file is running and the user switches machines. editor_stop gives up after 3 s and the job continues. The user switches back to Editor. ed is zeroed (src, out, clip_full, peaks, state) while s_running is still true. The job later sets ed.state = ED_DONE and ed.out over the new session, and every new Apply or Load is refused silently (the claim fails) until it finishes.
results.reasoning: editor_stop (:591) waits 300 x 1 tick = 3 s and then returns with the job alive. Jobs sleep a tick per 2048-frame chunk, so Normalize on anything over about 7 s of audio outlasts it. On re-entry editor_start memsets ed but s_running/s_scanning stay set, so ed_claim (:38) silently refuses every Load/Apply/clip until the old job ends. That job then sets ED_DONE over the zeroed struct (status reads 'wrote ' with no name), and on an I/O error fail_output gets an empty id and leaves the partial take. No memory is freed, so it is behaviour only; not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Follow fsnd_start (fs_machine.c:748): skip the memset while s_running || s_scanning. Or move the job/scan/clip tasks onto worker.h and check w.run in the span loops, so editor_stop aborts the job and fail_output() removes the partial take.

results.title: sample_resolve stat() calls run without sd_lock
results.claim: sample_resolve issues up to 28 unlocked stat() calls with no sd_lock. Callers in this scope are fs_pool_name, fs_audition_drop, editor open_src, editor_probe and sampplay_open, on the UI, httpd and job tasks. The project rule is that every SD burst holds sd_lock.
results.scenario: The UI task presses a result, and fs_pool_name resolves the name (28 directory walks) while the raw-FatFS audio reader tasks (Deck, Sampler) are mid f_read under sd_lock only. The two access the card bus concurrently, which the notes describe as the wedge/corruption case.
results.reasoning: This is 6.12 (Watch): the files_raw_handler lines it cited at ae6681a (513-517) are these same sample_resolve calls, so the unlocked stat was already recorded. Every reader calls it the same way (deck.c:135, sample_ram.c:112, sampplay.c:152). The concurrent-bus corruption claim does not hold: FatFS is built FF_FS_REENTRANT=1 (IDF 4.3 ffconf.h:287), so f_stat and the raw f_read serialise on the volume mutex. It remains a breach of the sd_lock house rule with no traced consequence.

results.title: /fs/search proxy stores the %-encoded q in fsm.last_query
results.claim: The raw-proxy handler stores the still %-encoded, underscore-filtered `q` into fsm.last_query. That is the persisted preset query and the string the panel paging, entry seed and Setup use. It is written from httpd without touching fsm.page or fsm.results. The handler also runs a full TLS session on httpd's 8 KB stack (config.stack_size = 4096*2), where the search task measured about 5.5 KB.
results.scenario: The web page searches 'tabla loop' (sent as tabla%20loop). last_query becomes 'tabla%20loop'. The panel results page then pages with fs_search_start(fsm.last_query, page+1) and searches the literal encoded text, so the next page does not match the shown results. The preset autosave persists the garbled query. Separately, a TLS handshake on the 8 KB httpd stack is close to its measured peak and risks a stack overflow reboot.
results.reasoning: The handler copies the still-encoded, filtered q into fsm.last_query without touching page/results. The panel then pages with fs_search_start(fsm.last_query, page±1) (fs_menu.c:351/359), url_escape re-encodes the '%', and fsnd_preset_save persists the string. The shipped page no longer calls /fs/search (index.html:1527 uses /fs/query), so only a direct API client with a multi-word query hits it. The httpd-stack claim is not established: the measured search peak is about 5.5 KB including a cJSON parse against an 8 KB httpd stack, and this was the production search path until 09-12.
results.fix_sketch: Delete the strlcpy at :81; last_query belongs to fs_search_task (fs_machine.c:590), which sets it together with page and results. If the proxy must record it, run the existing urldecode() on a copy first.

results.title: /fs/state emits fsm.err unescaped into hand-built JSON
results.claim: /fs/state builds JSON by hand with fsm.err unescaped. fsm.err can hold a server-supplied `detail` string (set_err(det->valuestring)).
results.scenario: Freesound returns a `detail` containing a double quote or backslash. /fs/state then emits invalid JSON, and the web card's poll fails to parse it and stops updating the pipeline status.
results.reasoning: fsm.err can hold the server's `detail` text (fs_machine.c:200), after cJSON has unescaped it, and it is printed with a bare %s. A quote or backslash in it gives invalid JSON; fsState() (index.html:1633) swallows the parse error, so the card stays on its last status and keeps polling. Sizes are fine (worst case about 190 of 256 bytes) and id/name are sanitised. Missing: evidence that Freesound returns a detail containing a quote or backslash on a GET.
results.fix_sketch: Build the reply with cJSON as fs_results_handler does in the same file (cJSON_AddStringToObject + cJSON_PrintUnformatted), which escapes err.

results.title: Freesound sidecar write failure is ignored; job still reports done
results.claim: The sidecar write result is ignored: writeJSONFile returns void and fs_write_sidecar always returns 0. Pool listings require the .JSN, so a failed write leaves the take unlisted while the pipeline reports FS_DONE. The f_close at line 324 is also unchecked.
results.scenario: The card is nearly full or the fopen fails after the WAV lands. The job reports 'got NAME' and autoplays it, but /files and the browsers never list the sample, and Drop Last cannot find its sidecar.
results.reasoning: writeJSONFile (fileio.c:311) returns void and ignores fopen/fwrite/fclose results; fs_write_sidecar returns 0 unconditionally, also when cJSON_Print returns NULL, so the check at :365 is dead. GET /files skips ids with no .JSN (rest-api.c:264), so the take is missing from the web list, and fs_pool_name then treats the bare WAV as a different sound and re-downloads it as <title>_<id>. Overstated parts: the panel browsers do not need the sidecar, Drop handles a missing one (:735-738), and a failed f_close at :324 leads to 'convert failed', not a false success.
results.fix_sketch: Make writeJSONFile return int (fopen, fwrite length and fclose checked; existing callers may ignore it) and have fs_write_sidecar return that, with -1 when cJSON_Print is NULL. The set_err("sidecar write failed") path at :365 already exists.

results.title: PUT /drop_ot ignores the f_write result and publishes a short .OT over the good one
results.claim: Sibling of the mod_upload fix in 11810ee. That commit made the module upload check f_write and refuse to publish a short file. drop_ot_put_handler still ignores the f_write result, then f_close and f_rename publish OT_TMP as the real .OT.
results.scenario: The card fills, or an SD write error hits, during PUT /drop_ot. f_write returns FR_DENIED or writes fewer bytes than asked. The handler ignores it, renames a truncated .OT over the good one, and replies 200. The Slicer then reads a short slice map. The old .OT was already f_unlink'd on line 2176, so the good copy is gone.
results.reasoning: drop_ot_put_handler discards both the FRESULT and bw at :2172, then f_close / f_unlink(path) / f_rename at :2175-2177 publish OT_TMP and the handler replies 200. On a full card FatFS f_write returns FR_OK with bw=0, so a 0-byte .OT replaces the existing one. Correction to the scenario: the Slicer does not read a short map, slicer_parse_ot rejects anything that is not 832 bytes (slicer_ot.c:63) and falls back, so the harm is the lost previous slice map plus a false success, no crash. Sibling that 6.8 did not name (it listed mod_upload and drop_sample only, fixed in 11810ee / e327f6f); drop_ot was never recorded.
results.fix_sketch: Copy the check mod_upload_handler already has at rest-api.c:2102-2109: keep FRESULT wr and bw, and on wr != FR_OK || bw != (UINT)ret do f_close + f_unlink(OT_TMP) under sd_lock and return 500 before the unlink/rename. While there, use recv_bounded() like the other upload handlers and check f_close before publishing (the last 320 bytes are only flushed at close).

results.title: DoubleDecker analysis task clears an_running again outside s_an_mux on exit
results.claim: The analysis task clears an_running again after its loop, outside the critical section. dd_maybe_analyze can set an_running = true and an_track for a new job, then call worker_idle(&s_an, 500), in the gap between the task leaving the critical section (line 327) and this line.
results.scenario: The task empties the queue and leaves the critical section with an_running = false. The UI thread then loads a track on deck B, sets an_running = true and an_deck = B, and starts waiting for the old task to exit. The old task runs line 336 and clobbers an_running to false, then exits. A new task is spawned, but an_running now reads false. A later load on deck A sees 'not running', sets it true, waits 500 ms, and worker_spawn refuses because the task is alive. The error path on line 367 then sets an_deck = -1 and an_running = false. Deck A's analysis is lost, and deck B's result is dropped by the 'd >= 0' adopt check. The window is very small.
results.reasoning: The unlocked store at :336 (added in cb19915, only needed for the !s_an.run break at :313) runs after the task has left the critical section at :333, so dd_maybe_analyze (:348-360) can claim an_running/an_track in between and have an_running clobbered to false while the respawned task runs. The consequence is worse than stated: a later load in that ~1 min run overwrites dd.an_track, the spawn is refused (:364-368), and the live task then writes the OTHER track's bpm/grid into the new track's sidecar at :315, which then counts as already stamped (:345). Not established: the trigger needs the UI to enter dd_maybe_analyze inside a window of a few instructions (or a preemption exactly there) and then a second load during the orphaned run. Not recorded on 09-16; it is a new defect in the 10.4/10.5 fix code.
results.fix_sketch: Delete the unconditional store at :336 and clear an_running / an_deck (and an_pending) under s_an_mux only on the stop path, i.e. in the `if (!s_an.run)` break at :313. The normal exit already cleared them inside the critical section at :327, so worker_exit(&s_an) can follow directly.

results.title: Keys process() guard and cubic_read can see different z->frames
results.reasoning: Nothing is stored between the guard at :577 and the cubic_read calls at :578/:587, and the build is -O2 (sdkconfig CONFIG_COMPILER_OPTIMIZATION_PERF), so the compiler loads z->frames once per sample: in the existing object (build/esp-idf/machine_instsampler/libmachine_instsampler.a, keys_process+0x907 `l32i a2,a9,40`) the same register feeds the guard and both clamps (+0x9ac, +0xc2c). A zeroed frames therefore fails the guard and cubic_read never runs with n=0; buf stays valid until machine_block_wait() returns (:94, :204). Even if it did reload, the result would be one stray sample with no fault at a moment the note is hard-cut anyway. Source-level hardening only: a per-sample local for frames, as 7c04ccd gave Synth's wave_len, would make it independent of the compiler.

results.title: Keys in-place reload of the last zone overwrites the buffer without the handshake
results.reasoning: The in-place branch (zi == nzones-1, :126) is dead code: every caller passes zi = -1 (instsampler.c:264 after keys_clear_zones(), instsampler.c:756 after keys_clear_zones(), isampler_menu.c:1111 Add Zone), so every load appends into an unused slot whose frames is already 0 and which no voice maps to (:276, :465). Load Sample goes through keys_load_zone (:261-265), which runs the full keys_clear_zones handshake (:92-94) before loading. Were the branch ever reached, inst.loading (:142) silences every block after the one in flight, which ends within 1.45 ms, before sample_load's resolve + fopen + probe + first SD read (sample_ram.c:112-136) can write anything.

results.title: MP3 sync search scans past the bytes read; nRead - offset wraps in memmove
results.claim: The new slide-to-front code trusts `offset` from MP3FindSyncWord(input, MAX_FRAME_SIZE). That call scans all 4096 bytes even when f_read returned fewer (nRead < 4096). A sync pattern in the stale, uninitialised or recycled tail gives offset >= nRead, so `nRead - offset` wraps as unsigned.
results.scenario: A short or corrupt MP3/garbage file (under 4 KB, or whose ID3 skip leaves under 4 KB before EOF) has no sync word in its valid bytes. `input` is a fresh malloc, often reusing the previous decode's freed block, which is full of 0xFFEx patterns. FindSyncWord returns an offset past nRead, `nRead - offset` becomes about 4 billion, memmove crashes the device, and `valid` would be garbage. Before this commit `offset` was unused, so this is a new crash path, reachable from import or upload of a bad file.
results.reasoning: mp3.c:100 calls MP3FindSyncWord(input, MAX_FRAME_SIZE) although f_read may have returned nRead < 4096, and `input` is an uninitialised malloc (mp3.c:299). On a short FIRST read with no sync in the valid bytes, a 0xFF/0xEx pair in the stale tail gives offset > nRead, so `nRead - offset` (UINT) wraps and memmove runs off the heap. Only the first read can hit it (later short reads have a tail already proven sync-free), so it needs a file that passes magic_is_mp3 on the bare "ID3" test (sampimport.c:176) with under 4 KB left after the tag skip and no frame in it; it also depends on heap garbage, which is likely after an earlier decode. New path introduced by the 3.5 fix (38239db); runs in the importer task and the Freesound pipeline.
results.fix_sketch: Pass nRead to MP3FindSyncWord, as radio.c:312 already does with its fill count, and treat offset >= nRead as no sync. Optionally memset the tail or calloc `input` in decodeMP3FileSync.

results.title: Re-upload under an existing name is refused by imp_publish and left unconverted
results.claim: imp_publish now refuses to replace an existing destination .WAV. Re-uploading a sample under an existing name (POST drop_sample writes <name>.RAW, then the importer targets <name>.WAV) leaves the new audio unconverted beside the old WAV. The same happens when a Freesound web download names a sound that is already in the pool.
results.scenario: The user uploads kick.wav, edits it, and uploads it again as 'kick'. The JSN sidecar is rewritten and the HTTP call returns 200. The import fails silently (only a fail counter and a log line), so kick.RAW stays next to the old KICK.WAV and the OLD audio keeps playing. Every later import scan logs and fails on it again. For /fs/get of the same freesound id that is already present, the pipeline ends in 'convert failed' and unlinks its mp3.
results.reasoning: The web page uploads mp3/wav/aif bytes as-is (index.html:1292,1342,1417) to usr/<name>.RAW; the first upload converts to <name>.WAV, the second hits stat(dst)==0 at sampimport.c:274 and returns -1 while drop_sample has already answered 200. Finder's consequence is wrong in one detail: the old audio does not keep playing, because sample_resolve tries .RAW first (sampfile.c:72,88-91), so the unconverted upload shadows the old WAV: a 48k/24-bit WAV then fails to load ("WAV: not 44.1kHz") and MP3 bytes fall through sf_parse as headerless RAW (sampfile_int.h:151) and play as noise. Every later scan retries and fails again. The 3.3 fix holds for what it recorded (no source loss); this is the case it left refused. The Freesound same-id case only yields a misleading "convert failed" with the existing sample intact.
results.fix_sketch: In imp_publish, when dst exists and src is the upload/download scratch twin (.RAW or .MP3 of the same base), replace it with the existing IMPBAK.TMP park-and-rename path (dst to bak, tmp to dst, remove bak and src), restoring on failure. Keep the refusal for X.AIF beside X.WAV, and surface the failure through the import fail counter the page already polls.

results.title: cJSON PSRAM hook makes JSON writes fail on the SDMMC bounce buffer
results.reasoning: The bounce buffer for a non-DMA source is one 512-byte sector (esp-idf-v4.3 sdmmc_cmd.c:377), not the whole buffer, and with CONFIG_FATFS_ALLOC_PREFER_EXTRAM=y (sdkconfig:634; ffsystem.c:20, vfs_fat.c:161) the VFS FIL sector caches and FATFS window already live in PSRAM, so every VFS write needs that same 512-byte allocation wherever the source string is. The hook adds no new failure mode and removes a ~5 KB internal allocation; sampimport.c:228-246 already fwrites PSRAM buffers. writeJSONFile ignoring fwrite's result (fileio.c:329) is real but pre-existing and independent of the hook; the 09-16 bench logged 0 autosave errors in 110 saves after it.

results.title: savePresetConfig leaks the cJSON_Print string
results.reasoning: The leak is in the code, but savePresetConfig is only called from machine_sampler2/sampler_menu.c:1168 and :2088, and repairAudioFileAssigment (fileio.c:195) only from machine_sampler2/sampler.c:1484; that component is excluded from the build (CMakeLists.txt:10) and out of scope. fileio.c:62 (createConfigFile) runs once at boot, only when CONFIG.JSN is missing or invalid (fileio.c:138-140), so it is a single leak of a few hundred bytes, not a per-use one. The live CONFIG.JSN writers (menu_config.c:72,100; menu.c:513,718; rest-api.c:1229,1826) all free the string.

results.title: A long gap poisons ext_period and stretches the fallback wait
results.reasoning: ext_period is rewritten on every fired edge (clock.c:389), so the stretched wait lasts only until the jack's second pulse; the scenario needs the jack pulled again after exactly one pulse. The first-pulse-after-gap stretch is the 1.10 design (comment at clock.c:392-395, commit 8f999ef): leaving fallback, ext_idle is always at least 2 s, and that is what lets a jack slower than 2 s deliver its second pulse before the stand-in returns. A saturated counter gives 0 (default 2 s). Residual, low: a lone stray edge on a dead jack suspends the INT stand-in for up to 10 s where it was 2 s.

results.title: drop_sample ignores the f_close result (the pad write cannot fail on a full card)
results.claim: The new short-write checks cover only the main upload loop. The final frame-align pad write and the later f_close are still unchecked. A card that fills on the last sector returns 200, starts the importer and fires EV_DECODING_DONE on a file that is short or misaligned.
results.scenario: The upload's last chunk fills the card exactly. The 1 to 3 pad bytes fail to write and f_close fails to flush. The handler returns 200 and starts the importer on an unaligned or truncated RAW, which is then imported as a silently cut sample. This is the same class as review 6.8, left unfixed a few lines below the fix.
results.reasoning: The card-full scenario does not hold: the pad is written only when content_len % 4 != 0, so the file end is mid-sector in an already-allocated cluster and the 1-3 bytes are a copy into the FIL sector cache with no allocation and no disk I/O; a full card is caught by the checked loop write at rest-api.c:1426, so the 6.8 fix holds. What remains is the unchecked f_close at rest-api.c:1468: if its flush or directory update hits a card I/O error, the handler still returns 200 and starts the importer on a file whose directory entry was never updated (size 0). I could not establish a trigger other than a failing card.
results.fix_sketch: Check the FRESULT of the pad f_write and of f_close; on failure reuse the existing error branch at rest-api.c:1430-1437 (f_unlink, EV_DECODING_DONE, 500 "SD write failed") and skip samp_import_start().
