results.title: Sampler3 reverse: read_playback_frames reverses in place with dst == stage, scrambling every chunk
results.claim: read_playback_frames() reverses a chunk in place: every caller passes the same pointer for dst and stage (rebuild_head, loop-start cache, ring fill, waveform thumbnail), so the forward copy loop overwrites source frames before they are read.
results.scenario: Reverse mode on (REV, or preset rev:true via s3_set_reverse). For got=4 the stage [a,b,c,d] becomes [d,c,c,d] instead of [d,c,b,a]. In each chunk of up to 4096 frames the first half is the reversed tail and the second half is the forward audio. The head cache, the ring and the loop-start cache are all built this way, so reverse playback is scrambled, and the thumbnail is drawn from scrambled data too.
results.reasoning: All four callers pass (stage, stage) (sampler3.c:107, 126, 325-326, 375), so the forward copy loop reads frames it already overwrote: for i >= got/2 it copies back the original frame i. Each chunk of up to 4096 frames ends up as reversed second half followed by the un-reversed second half; head cache, loop-start cache, ring and thumbnail are all built from that. Present since the first sampler3 commit (3a6298c); the 09-16 review only recorded 8.4 (preset REV not rebuilding the head), not this.
results.fix_sketch: When dst + got_total*2 == stage, reverse with a two-pointer frame swap over i < got/2 (the tape_reverse pattern, tape.c:684-691) instead of the forward copy. Keep the existing forward copy for the dst != stage case.

results.title: Slicer reverse: read_slice_frames reverses in place with dst == stage, scrambling heads and tail
results.claim: Same in-place reversal bug as sampler3: read_slice_frames() is always called with dst == stage (build_heads line 201-202, tail fill line 295-296), so the reverse branch reads frames it has already overwritten.
results.scenario: sl.reverse is set from the Setup row or from preset 'reverse':true. build_heads then stores scrambled slice heads: first half is the reversed tail, second half is unflipped. The streamed tail is scrambled the same way, so every slice plays wrong in reverse.
results.reasoning: Both callers pass (stage, stage): build_heads at slicer.c:201-202 and the tail fill at 295-296, and n never exceeds SL_CHUNK (4096; heads are 3528) so it is always a single aliased pass. The loop therefore yields reversed second half + forward second half per read, which is what lands in the slice heads and the ring when sl.reverse is on (Setup row slicer_menu.c:355 or preset 'reverse'). Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Same fix as sampler3: in-place two-pointer frame swap when dst aliases stage (tape_reverse pattern). Ideally share one helper between sampler3 and slicer since the code is a copy.

results.title: s3_stop leaves an active take, a parked writer and TRIG_FUNC_RECORD behind on machine switch
results.claim: s3_stop() never finishes an in-flight take, cancels a prepared recording writer, or restores the recording trig_func. The core keeps feeding line-in to the recorder whenever rec_active, whatever machine is active.
results.scenario: (a) Gate-arm or record a take in Sampler, then switch machine mid-take. recording_is_active() stays true, audio.c keeps calling recording_push(in), and the rec_writer task keeps writing the line input until the card is full. Nothing in any other machine stops it. (b) Arm a voice (recording_prepare has parked the writer with an empty file) and switch away. rec_prepared and trig_func[vid]=TRIG_FUNC_RECORD persist. audio_bounce_start() refuses with 'armed take counts as busy', and on return to Sampler the gate starts a take although s3.arm_target was reset to -1 by memset in s3_start. Stale s_arm_req/s_rec_abort_req also survive start().
results.reasoning: s3_stop (519-528) only stops the reader and frees buffers; it never calls recording_finish/cancel_prepared/set_trig_func, unlike tape_stop (tape.c:1032-1033). audio.c:643 pushes line-in whenever rec_active && !s_bounce regardless of machine, so a take in flight keeps writing until the card/file limit (and /reboot refuses, rest-api.c:2539), and an armed writer keeps rec_prepared set so audio_bounce_start returns silently at audio.c:168. trig_func stays RECORD and s_arm_req/s_rec_abort_req/s_discard_next are file statics not cleared by s3_start's memset, so on return the gate drives a take with arm_target = -1. Not recorded on 09-16 (1.3 only made bounce refuse an armed take).
results.fix_sketch: In s3_stop, before worker_stop, do what tape_stop does: if recording_is_active() recording_finish(); recording_cancel_prepared(); then recording_set_trig_func(0/1, TRIG_FUNC_VOICE). Clear s_arm_req, s_rec_abort_req and s_discard_next in s3_start and drain recording_poll_load there so a stale pickup cannot land.

results.title: tape_set_len_sel frees the tape banks under a running save_task (no save_busy/autosave_req check)
results.claim: tape_set_len_sel() frees and reallocates the tape banks whenever the transport is stopped. It does not check save_busy (the background save_task reading the banks) or tp.loading. bank_free() only waits for the audio task, not for the writer or loader.
results.scenario: Record a take and punch out. tape_rec_stop queues an auto-save and save_task streams frames [save_a,save_b) via tp_rd(). While it runs (seconds for a 30-40 s take), Setup > Length is turned (tape_menu.c:870) or a web /remote/params with a different 'lsel' is applied. bank_free() frees the blocks and NULLs blk[i], so save_task's tp_rd() dereferences a freed or NULL bank (LoadStoreError panic or garbage take). The same happens if the change lands between the audio task raising autosave_req and tape_autosave_kick spawning the writer. The same path also sets take_dirty=false, discarding the unsaved take. A preset 'lsel' change during a tape_load would free the bank the loader is writing into. Paste/cut/norm/reverse/fade during save_busy are not flagged as drop_spoiled either, so they silently corrupt the saved file.
results.reasoning: tape_set_len_sel only checks tp_stopped(); bank_alloc -> bank_free (tape.c:56-63) waits for the audio block only, then frees and NULLs blk[], while save_task (768-798) is still reading via tp_rd/bank_rd, which dereferences blk[i>>shift] unguarded (tape_priv.h:56-59) -> NULL/freed read or a garbage take, and take_dirty=false drops the take. A pending autosave_req has the same hole (tape_autosave_kick then saves stale save_a/save_b from the new bank). Reached by Setup > Length (tape_menu.c:870) or a web preset 'lsel' while a long take is still saving after TR1 stop; the 11.3 fix covered only the audio task. The finder's 'preset lsel during tape_load' part cannot happen (both run on the UI task), and the edit-ops-during-save part is real but only yields an unflagged blended file.
results.fix_sketch: In tape_set_len_sel refuse (return -1) while tp.save_busy || tp.autosave_req || tp.adopt_id[0], or kick tape_autosave_kick() and wait on save_busy the way tape_stop does (tape.c:1034-1037) before bank_alloc. Give tape_norm/reverse/fade/cut/paste the same save_busy guard (or set drop_spoiled).

results.title: Reader tasks never check their internal DMA staging allocs (deck, dualdeck, sampler3, slicer)
results.claim: Reader tasks allocate their 16 KB internal DMA staging buffer (and a 2 KB tail buffer) at task start and never check for NULL. start() has already returned ESP_OK by then, so a failure crashes later. Internal RAM is the scarce pool.
results.scenario: Start Deck when internal RAM is fragmented and there is no contiguous 16 KB DMA block (Radio or broadcast active, or after a long session; the tracker note records exactly this failure on a fresh boot). reader_task keeps running, and the first track load calls sampfile_read(f,&sfl,NULL,...) and fills/memcpy's through NULL, which panics the module. The same unchecked pattern is in dualdeck.c:240-241 (chunk, tail), sampler3.c:142 (stage) and slicer.c:219 (stage).
results.reasoning: chunk (16 KB) and tail are allocated inside reader_task after start() already returned ESP_OK and are used unchecked: sampfile_read (sampfile.c:29-36) freads straight into dst, and the seam blend reads tail[]. Same at dualdeck.c:240-241, sampler3.c:142 and slicer.c:219. The 09-16 bench notes record the internal largest block dipping to 10 KB and a Deck start landing on Stub after a 22 KB leak, so a task stack fitting while the 16 KB block does not is credible, but it still needs internal-RAM exhaustion. Not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: Allocate the staging buffers in start() before worker_spawn (static pointer or task arg) and return ESP_ERR_NO_MEM on failure so machine_activate's Stub fallback handles it; free them in stop() only when worker_stop succeeded. Apply the same to all four readers.

results.title: radio_play_url sleeps between the ring check and task spawn; radio_stop could free the ring in between
results.reasoning: The premise is wrong: machine_activate calls s_web_cb(NULL) before stop() (machine_core.c:65-67), and machine_web_apply (rest-api.c:1997-2009) queues the URI swap on the single httpd task and waits for it, so an in-flight /radio/play handler (max 400 ms sleep) returns, with its stream task already counted in s_ntasks, before radio_stop runs; radio_stop_stream then waits for that task. The panel path (radio_menu.c:135) runs on the UI task, the same task that performs the switch. The only escape is the 10 s give-up at rest-api.c:2007, which needs httpd stalled by another handler for >10 s plus a queued /radio/play landing in the stop window.

results.title: glitch_start leaks the surviving PSRAM block on a partial allocation failure
results.claim: On a partial allocation failure glitch_start() returns without freeing the block that did allocate. machine_activate() does not call stop() for a failed start, and the next glitch_start() memsets gl, dropping the pointer.
results.scenario: PSRAM is fragmented: the 88 KB window allocs but the 352 KB ring fails (or the reverse). The machine falls back to Stub, and the successful block stays allocated with its pointer in gl.win/gl.ring. The next glitch_start() does memset(&gl,0) first, so that block is leaked permanently. Every retry can leak another, starving Tape, Keys and the FX slabs of the 4 MB pool.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 12.5 verbatim; it sits on the Watch list (low consequence, needs a PSRAM alloc failure) and was not part of the theme B/C fix commits, which covered 11.9 but not 12.5. The code is unchanged (no free on the error path, memset at line 54 drops the pointer) and the Watch reasoning still holds. Sizes check: ring 352,800 bytes, window 88,200 bytes.

results.title: Deck reader writes a chunk read for the old wpos after loop toggle truncated wpos
results.claim: The reader reads dk.wpos for the file position (ff = dk_map(dk.wpos)), does the SD read without any lock against the audio task, then re-reads dk.wpos for the ring slot and adds got to it. deck_loop_toggle (audio task) truncates dk.wpos and rewrites map_p0/map_f0 in between. On release the mapping words are written before loop_active is cleared.
results.scenario: TR2 loop engage or release lands while the reader is inside sampfile_read (a chunk read takes milliseconds and happens every ~90 ms while the loop lead cap is small). The audio task sets dk.wpos = valid_to. The reader then writes the chunk it read for the OLD wpos (linear continuation past the window end) into ring slot valid_to, which the new mapping defines as the window start, then wpos += got. One 4096-frame (~93 ms) chunk of the wrong file region plays at the seam. On release, dk_map can also see the new map_p0 with loop_active still true. The same structure is in dualdeck.c (reader_serve / dualdeck_loop_toggle).
results.reasoning: The reader computes ff = dk_map(dk.wpos) at deck.c:193, does the SD read, then re-reads dk.wpos for the ring slot and does dk.wpos += got (225-230) with no re-validation, while deck_loop_toggle on the audio task (call at 750) sets dk.wpos = valid_to and rewrites map_p0/map_f0 (459-463, 529-534). In steady play the reader reads one 4096-frame chunk about every 93 ms, so an engage landing inside that read puts up to 93 ms of audio from the old frontier (about 7 s ahead) into the slots the new mapping defines as the loop start, heard once at the first seam. dualdeck.c reader_serve (168-205) and dualdeck_loop_toggle have the same structure; the release-ordering window (459-462) is real but only instructions wide. Hit rate per engage is read time / 93 ms, which I could not measure from reading.
results.fix_sketch: Reuse the slicer generation pattern (sl.gen / fill_gen, slicer.c:275-307): bump a volatile loop generation in deck_loop_toggle, have the reader snapshot wpos and the generation before dk_map, and after the read drop the chunk (cur_ff = -1) if either changed, otherwise write at the snapshot and publish wpos = snapshot + got. Same change in dualdeck reader_serve.

results.title: radio_play_url zeroes ring counters under a live radio_process drain; rpos ends above wpos
results.claim: radio_play_url() (httpd/UI task) zeroes both ring counters while rd.state is still RADIO_PLAYING and the audio task may be inside radio_process, whose rd.rpos++ is a non-atomic read-modify-write. radio_stop_stream does the same.
results.scenario: The audio task loads rpos=R, the UI stores rpos=wpos=0, and the audio task then stores R+1. Now rpos > wpos, and unsigned wpos-rpos is huge. ring_write's backpressure test (wpos-rpos >= RING-2) is permanently true, so the new stream task spins in vTaskDelay(1) and never buffers. process() sees rpos>=wpos and plays silence. Radio is wedged until another play/stop. The window is microseconds per station change, so it is rare.
results.reasoning: A web station change (index.html:2776 posts /radio/play with no stop first) reaches line 387 with rd.state still RADIO_PLAYING, because a retired task never touches state and state is only set at 394. httpd is pinned to core 0 (rest-api.c:2687) and the audio task to core 1 (audio.c:760), so radio_process can sit between its 'rpos < wpos' test (452) and 'rd.rpos++' (456) when both are zeroed, leaving rpos >= 1 and wpos == 0. The new task then waits forever in ring_write's backpressure loop (121, unsigned wpos-rpos is huge) and the station shows 'buffering' until a stop/play. The window is the drain loop, roughly 0.5% of each block, so it is rare; the unit itself does not hang, so the class is wrong-behaviour. The same zeroing in radio_stop_stream (369) is healed by the next play.
results.fix_sketch: In radio_play_url, set rd.state = RADIO_BUFFERING before the reset and call machine_block_wait() so process() is out of its drain loop, then zero wpos/rpos; do the same wait before the zeroing in radio_stop_stream. Also add the 'gen == s_gen' test to ring_write's backpressure loop so a retired task cannot write after the reset.

results.title: Radio ring and resampler scratch leaked for good after a stop timeout
results.claim: When radio_stop() leaves the ring because a stream task is stuck in a slow connect, rd.ring and s_rs.ext stay set. Once that task eventually exits, the next radio_start() sees ntasks==0, memsets rd (dropping rd.ring) and overwrites s_rs.ext with a fresh allocation, so the old slabs can never be freed.
results.scenario: Start a station whose DNS/TLS connect takes longer than the 7 s stop wait, then switch away (ring ~690 KB and scratch ~4.8 KB leaked by design). The task exits a few seconds later. Switching back to Radio, radio_start passes its ntasks check and calls memset(&rd,0,...); rd.ring = heap_caps_malloc(...). The 690 KB PSRAM block and the scratch buffer are lost until reboot, unlike a true deferred free.
results.reasoning: This is the recorded outcome of 09-16 finding 13.6 (theme B fix note: 'Radio: counts tasks at creation, no longer forces the count to 0, leaks on timeout'; worker.h policy 'leaks, never frees'), and the comment at radio.c:433 states it. The claim is accurate that radio_start's memset (418) and the new s_rs.ext allocation (422) then drop the old pointers, so about 690 KB of PSRAM stays lost after the task exits. It needs a DNS/TLS stall that outlasts the 7 s wait. The only thing not in the 09-16 notes is that the blocks could be reclaimed on the next start.
results.fix_sketch: Optional refinement: radio_start already proves s_ntasks == 0 at line 417, so it can free a non-NULL rd.ring and s_rs.ext before the memset.

results.title: looper_bounce re-reads volatile t->len for the modulo; audio task can zero it (divide by zero)
results.claim: looper_bounce() (UI task) re-reads the volatile t->len after checking it is non-zero, while the audio task can zero it (apply_cmd re-arm on a TR1 press, or cmd_clear). The bounce runs for a long time over up to 4x8 s of audio with float SVF.
results.scenario: Bounce with a track in LP_STOP while TR1 is pressed on the selected track (or cmd_clear runs). apply_cmd sets t->len = 0 between the 'if (t->len == 0 ...) continue' test at line 400 and the modulo at line 401. On Xtensa the integer divide by zero raises an exception and the module panics. The window is a few instructions per sample, so the trigger is unlikely.
results.reasoning: t->len is volatile (looper_priv.h:26), so lines 400 and 401 are two separate reads. The bounce runs on the UI task (core 0, ui.c:349) for around a second while the audio task (core 1) keeps running apply_cmd: a TR1 edge on the selected track in LP_STOP sets t->len = 0 (looper.c:131), and TR1 is a jack, so a patched gate fires it without the frozen UI. A zero landing between the two reads makes 'j % t->len' a remu by zero, which panics on the ESP32. cmd_clear is never set anywhere, so the TR1 re-arm is the only trigger; not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Snapshot each contributing track's len (and vol/f/q) into locals in the gather pass at 380-386 and use only those locals in the inner loop. Buffers are always LP_BUF_FRAMES long, so reading a track that re-armed mid-bounce is memory-safe.

results.title: slicer_build_ot bounds its loop on volatile sl.n_slices re-read after the <=64 check
results.claim: slicer_build_ot() checks sl.n_slices <= SL_OT_SLICES once, then re-reads the volatile sl.n_slices on every loop iteration while writing into the 832-byte buffer (also checked in slicer_web.c). The reader task can change it concurrently via reslice or load.
results.scenario: GET /slicer/ot runs on the httpd task with 64 slices. A panel reslice or transient-mode change makes the reader task's recompute_slices raise sl.n_slices to up to 128 during the loop. The loop then writes slices past out[832] on the httpd stack (i*12 up to 1524 bytes), smashing the stack. The window is microseconds, so it is very unlikely.
results.reasoning: The defect is in the code: n_slices is volatile (slicer_priv.h:72), checked once at 115 and re-read every iteration at 137, while the reader task (unpinned, prio 6, above httpd's 5) can store up to 128 from recompute_grid/pick_transients (slicer.c:37, 88). At 128 the loop writes to offset 58 + 127*12 + 12 = 1594 of the 832-byte buf on the httpd stack (slicer_web.c:41). What I could not establish is a realistic trigger: the store has to land inside a loop lasting a few microseconds, and reslices come only from panel edits or a load, so a panel detent must coincide with a web .OT download to that precision. The handler also ignores sl.loading, so a download during a load or reslice can return a half-updated slice map, which is far more likely than the overrun.
results.fix_sketch: Read sl.n_slices once into a local at the top of slicer_build_ot and use it for the range check, the loop bound and the count field. Have slicer_ot_get_handler refuse (409 or 503) while sl.loading is set.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: components/audio/recording.c, audio.c, components/drivers/{gpio,spi_per,storage,i2s_per}.c, components/util/{fileio,preset_store,sample_ram,sample_list_recent,sampfile,sampfile_int.h,sampimport,sampplay,mp3,sd_lock,timer_utils}.c, components/util/include/worker.h, components/machine/machine_core.c, components/machine_granular/granular.c, components/machine_glitch/glitch.c, components/machine_radio/radio.c, machine_freesound/fs_machine.c, fs_priv.h, components/freesound/freesound.c (dead code; freesoundGetInstance has no callers), components/rest-api/rest-api.c (all but some tail handlers skimmed), components/machine_looper/looper.c and looper_web.c, components/machine_editor/editor.c lines 1-330, components/menu/setup_menu.c, menu_config.c. Read in part: sampler3.c 1-620, slicer.c 20-470 and 520-575, deck.c 55-300 and some loop_toggle code, tape.c 1-140, 596-1000, ui.c 60-345, menu.c 340-420 and 560-760.

Mechanical sweeps run over all 188 in-scope .c/.h files:
- (a) zero-tick sleeps: found sampplay.c, audio.c:530, espnow_probe.c and the remote-trig deadline. timer_utils delays are >=250 ms.
- (b) FatFS versus VFS path conventions: no violations.
- (c) lock scan: only the looper save and the unlocked sample_resolve/stat loops were real. sample_resolve() stats 7x4 paths with no lock and most callers do not hold it. I judged that low consequence because FatFS serialises internally, so I did not list it separately.
- (d) PSRAM-to-SD: sampimport, fs_machine and freesound found. writeJSONFile is PSRAM-fed through the cJSON hook in ui.c and is folded into the fileio finding.
- (e) buffer sizing: path and id buffers checked against 31+5+prefix and are fine. All unbounded strcpy/sprintf sites checked: only dead code (menu_config loadPresetConfig, freesound.c) is unsafe.
- (f) enum-parallel arrays: SF_DIRS, SF_DIRS_F, sample_ram dirs, sample_list_recent, rest-api jdirs/fdirs/del/mv/rn/peaks and sampimport dirs all have 7 entries with static asserts or literals that match. All setup_menu_t.n literals (slicer 9, tracker 9, deck 13) match their item tables.
- (g) pinned file tasks: only dead code (mp3.c decodeMP3File, freesound.c instance_request). The UI task ui_ev_loop is pinned to core 0 and does SD I/O by design, which I treated as not a violation.
- (h) only a bare INTERNAL|8BIT alloc in the screenshot path, fine.
- (i) found the static prev_trig pattern.
- (j) no _audio_status reads outside audio.c.

Dropped as low value: radio ring_write has no generation check (a few ms of old-station audio and a racy wpos after a fast station change); drop_ot ignores f_write results; the importer skips any file starting with 'IMP' (real user samples like IMPACT.WAV never convert); /ice/state returns the icecast password unauthenticated; granular/looper preset density and bars are unclamped (a huge value stalls the audio task); audio_task's ctrlData is uninitialised until the first ULP sample; CONFIG.JSN read-modify-write races between tasks.

Not reached, or only skimmed: deck.c, dualdeck.c, instsampler.c, drum.c, tracker.c and synth.c processing and UI paths, the *_menu.c files, beatlisten.c, reverb.c, fxrack.c, tuner.c, wifi.c, menu.c beyond the parts above, menutft.c, cvmtx.c. I found no sibling SD or name bugs in the parts I saw."

results.title: Sampler3 reverse read flips in place without a swap (dst == stage)
results.claim: read_playback_frames() reverses a chunk by copying stage into dst, but every caller (rebuild_head, loop-start cache, ring top-up) passes the SAME buffer for dst and stage. That makes the reversal an in-place copy without a swap.
results.scenario: Reverse is on and a chunk of got=4096 frames is read. The first 2048 output frames are the correctly reversed second half. For i>=2048 the source slots were already overwritten, so the second half comes out in forward order. The audible result is half-reversed, stuttering audio every 4096 frames (head, loop cache and ring alike). The two-half pattern repeats per chunk.
results.reasoning: All four call sites (sampler3.c:107, 126, 325, 375) pass stage as both dst and stage with want <= 4096, so got_total is 0 and the loop at 77-80 overwrites its own source. Working it through gives [a(n-1)..a(n/2), a(n/2)..a(n-1)]: the second half of each file chunk plays backward then forward, and the first half is never heard. Present since 3a6298c (07-12); not in the 09-16 review (8.4 is a different reverse bug).
results.fix_sketch: Reverse stage in place with a two-index frame swap (i<j), exactly as editor.c span_rev does at 188-192, then memcpy to dst only if dst != stage. Put that swap in one shared helper next to sampfile_read and use it from sampler3 and slicer.

results.title: Slicer reverse read has the same in-place non-swap flip
results.claim: read_slice_frames() has the same in-place reverse bug (copied from sampler3). build_heads() and the tail streamer both call it with dst == stage.
results.scenario: Slicer with Reverse on: the slice head and every 4096-frame tail chunk come out with only the first half reversed. The second half is forward, so reversed slices are garbled.
results.reasoning: build_heads (slicer.c:201) and the tail streamer (slicer.c:295) both call read_slice_frames with dst == stage; SL_HEAD_FRAMES 3528 < SL_CHUNK 4096, so each call is one pass with got_total 0. The loop at 130-133 reads slots it has already overwritten, so every head and every tail chunk is half reversed, half forward. Reverse is a Setup row (slicer_menu.c:355) and a preset key (slicer.c:678).
results.fix_sketch: Same fix as #0: share one in-place frame-swap helper (the editor.c:188-192 loop) and call it on stage before the existing copy to heads/ring.

results.title: sampplay reader busy-spins on a full ring (pdMS_TO_TICKS(5) == 0)
results.claim: pdMS_TO_TICKS(5) is 0 at CONFIG_FREERTOS_HZ=100, so vTaskDelay(0) just yields. The reader task (prio 4, unpinned) therefore never blocks once the ring is nearly full, which is its steady state. It also still calls fill_once() each pass, doing tiny SD reads under sd_lock for whatever space is left.
results.scenario: Freesound audition (or any sampplay user) is playing and the ring is nearly full. The reader loops flat out at prio 4: it takes mx, reads a few frames under sd_lock, gives back, yields. It starves lower-priority tasks and the idle task on its core. Idle cleanup of self-deleted task stacks stalls, so a later 40 KB fs_pipeline allocation can fail. It also hammers sd_lock and competes with other SD users.
results.reasoning: pdMS_TO_TICKS(5) is 5*100/1000 = 0, so the full-ring branch is vTaskDelay(0), and a full ring is the steady state whenever f && playing. fill_once (sampplay.c:49-55) reads any space below SP_CHUNK, so each 64-frame drain triggers a 256-byte fseek+read under sd_lock instead of 1024-frame bursts. It breaks the CLAUDE.md 'Sleep at least one tick' rule; added in 6737be2 (09-12) and not listed on 09-16. The finder's idle-cleanup/40 KB alloc chain is not shown: idle WDT checks are off and the other core's idle still runs, so the class is starvation plus dribble reads, not a hang.
results.fix_sketch: Use vTaskDelay(1) in both branches, and in fill_once return unless space >= SP_CHUNK (or the read finishes the loop span), like sampler3's 'no dribble reads' guard.

results.title: :8000 WAV broadcast loop busy-spins between audio blocks (pdMS_TO_TICKS(8) == 0)
results.claim: The :8000 WAV broadcast loop idles with pdMS_TO_TICKS(8), which is 0 ticks (vTaskDelay(0) only yields). When the ring is empty, which is almost always because the audio task supplies only 64 frames per 1.45 ms, the prio-5 bc_srv task busy-spins.
results.scenario: Enable broadcast and connect a client to http://<ip>:8000/ (WAV). bc_srv spins at 100% CPU at prio 5 for as long as the client stays connected. It starves lower-priority tasks and the idle task on its core (sampler readers at prio 4, radio stream, etc.) and competes with httpd. Audio dropouts and stalled SD readers follow.
results.reasoning: pdMS_TO_TICKS(8) is 0 ticks, so with a WAV client connected the prio-5 unpinned bc_srv task (audio.c:776) spins whenever the ring is empty and sends 64-frame packets per block. This breaks the CLAUDE.md 'Sleep at least one tick' rule; 09-16 finding 1.5 covers the same loop for a different defect (no s_bc_srv_run check). Over-stated: streaming readers are prio 6 and httpd is prio 5 (rest-api.c:2688), so only prio-4 workers (sampplay, editor jobs, dd_an) and one core's idle lose time.
results.fix_sketch: Change to vTaskDelay(1), as the MP3 path already does at audio.c:411 with pdMS_TO_TICKS(10). One tick accumulates about 441 frames, well inside the 1024-frame sbuf.

results.title: ESP-NOW probe spins flat out for hz > 100 (period < 10 ms is 0 ticks)
results.claim: period_ms = 1000/hz is clamped only to >=1. For hz 101..500 it is 2..9 ms, which is 0 ticks at 100 Hz, so vTaskDelay(0) yields and the task spins.
results.scenario: POST /espnow?hz=200 (the handler accepts up to 500). The prio-5 espnow_probe task calls esp_now_send in a tight loop with no blocking, floods the radio and WiFi queue, and starves lower-priority tasks. The audio-coexistence spike is then measured against a runaway sender rather than the requested rate.
results.reasoning: hz 101..500 gives period_ms 9..2, which pdMS_TO_TICKS turns into 0, so the prio-5 task (espnow_probe.c:87) loops on esp_now_send with no blocking; set_hz clamps only to 500 and the REST handler (rest-api.c:1902) adds no clamp. hz 51..99 also all run at 100 Hz. It is measurement scaffolding and tools/bench/espnow_cost.py only uses 0/25/100, so the recorded spike result is unaffected; only a hand-posted hz above 100 hits it.
results.fix_sketch: Clamp hz to configTICK_RATE_HZ in espnow_probe_set_hz and floor the delay at one tick (ticks = pdMS_TO_TICKS(period_ms); if (ticks < 1) ticks = 1). Echo the clamped hz in the POST reply.

results.title: /remote/trig with ms 5..9 never asserts the soft gate
results.claim: The REST handler accepts ms>=5 (it clamps `if (ms < 5) ms = 5;`), but pdMS_TO_TICKS(5..9) is 0. The deadline equals now, and the audio task tests `now < s_remote_trig_until[t]`, which is false.
results.scenario: POST /remote/trig?t=1&ms=5 (short gate pulse from a web script or bench rig): the handler answers ok:true with ms=5, but the soft gate never asserts and the machine never sees the trigger. For ms 10..19 the pulse length is 0..10 ms depending on tick phase.
results.reasoning: The handler clamps ms to >= 5 (rest-api.c:1728) and pdMS_TO_TICKS(5..9) is 0, so until == now and the audio task's 'now < until' test (audio.c:629-630) is false; ms 10..19 gives 0..10 ms and can miss a block. The web page only sends ms=5 as the RELEASE of a hold (index.html:2698), where an immediate deadline is what it wants, and the pulse button defaults to 40. So only a script asking for a fresh 5..9 ms pulse is affected, and the reply's now == until shows it.
results.fix_sketch: In audio_remote_trig, floor the tick count at 2 so a pulse always spans at least one audio block. The web release still works: the gate drops 10-20 ms later with no new edge.

results.title: Reader tasks never NULL-check their 16 KB DMA staging buffers
results.claim: The reader task allocates its 16 KB contiguous internal DMA staging buffer (and a tail buffer) and never checks for NULL. The same pattern is at dualdeck.c:240-241 (chunk, tail), sampler3.c:142 (stage) and slicer.c:219 (stage). The project notes say internal RAM is scarce and the largest free block is what fails.
results.scenario: Switch to Deck/DoubleDecker/Sampler3/Slicer while WiFi, broadcast or Radio have fragmented the internal heap, so no 16 KB block is free. The reader task starts anyway and the first track load calls sampfile_read(f, &sfl, NULL, ...). fread into NULL gives LoadProhibited and the whole module reboots.
results.reasoning: deck.c:124-125, dualdeck.c:240-241, sampler3.c:142 and slicer.c:219 allocate MALLOC_CAP_DMA buffers with no check, then pass them to sampfile_read (deck.c:204), which is a bare fread into dst (sampfile.c:29-35); a NULL buffer faults on the first track load. worker_spawn only needs a 4 KB stack, so it can succeed while a contiguous 16 KB block is missing; the 09-16 bench note records the largest internal block dipping to 10 KB. Not recorded on 09-16 (6.10 covers rest-api mallocs only). The fault would be a store to NULL, not LoadProhibited.
results.fix_sketch: Allocate the staging buffers in each machine's start() before worker_spawn and return failure if either is NULL, so machine_activate's existing Stub fallback takes over. Hand them to the reader and free them on the worker_stop success path.

results.title: Bootlogo header check does misaligned 32-bit loads
results.reasoning: The ESP32 LX6 core does unaligned loads in hardware and raises no exception: XCHAL_UNALIGNED_LOAD_EXCEPTION 0 and XCHAL_UNALIGNED_LOAD_HW 1 at esp-idf-v4.3/components/xtensa/esp32/include/xtensa/config/core-isa.h:171-174. The LoadStoreAlignment trap the finder describes is the ESP8266 behaviour. The loads at buf+10/18/22/30 are non-portable style only; a valid upload passes the check and is written.

results.title: writeJSONFile truncates in place, unchecked; interrupted AUTOSAVE/CONFIG write loses state
results.claim: writeJSONFile truncates the target and then writes the cJSON_Print buffer in place, with no temp+rename. fwrite and fclose results are unchecked. The buffer is also PSRAM-resident, because ui.c installs a PSRAM-first cJSON malloc hook and the SD bounce path can fail with NO_MEM. Every CONFIG.JSN and AUTOSAVE.JSN write goes through this.
results.scenario: Power cut or a failed write during the AUTOSAVE.JSN rewrite leaves a truncated file. readJSONFileAsCJSON then returns NULL (parse fail), and autosave_now() sees `getFileSize("/sdcard/AUTOSAVE.JSN") > 2`, logs 'read failed on existing file' and skips the save on every later autosave. No machine can persist state until the file is deleted by hand. A truncated CONFIG.JSN instead fails validateConfig at boot, and createConfigFile() silently resets WiFi credentials and the API key.
results.reasoning: fopen("wb") truncates the live file and the fwrite/fclose results are ignored (fileio.c:319-330); no temp+rename. A power-off inside the write leaves a 0-byte file: autosave_now then mints a fresh root (menu.c:707-713) and every other machine's saved state is gone, and a 0-byte or truncated CONFIG.JSN fails validateConfig so createConfigFile resets ssid/passwd/apikey to placeholders (fileio.c:138-140, 49-54). A short write that still closes (card full) leaves a truncated file over 2 bytes, and the guard at menu.c:708-711 then skips every later autosave until the file is deleted by hand. Not in the 09-16 review (3.11 and 6.9 are other defects); the print buffer is PSRAM-first (ui.c:316-324), so the write also depends on the SDMMC bounce.
results.fix_sketch: In writeJSONFile write to a sibling temp file under the same sd_lock, check fwrite == len and fclose == 0, then publish with the backup/rename/restore sequence imp_publish() already uses in sampimport.c; on any failure keep the old file. Have readJSONFileAsCJSON fall back to the backup when the main file is missing or empty.

results.title: REST name parameters allow '..' traversal to CONFIG.JSN
results.reasoning: FatFS rejects dot segments on this build: FF_FS_RPATH is 0 (esp-idf-v4.3 components/fatfs/src/ffconf.h:171) and LFN is on, so create_name strips the trailing dots of '..' and returns FR_INVALID_NAME (components/fatfs/src/ff.c:2869-2875). That covers VFS fopen/stat/remove/rename and raw f_open alike, so the DELETE, /files/raw and /drop_sample scenarios against CONFIG.JSN all fail. A bare '/' only reaches subfolders of usr/ with the fixed .RAW/.WAV/.AIF/.AIFF/.JSN/.OT extensions, which the same unauthenticated API already lets any client read or delete.

results.title: sample_name_id truncates stems over 31 chars and still lists them
results.claim: sample_name_id() truncates an over-long stem to 31 chars and still returns true. LFN is on (FATFS_MAX_LFN=64), so files with 32..60 char stems can exist (copied in from a computer).
results.scenario: A card has 'My_Very_Long_Field_Recording_Name_01.wav'. The sample browsers (sample_list*, folder counts) list the 31-char truncated id. Loading it fails because sample_resolve can't find '<trunc>.RAW/.WAV' ('cannot open'), and two files sharing a 31-char prefix collapse into one entry. rest-api's /files skips such names, so the panel and web disagree.
results.reasoning: keep is clamped to id_len-1 and the function returns true (sampfile.c:147-151), so sample_list_dir, the folder counts and sample_list_recent (sample_ram.c:42, :59; sample_list_recent.c:43) list a 31-char id for a file whose stem is 32..64 chars (FATFS_MAX_LFN=64). sample_resolve builds '<trunc>.RAW/.WAV' paths that do not exist (sampfile.c:85-95), so the entry can never load, and two files sharing a 31-char prefix dedup into one row. The web index skips such names (rest-api.c:237), so panel and web disagree. Only reachable by copying long-named files onto the card from a computer, since upload and rename both cap the length.
results.fix_sketch: Return false from sample_name_id when the stem does not fit (keep >= id_len), matching the skip at rest-api.c:237, so un-addressable files are not listed. The only other caller (files_raw_handler) passes a 32-byte name and is unaffected.

results.title: Import and Freesound write PSRAM buffers to SD through the SDMMC bounce path
results.claim: The converted PCM buffers (pcm and res) are PSRAM and are written straight to SD. SDMMC DMA cannot target PSRAM, so the driver must bounce every sector through a temporary DMA allocation, which can fail with NO_MEM. The same shape appears at fs_machine.c:275 (`f_write(&fmp3, body + off, ...)`, body in PSRAM) and freesound.c:333.
results.scenario: The importer or Freesound pipeline runs while internal DMA RAM is tight (the code itself documents a ~10 KB largest block in this situation). The write returns short or FR_DISK_ERR and the conversion or download fails (for Freesound, 'SD write failed'). It is slow even when it works, because it goes one sector at a time.
results.reasoning: pcm/res are MALLOC_CAP_SPIRAM (sampimport.c:228-231) and body is PSRAM (fs_machine.c:239, :275), so sdmmc_write_sectors allocates a 512-byte DMA buffer per write and sends one sector at a time (esp-idf-v4.3 components/sdmmc/sdmmc_cmd.c:371-392). It is not data loss: both write results are checked (sampimport.c:248, fs_machine.c:277-281) and the source is only removed after a successful publish, so the worst case is a cleanly reported failed conversion or download. Missing: whether a 512-byte DMA block can actually be unavailable right after the same function was granted a 2 KB or larger DMA buffer. freesound.c:333 is legacy code only reached from Sampler2 and is out of scope.
results.fix_sketch: In convert_pcm copy each output burst through the existing internal `raw` DMA staging buffer (chunk*8 bytes) before fwrite, so the write is a direct multi-block DMA transfer. Low priority; the Freesound body write is documented as deliberate buffering (fs_machine.c:224-235) and can stay.

results.title: samp_import_file has no mutual exclusion between the import scan and Freesound
results.claim: samp_import_file() uses a fixed per-directory temp name (IMPNEW.TMP, and IMPMP3.TMP for mp3). It is called both from the background import task and directly from the Freesound pipeline (fs_machine.c:353) with no mutual exclusion; samp_import_busy only guards the scan task.
results.scenario: A web upload starts the importer (rest-api.c:1478) while a Freesound download is converting into usr/. Both open /sdcard/usr/IMPNEW.TMP with 'wb' and interleave writes, so one of the published .WAV files is corrupt. The scan can also pick up and delete the partially downloaded usr/<name>.mp3. A second upload while busy returns -1 silently, so a file that lands after the scan passed its folder is never converted.
results.reasoning: This is 09-16 finding 3.4, which appears in themes G/H but in no fix tier and not in Watch, and the code is unchanged: samp_import_file takes no lock, and fs_pipeline (fs_machine.c:353) and import_task (sampimport.c:428) both call it. The finder's interleaved-write corruption does not happen in the same folder, because CONFIG_FATFS_FS_LOCK=5 makes the second open of IMPNEW.TMP/IMPMP3.TMP fail with FR_LOCKED; the second conversion fails instead (Freesound reports 'convert failed' and deletes its download, or an uploaded MP3 stays as a .RAW that plays as noise). When the scan decodes an MP3 in another pool folder at the same time, both tasks share the global `input` in mp3.c:29 (malloc at :296, free at :305), giving a use-after-free and a double free. A busy samp_import_start from drop_sample is also ignored (rest-api.c:1478), so an upload arriving after the scan passed usr/ is not converted.
results.fix_sketch: Serialise samp_import_file with one static mutex in sampimport.c so the scan task and the Freesound pipeline queue behind each other, and make mp3.c's `input` a local passed into decode(). Have drop_sample set a rescan flag when samp_import_start returns busy, and let import_task loop once more when it is set.

results.title: looper_save_track does mkdir/fopen/fwrite/fclose without sd_lock
results.claim: looper_save_track() does mkdir, sample_next_index, fopen, every fwrite and fclose without sd_lock (only the JSON sidecar is locked inside writeJSONFile). It runs on the UI task or the /looper/save worker at prio 5.
results.scenario: Saving a long loop writes the whole file as unlocked back-to-back bursts while httpd, autosave or the recorder hold or want the bus. The SD bus house rule (every burst under sd_lock with courtesy gaps) is bypassed, so other SD users see unpaced contention and long stalls.
results.reasoning: The defect is there: mkdir (looper.c:309), fopen (:316), every fwrite (:333), sampwav_finish and fclose (:337-338) run outside sd_lock, against the CLAUDE.md rule that every SD burst holds it; only sample_next_index and writeJSONFile lock internally. No corruption path can be traced from reading, because FatFS is reentrant here (FF_FS_REENTRANT 1, ffconf.h:287) and each call takes the volume mutex; what remains is an unpaced write loop with no courtesy gap that needs a concurrent SD user (web file list or upload, a bounce recording, autosave during a web save) to matter. Looper itself runs no SD reader tasks. The same unlocked block is the subject of 11.8 (Watch) from the duplicate-filename angle.
results.fix_sketch: Wrap mkdir + sample_next_index + fopen + sampwav_start in one sd_lock_take/give (this also closes 11.8), take the lock around each fwrite chunk with vTaskDelay(1) between bursts as convert_pcm does (sampimport.c:245-250), and lock sampwav_finish + fclose. Use a larger DMA chunk so the courtesy gap does not stretch a long save.

results.title: Function-static prev_trig not re-seeded in start() fires a phantom trigger
results.reasoning: In the finder's scenario the static holds 0x03, which is exactly what a re-seed in start() would set (drum.c:158), so the first block with a gate held low fires the same falling edge either way (sampler3.c:593, slicer.c:466, looper.c:156, glitch.c:108). That edge comes from a gate that really is asserted, and seeding idle-high is the documented convention (CLAUDE.md, Trig inputs: 'seed the previous state to idle-high (0x03)'). The static only differs from a re-seed when it was left low, and then it suppresses an edge rather than inventing one, which the finder also notes is fine.

chunks.coverage_notes:
Read in full: components/fxrack/fxrack.c, components/menu/cvmtx.c, components/machine_synth/synth.c, components/machine_instsampler/instsampler.c, components/machine_drumsampler/drum.c, components/machine_tape/tape.c, components/machine_granular/granular.c. I read preset_store.c (the save path and the list/load code) and the autosave and bind code in menu.c (lines ~260-330, 590-740, 738-950). In rest-api.c I read the /remote/params GET and POST handlers, in index.html the rpApply/rpLoad flow, and in fileio.c the readJSONFileAsCJSON and writeJSONFile functions.

Read only preset_save and preset_load plus the code they call, not the whole file: machine_slicer/slicer.c (~20-330 and 560-708), machine_sampler3/sampler3.c (470-540, 760-830, 1130-1353), machine_deck/deck.c (985-1122), machine_dualdeck/dualdeck.c (1270-1386), machine_glitch/glitch.c, machine_looper/looper.c (400-485), machine_tracker/tracker.c (860-965), and the freesound and radio preset functions. Also read: editor.c preset stubs (they do nothing), reverb.c mode/mix setters, fxdelay.c, flanger.c init, util/lfo.c, util/sample_ram.c sample_load, and the resolvers in sampfile.c and sampfile_f.c.

Not read in full: the machine *_menu.c files, the remaining ~2000 lines of rest-api.c, the rest of menu.c, the deck/dualdeck/sampler3/slicer/tracker/looper/glitch process() bodies beyond the parts named above, and preset_store.c lines 1-55 (seen only in the truncated output). Other C files in the machine components were read only as far as tracing calls from the preset code needed.

Dropped or judged non-findings:
- Contrived values only reachable with 1e999 or inf JSON (Keys lfo_rate NaN latching in lfo phase, Synth fm_ratio inf).
- Glitch division shifts (UB but no divide-by-zero on Xtensa).
- Keys and Synth unclamped envelope sus, which only produces clamped loud or negative output.
- A pre-parse memory-exhaustion DoS from an 8 KB array body in /remote/params.
- Truncated 11-char preset ids in preset_store_list for long LFN names, and the idx 999 overwrite in preset_store_save.
- Tape's tape_set_len_sel discarding an unsaved take on an lsel change.
- Keys' 'ts' key being written but never read (documented as read-only).

I did not confirm the trigger for the Keys in-place zone reload without a block wait, which only causes a one-block glitch.

results.title: Granular preset_load takes density unclamped; a huge value stalls the audio task
results.claim: granular_preset_load takes density (and grain_ms, spray, spread) straight from JSON with no clamp. The menu limits density to 1..120, but the loader does not.
results.scenario: POST /remote/params {"density":2000000000}, or a hand-edited AUTOSAVE.JSN. In granular_process, spawn_per_sample = density/44100 is about 45000, so `while (gr.spawn_phase >= 1.0f) { ...spawn_grain(); }` runs about 2.9M times per 64-frame block. The audio task overruns for seconds and the task WDT resets the unit. The UI task's 2 s autosave debounce writes the bad value to AUTOSAVE.JSN. The next boot loads it in menuMachineBindNow and resets again, giving a boot loop until the card is edited. A negative density sends spawn_phase hugely negative, so the machine is silent until it is reloaded.
results.reasoning: granular.c:254-257 store grain_ms/density/spray/spread with no clamp (the menu clamps 1..120 at granular_menu.c:133), and the spawn loop at granular.c:175 then runs density*32/44100 times per block, so values above roughly 1e5-1e6 overrun the 1.45 ms budget and INT_MAX means over a million spawn_grain calls per block. The bad value is autosaved (menu.c:626 autosave_kick) and comes back on the next boot. The WDT reset and boot loop are wrong: sdkconfig:417-420 has TASK_WDT panic and both idle checks off, and audio is pinned to core 1 while UI and httpd sit on core 0 (audio.c:760, ui.c:349, rest-api.c:2687), so the unit stays reachable and one Density detent, a K8 move or a sane POST recovers it. Negative density does leave spawn_phase stuck hugely negative until the machine restarts.
results.prior_ref: 12.6 (same class, Glitch division; this one not recorded)
results.fix_sketch: Clamp in granular_preset_load to the same ranges the menu uses (grain_ms 10..500, density 1..120, spray/spread 0..100). Optionally cap spawns per block in granular_process and reset spawn_phase when it is out of 0..1.

results.title: AUTOSAVE.JSN is rewritten in place with an unchecked write; a bad file is never replaced
results.claim: AUTOSAVE.JSN is rewritten in place. writeJSONFile does fopen("wb"), which truncates, then fwrite, with no temp file or rename and no fwrite check. A power cut or a full card leaves a truncated, unparseable file. autosave_now then treats every later save as 'read failed on existing file' and skips it.
results.scenario: The rack is switched off within the ~64 ms write window that follows any edit, or the card fills mid-write. AUTOSAVE.JSN is left as a JSON prefix. On the next boot readJSONFileAsCJSON returns NULL, so every machine loads defaults. From then on every autosave_now sees a NULL read with size > 2, logs 'skip (won't clobber)' and returns. No machine's state ever persists again until someone deletes the file by hand.
results.reasoning: writeJSONFile (fileio.c:311) does fopen("wb") + fwrite with no result check and no temp/rename, and autosave_now (menu.c:706-712) skips every save while the file is larger than 2 bytes but unparseable, so a short write (card full, I/O error) does stop all persistence until the file is deleted. The power-cut scenario differs from the claim: FatFS FA_CREATE_ALWAYS commits size 0 first and only writes the real size at close, so a cut mid-write leaves a 0-byte file. That takes the `> 2` false path: every machine boots on defaults and the next save recreates the file with only the active machine, so all other machines' state is lost but saving continues. Not recorded on 09-16.
results.fix_sketch: Write to a temp file under sd_lock, check fwrite/fclose, then remove+rename over the target (the pattern the module upload in rest-api.c and sampimport already use). In autosave_now, when the read fails with a parse error rather than an allocation failure, replace the file instead of skipping forever.

results.title: fxrack_load sets both FX slots Off when the node has no "fxsl" (partial /remote/params)
results.claim: fxrack_load always runs the legacy-migration branch when the node has no "fxsl" array. That branch sets both generic FX slots to Off and slot_gc then frees the delay and flanger slabs. /remote/params is documented as a partial preset, and Keys, Synth, Tape and Drums all call fxrack_load unconditionally.
results.scenario: With Keys, Synth, Tape or Drums running with Delay in FX1, POST /remote/params {"cut":800} (the kind of write the bench scripts make) or any body without "fxsl". The FX slots go to Off, the ~690 KB delay slab is freed, and the next autosave persists the empty rack. The user's FX are silently lost by an unrelated single-key write.
results.reasoning: With no "fxsl" array the else branch at fxrack.c:423-430 runs the legacy migration, finds no legacy keys, sets both slots Off, and slot_gc at :482 frees the delay/flanger slabs; Keys, Synth, Tape and Drums all call it unconditionally (instsampler.c:800, synth.c:344, tape.c:1089, drum.c:772) and EV_REMOTE_PRESET then arms the autosave. The web page always posts the full readback including fxsl, so only partial posts hit it: tools/bench/mix_sweep.py posts {"rvmx":..} alone and rig.py:256 documents the body as a partial preset. The 5.2 fix applied exactly this partial-update rule to cvmtx_load (cvmtx.c:287) but not to the rack.
results.fix_sketch: In fxrack_load, touch rk->slot[] only when "fxsl" is an array or at least one legacy key (od/flg/trem/dly) is present; otherwise leave the slots as they are, mirroring cvmtx_load's 'no matrix = partial update' rule.

results.title: Web Apply reloads the sample on Slicer, Granular, Drums, Synth and Keys every time
results.claim: Several loaders reload the sample on every preset_load, with no check for 'same as loaded'. The web Remote page's Apply posts the full state (rpApply sends the whole readback), so every Apply triggers a full reload. Deck, DoubleDecker, Tracker and Sampler3 guard against this with strcmp against the current name. The others do not.
results.scenario: On the Slicer, change one Setup value in the web page and press Apply. slicer_load sets loading and playing=false and forces the reader to redo the envelope scan and head build, about 1.5 min per 8 min of audio, with the machine muted. Selection and cur reset to 0. The same happens in granular_preset_load (granular.c:258, granular_load), drum_preset_load (drum.c:861, every pad and B layer reloaded and stopped), synth_preset_load (synth.c:332, synth_load_wave under machine_block_wait) and keys_preset_load (zones cleared and reloaded, instsampler.c:751). Touching any one parameter drops the audio.
results.reasoning: rpApply (index.html:2633-2651) posts the whole readback including the sample name, and slicer_preset_load calls slicer_load unconditionally; slicer_load (slicer.c:633) sets loading and playing=false, and the reader (slicer.c:225-258) redoes scan_file, the .ot parse and build_heads and resets cur/sel. The same unguarded reload is in granular.c:258, drum.c:860-863, synth.c:332 and instsampler.c:749-756 (clear all zones, reverb forced off, every zone reloaded). Deck, DoubleDecker, Sampler3 and Tracker guard with strcmp (deck.c:1097, dualdeck.c:1356, sampler3.c:1328, tracker.c:939). Apply sits on the CV matrix, FX and Advanced cards, so this is ordinary web use.
results.fix_sketch: Add the strcmp-against-current-name guard the decks and Sampler3 already use to each loader. On Slicer call slicer_reslice() instead when only slices/transient/sens changed; on Keys skip the clear+reload when the zones array names match the loaded zones and just apply root/fn/loop.

results.title: A zone or pad that fails to load is dropped from the next autosave (Keys and Drums)
results.claim: When a zone fails to load (arena full, PSRAM ladder short, file missing), keys_preset_load skips it. preset_save only writes zones with frames != 0, so the next autosave permanently drops that zone from the multisample. Drums has the same loss: drum_load_layer blanks the stored name on failure (drum.c:677 `if (n == 0) { L->sample[0] = 0; return -1; }`, and on alloc failure at drum.c:672).
results.scenario: Keys autosave holds 5 zones. After a reboot PSRAM is fragmented and the arena ladder drops to 750000 frames. Only 4 zones load (the file's own comment records PAT_001 restoring 4 of 5). Any encoder touch arms the autosave, and AUTOSAVE.JSN now lists 4 zones for good. On Drums, a transient PSRAM failure or SD read error on pad N writes "s":"" for that pad, so the kit reference is gone.
results.reasoning: keys_preset_load skips a failed keys_load_zone_at with `continue` (arena full, load failed, no PSRAM), and keys_preset_save (instsampler.c:657-659) only writes zones below nzones with frames != 0, so the next encoder touch or machine switch rewrites the Keys entry without that zone. A zone truncated to the remaining arena room is kept, but its loop_end is clamped at :771 and saved that way. Drums is the same: drum_load_layer blanks L->sample on alloc or read failure (drum.c:672, :677) and preset_save writes it as "s":"" (drum.c:735/743). The arena ladder landing short is a documented ordinary condition, not only a fault; named PAT_ patch files are not affected, only the autosave.
results.fix_sketch: Keys: keep the names (SAMPLE_ID_LEN) and root/fn/loop of zones that failed during preset_load in a small pending list that keys_preset_save appends to "zones", cleared by Load Sample / Clear Zones. Drums: on a failed load keep L->sample with len 0 so "s"/"s2" round-trip and the next boot retries.

results.title: fxrack CV push is visible to fxrack_save and GET /remote/params from another core
results.claim: cv_push overwrites the live effect parameter for the whole stage call (delay, flanger and reverb stages take a large share of the 1.45 ms block). fxrack_save and GET /remote/params read the same fields from the UI or httpd task with no synchronisation. The 'menu + preset always see the un-modulated value' claim is only true between stages.
results.scenario: An FX param is patched to a moving CV, so its offset is non-zero. The 2 s autosave, or the web page's GET /remote/params, can read the pushed value. AUTOSAVE.JSN then stores base+CV for that instant. The web page keeps that snapshot in rpData, and the next Apply posts every FX field back through fxrack_load, so the modulated values become the new bases. Presets drift away from what the user dialled in.
results.reasoning: cv_push writes base+offset into the live field for the whole stage call on the audio task (core 1, audio.c:760), while fxrack_save reads the same fields unsynchronised from the UI task and httpd on core 0 (ui.c:349, rest-api.c:2687), so a save or readback landing inside a stage stores the modulated value, and a web Apply then posts it back as the new base. Scope is narrower than claimed: only Tape writes cv1/cv2/cv_rv (tape.c:360-364), so Keys, Synth and Drums never push. Not established from reading: how long each stage runs (the hit probability per save) and that Tape's rack is running with an FX destination routed at save time. The 09-16 note 'fxrack CV offsets restored correctly' covered the restore, not this cross-task read.
results.fix_sketch: Publish the pushed pointer and base in fxrack_t while a stage runs, and have fxrack_save and the menu fmt functions read through a small helper that returns the stashed base when the pointer matches. Alternatively pass the offset into the stage as a separate mod field so the shared base is never overwritten.

results.title: tracker_preset_load resets file, flags and CV matrix before reading a partial node
results.claim: tracker_preset_load resets loop, sync, amiga, show_text, loop_freeze and file, and calls cvmtx_reset_defaults, before reading the node. A partial /remote/params body therefore wipes the state that is not in the body. Freesound has the same pattern: fsnd_preset_load zeroes recents and saved via load_str_array when the keys are absent.
results.scenario: POST /remote/params {"loop":true} to Tracker with a module loaded and sync on. trk.file becomes "", sync goes false, and the CV matrix returns to defaults. preset_load does not unload the running module, but the next autosave stores file "", so the module is not restored after a reboot and sync and matrix settings are lost.
results.reasoning: tracker.c:914-920 set loop/sync/amiga/show_text/loop_freeze to defaults, zero trk.file and call cvmtx_reset_defaults before the `if (!node) return`, so a body without those keys wipes them; the running module keeps playing but the 2 s autosave stores file "" and the defaults. The web page posts the full readback so it is unaffected; partial posts do hit it (tools/bench/review_bench.py:361 posts {"file":..} alone and so resets sync and the matrix). Freesound is the same: load_str_array zeroes the count when the key is absent and autoplay falls back to true (fs_machine.c:796-798, :821-823). The 5.2 fix made cvmtx_load honour partial updates, but Tracker's unconditional reset bypasses it.
results.fix_sketch: Apply the defaults and cvmtx_reset_defaults only when node is NULL; otherwise overwrite only the keys present (cvmtx_load already resets when a stored matrix is present). In Freesound's load_str_array leave dst and the count untouched when the key is absent, and only change autoplay when the key exists.

results.title: Slicer preset_save omits the FX box, reverb mode and mix, and the OT/grid choice
results.claim: Slicer preset_save omits the FX box entirely. sl.fx_on, the DJ filter position fx_filt, fx_fmode, the reverb mode (fx_rv.mode) and the reverb mix (fx_rvmix) are user-editable on the Live page and in Setup rows 6 and 7, and none are persisted. The OT/grid mode choice is also only partly stored.
results.scenario: The user turns on the Slicer FX box, picks Hall reverb at 40% mix and sets a filter sweep. After a machine switch or reboot, bind loads AUTOSAVE, which has no FX keys. The reverb is Off, the mix is 0 and the box is off, even though the page showed those settings before.
results.reasoning: slicer_preset_save/load (slicer.c:656-684) carry no FX keys, although fx_on is toggled on the Live page (slicer_menu.c:287) and reverb mode and mix are Setup rows 6/7 (slicer_menu.c:357-367). slicer_start memsets sl and sets Room at 25% with the box off (slicer.c:384, :404-409), so after a switch or reboot the state is that default, not 'Off / 0' as the finding says, but the user's settings are lost all the same. ot_active is not stored either and is re-derived from the .ot file on every load (slicer.c:244), so a Grid choice on a sample with an .OT reverts. fx_filt is a knob (matrix ABS entry) and correctly needs no key; nothing in CLAUDE.md or the slicer-fx-v1 README says this is deliberate.
results.fix_sketch: Add "fx" (bool), "rv" and "rvmx" (the fxrack key names) and an "ot" mode key to slicer_preset_save, and restore them in slicer_preset_load with reverb_set_mode / reverb_set_mix, range-checked against RV_N_MODES and 0..1. Apply the stored OT choice after the reader's load instead of forcing ot_active from the file.

results.title: Drums preset omits knob-7 clockwise values (attack_ms, start_off, loop_ms)
results.claim: The knob 7 clockwise gestures set attack_ms, start_off and loop_ms (retrig length). These flag machine_state_dirty() and are shown on the Pads page, but drum_preset_save never writes them. Only decay_ms is written, and loading never restores them.
results.scenario: The user dials knob 7 clockwise on a pad in ATTACK, START or LOOP mode (for example 'start 40%'). The autosave fires but contains no such key. After a reboot or machine switch the pad plays from the top with no attack ramp and no stutter loop, so the sound the user built is silently different.
results.reasoning: process() sets attack_ms/start_off/loop_ms from knob 7 and flags machine_state_dirty() (drum.c:262-297), and the Pads page shows them (drum_menu.c:652-663), but drum_preset_save writes only dec/cw/reps/pit and drum_preset_load has no key for the three. drum_start memsets dr (drum.c:120), so after a reboot or machine switch they are 0 and return only when knob 7 is moved with that pad selected (takeover). CLAUDE.md states the intent that kits dialed in by knob autosave, and the sibling knob targets decay_ms and pitch_semi are saved. Not in the 09-16 review (chunk 9 reported nothing for Drums).
results.fix_sketch: In drum_preset_save add three per-pad keys next to "dec" (attack_ms, start_off, loop_ms); in drum_preset_load read them after "cw" with clamps to DR_ATTACK_MAX, DR_START_MAX and DR_LOOP_MIN_MS..DR_LOOP_MAX_MS (0 allowed). The existing cvmtx_rearm + knob_last=-1 already keeps the loaded values until the knob moves.

results.title: Granular preset omits position, pitch and level, which became stored values with takeover
results.claim: Granular preset_save omits gr.position (K6, the cloud position), gr.pitch_cv (K7) and gr.level. The matrix entries are ABS/takeover, and cvmtx_track flags machine_state_dirty() when they move, yet the saved JSON carries none of those values.
results.scenario: The user sets the cloud position and pitch by knob and the autosave triggers. AUTOSAVE.JSN records grain_ms, density, spray, spread and the sample name, but not position or pitch. On the next boot the cloud sits at position 0 and pitch 2048, not the previous values. The knob takeover only starts when the knob is moved, so the machine plays from the start of the sample until then.
results.reasoning: Since 15c1ead position/pitch_cv/level are written only when cvmtx_abs reports a live (moved) knob (granular.c:160-164); before that commit they were read straight from the knobs every block, so nothing needed saving. granular_preset_save/load (238-262) carry grain_ms/density/spray/spread/sample and the matrix only, and granular_start resets position=0, pitch_cv=2048, level=255. So after every boot or switch the cloud sits at the sample start at unity pitch regardless of the knob until it is moved past the 0.03 threshold, while cvmtx_track still flags the autosave for those moves. The load comment "knobs recapture against the loaded values" has no loaded value for these three; not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Add position, pitch_cv and level to granular_preset_save and read them clamped (0..4095, 0..4095, 0..255) in granular_preset_load before cvmtx_rearm. Alternatively mark them performance-only with gr.mtx.nodirty and seed from the assigned channel the way Tracker's loop-window seed does; saving matches what grain_ms/density already do.

results.title: Delay/flanger init loses defaults: Tape sync/div wiped on first use; zeroed autosave marks params set
results.claim: fxdelay_init (and flanger_init) zero the whole struct when keep.params is false, which wipes sync and div that a host set before first use. Tape's tape_start sets `tp.dly.sync = tp.flg.sync = tp.trem.sync = true;` with `tp.dly.div = 2` and `tp.flg.div = 4`, but never sets params, so the first slot_set(DLY or FLG) resets them to sync OFF and div 0.
results.scenario: On a fresh Tape session the user picks Delay in FX1 from the menu. The documented default of a tempo-synced 1/8 delay does not apply: sync is OFF and the time is the 375 ms default. Presets that store dlysy and dlydv mask this. A menu first use, or a preset without those keys, gets the wrong default.
results.reasoning: As claimed: tape_start sets dly/flg sync and div (tape.c:1014-1015) without params, so with no Tape entry in AUTOSAVE.JSN (preset_load(NULL), menu.c:913-916) the first slot_set -> fxdelay_init/flanger_init memsets them to sync off, div 0, and the autosave then persists that; this path is rare (first Tape use on a card, or a preset without dlyfb). Incomplete fix of 2.2/2.3, reachable in normal use on every host: fxrack_save always writes dlyfb/flgrt, and fxrack.c:438-439 sets params=true on the mere presence of those keys, so an autosave written before the effect was ever used (all zeros) makes init keep the zeros. First Delay then comes up with fb 0 and damp 0 instead of 0.35/0.25, and first Flanger with rate 0.01 Hz, depth 0, fb 0 instead of 0.3/0.6/0.25 (slot_set only repairs wet).
results.fix_sketch: In fxdelay_init and flanger_init copy keep.sync and keep.div in the defaults branch too (a zero struct still gives off/0). In fxrack_save write the dly*/flg* keys only when the struct's params flag is set, and in fxrack_load set params only when the saved values are not the never-initialised pattern (e.g. flgrt > 0; dlyfb, dlymx, dlytn not all 0).

results.title: fxrack_load restarts the reverb on an unchanged mode and accepts the same effect in both slots
results.claim: fxrack_load re-applies the stored reverb mode unconditionally, even when it equals the current mode. reverb_set_mode fades out for up to 60 ms in the UI task, clears the tank and restarts the fade-in. The same function also does not enforce the one-effect-per-slot rule that slot_set enforces: `rk->slot[s] = ...` accepts both slots equal.
results.scenario: Any web Apply, or any preset load, with Hall or Plate running kills the reverb tail and restarts the tank. A body with "fxsl":[4,4] leaves the delay in both slots, so run_gen_slots calls fxdelay_block_f twice per block on the same state. The write head advances twice as fast and the delay sounds wrong and costs double.
results.reasoning: The web Apply posts the whole preset including "rv" (index.html rpApply, 2635-2651), which reaches preset_load on the UI task (menu.c:618-626), and fxrack_load calls reverb_set_mode unconditionally: fade to zero, mode OFF, tank cleared in 8 KB chunks with vTaskDelay(1) each (about 0.2 s dry), then fade in (reverb.c:183-257). So every Apply on Synth/Tape/Drums with a reverb running cuts the tail even when only an unrelated value changed. The web FX1/FX2 selects both offer every effect with no exclusion (index.html:1815-1821) and fxrack_load stores fxsl as given (414-420), so Delay+Delay runs fxdelay_block_f twice per block on one state (fxrack.c:201-206); the same holds for flanger, tremolo and filter. Neither part is in the 09-16 review, and CLAUDE.md documents the mute-and-clear only for mode switches.
results.fix_sketch: In fxrack_load call reverb_set_mode only when m differs from rk->rv->mode (Keys' OFF-before-load sequence still gets its restore because the mode differs there). After reading fxsl apply slot_set's rule: a later slot equal to an earlier non-Off slot becomes FXK_OFF. Optionally make fxSlotPick in index.html set the other select to Off on a duplicate.

results.title: Looper preset load does not clamp bars; bar_frames product can wrap uint32
results.claim: looper_preset_load reads bars as any int (looper.c:457, `lp.bars = j->valueint`), while the menu limits it to 1..8. The uint32 product of period, 4, ppb and bars can wrap, and the later `bf > LP_BUF_FRAMES` cap only catches a wrapped value that is still large.
results.scenario: POST {"bars":1000000000} with sync on and a locked clock. bar_frames wraps to a small number, so track_start_record sets t->target to a few frames and every synced recording ends almost immediately. The value is also persisted by the autosave.
results.reasoning: The load at looper.c:457 takes any int while the menu ladder is 1/2/4/8 (looper_menu.c:371-372), and the product at looper.c:46 wraps once bars exceeds roughly 6,000-130,000 depending on tempo. The stated scenario is overstated: with bars=1e9 at 120 BPM (period 22050) the product wraps to 2,846,576,640, which is over LP_BUF_FRAMES (352,800) and is capped to the 8 s buffer at looper.c:55; a wrapped value lands under the cap only about 1 time in 12,000 per period value, and 0 is also caught. When it does land low the result is a very short loop, with no out-of-bounds write since pos stays below target. It needs a crafted POST or a hand-edited AUTOSAVE.JSN; same pattern as Glitch's 12.6, which sits on the 09-16 watch list.
results.fix_sketch: Clamp in looper_preset_load to the menu's range (below 1 becomes 1, above 8 becomes 8), as the other preset loaders clamp rather than mask.

chunks.coverage_notes: Read in full: components/rest-api/rest-api.c (all 2739 lines); components/rest-api/html/index.html, the whole script (lines 1058-3766) plus the HTML at 676-1057 and 786-830 (Radio, Editor and Clock cards); machine_freesound/fs_web.c; machine_radio/radio_web.c; machine_editor/editor_web.c; machine_looper/looper_web.c; machine_slicer/slicer_web.c. Also read the relevant parts of setup_menu.c (remote JSON), menu.c (EV_REMOTE_* handlers), fxrack.c (save/load and ranges), drum.c (preset save/load), radio.c (station add/del), editor.c (editor_apply), fs_machine.c (names and errors), audio.c (MIDI note handlers). The endpoint-by-endpoint cross-check found that every URL and method the page calls is registered with a matching method. The /status, /sysinfo, /settings, /remote/params (including imap: l, s, k, d, o) and MC_* caps keys the page reads are all emitted. Dropped for lack of space, in order of consequence: a duplicated global in index.html, where `var cvLast` at line 2704 (perform-CV value) and line 3693 (scope spike text) are the same array, so cvEnd() can post a string such as '2048 @ 12:00:00' as v and the scope's 'last spike' column shows knob values; edWhole() (index.html:3270) is undone within 1 s by edState() re-reading in_pt/out_pt; /ice/state reads ICECAST.JSN from the SD card on every 500 ms poll (rest-api.c:2443, reached via bcastPoll -> icePoll); editor_apply and /edit/apply answer ok:true even when the job was rejected (busy, bad op); non-JSON error bodies (400/500 text) are swallowed silently by several .json() chains; a failed cJSON_ReplaceItemInObject on a missing 'ssid'/'apikey' key leaks the new item and does not persist it. Not chased: the largest /remote/params POST against its 8192-byte cap (no machine seemed near it), and the semantics of sample_resolve / sample_name_id and the sd_lock paths inside other components. The firmware does not clamp some values the page posts (clk_bpm outside 20..300 is ignored but answered ok:true); I judged that cosmetic."}

results.title: rdState() dereferences missing #rdnote; Radio card never updates
results.claim: rdState() dereferences #rdnote, which no longer exists anywhere in the HTML (the Radio tab became a card). The TypeError fires on the first line of the .then, and the .catch handler does the same getElementById('rdnote') and throws again.
results.scenario: Switch to the Radio machine. The RADIO card shows, rdState runs every 1 s, and each run throws before it reaches rdstate/rdinfo/rdbuf/rdstations. The built-in station buttons are never built, there is no now-playing or buffer meter, and saved stations and their delete buttons never appear. Only the custom-URL Play, Save and Stop buttons still work, blind.
results.reasoning: No element with id rdnote exists in the page (removed in 89be785 when the Radio tab became a card; only the two uses at 2750 and 2774 remain). getElementById returns null, so the first line of the .then throws and the .catch throws again, before rdstate/rdinfo/rdbuf/rdstations are touched. machCardPoll (3303) runs rdState every 1 s while Radio is active, so station buttons, now-playing and the buffer bar never render. The 09-16 review excluded index.html, so this is not recorded there.
results.fix_sketch: Delete the two getElementById('rdnote') lines (2750 and the body of the .catch at 2774); the card is only shown while Radio is active, so the 'not active' note has no job. Run html/convert.sh afterwards.

The .then throws on its first line and the .catch throws again, so edstate/edout/edbar/edm/edrange and the #edops buttons (3252-3256) are never written and edLoad() on 'done' never fires. #edops is empty in the static HTML (line 807), so edApply cannot be reached from the web. edLoad() at card open still fills the sample select.
