results.title: webPoll() throws on missing #ptag; Poll row never shows PAUSED
results.claim: webPoll() looks up #ptag, which does not exist (only a .ptag CSS rule is left). webPaused is flipped first, then this line throws, so webDraw() and pollStatus() are skipped.
results.scenario: Click the WEB > Poll row. webPaused becomes true and polling stops, but the row keeps saying LIVE and no PAUSED tag is shown. The user cannot tell whether the page is frozen. Clicking again resumes, but not before the next timer tick, because pollStatus() is never called.
results.reasoning: No element with id ptag exists (removed with the header in 499b75e; only the .ptag CSS rule at line 87 is left). The row's inline onclick calls webPoll(), which flips webPaused and then throws at 2575, so webDraw() and the resume pollStatus() are skipped. Polling does stop or resume (pollStatus/sysPoll check webPaused), but the row keeps its old LIVE/PAUSED text until something else calls webDraw (rpSetCard, scrZoom).
results.fix_sketch: Null-guard the lookup (var t=document.getElementById('ptag'); if(t)t.hidden=!webPaused;) or drop the line, since the WEB row already shows the state once webDraw() runs. Run html/convert.sh afterwards.

results.title: FX3 dropdown lacks Shimmer; any Apply posts rv:0 and turns reverb off
results.claim: The FX3 reverb dropdown has 4 modes, but the firmware's rv_mode_t has 5 (RV_SHIMMER = 4) and /remote/params emits rv as that number. With rv = 4 no <option> is selected, so the browser shows 'Off'. rpApply harvests every [data-rp] input, including this select, and posts rv = 0.
results.scenario: Keys, Synth, Tape or Drums has reverb on Shimmer (set on the panel). In the web page, click Apply on the FX card or on the CV MATRIX card (same rpApply). The body carries rv:0, preset_load runs reverb_set_mode(RV_OFF), and the reverb is silently switched off and Shimmer is lost.
results.reasoning: rv_mode_t has RV_SHIMMER = 4 (reverb.h:23-28), the panel cycles through it (fxrack.c:346-350), and fxrack_save emits rv as the raw mode (fxrack.c:372). fxSel (1781-1785) over the 4-entry FXRV marks no option selected for 4, so the select's value is '0'. rpApply (2643-2649) harvests every [data-rp] in the document and posts rv:0, and fxrack_load (408-411) calls reverb_set_mode(RV_OFF). Applies to every fxrack host: Keys, Synth, Tape, Drums.
results.fix_sketch: Add 'Shimmer' to FXRV so it matches reverb_mode_name(). Optionally have fxSel emit a selected option for a cur value outside the list, so a future enum addition cannot be posted back as 0.

results.title: Drums 'trig in' select has no 'none'; Apply rewires src 0 pads to CV1
results.claim: The Drums pad editor's 'trig in' select only offers CV1..8. The firmware emits src = 0 for a pad with no trigger (DR_SRC_NONE, settable from the panel and used in CV-select and TR modes), and src2 also uses 0 for none. No option is selected for 0, so the browser shows CV1, and rpApply then posts src:1.
results.scenario: A Drums pad whose trigger is 'none' (for example a kit driven by TR1/TR2 and the selector CV). Open Remote, change any other setting and press Apply. Every pad with src 0 is rewired to CV1 (drum.c:826 maps src 1 to CV1), so pads start firing from CV1. The same Apply also resets any pad whose sample id is not in the /files list (the options are built only from /files names, which need a .JSN) to '(none)', and clears the sample.
results.reasoning: drum_preset_save emits src = trig_src + 1, so DR_SRC_NONE (-1, reachable via src_cycle at drum_menu.c:710-714) is 0 (drum.c:741). The select only builds options 1..8, none is selected for 0, the browser falls back to CV1, and rpApply posts src:1, which drum.c:826-828 maps to trig_src 0 = CV1. The form sits in the ADVANCED fold (display:none, still in the DOM), so the FX and CV MATRIX Apply buttons trigger it too. The sample sub-claim is wrong: an unlisted sample posts s:"" and drum.c:860 ignores an empty string, so the pad keeps its sample.
results.fix_sketch: Prepend <option value="0">none</option> (selected when p.src is 0) to the cvs list in rpDrumForm. For the sample select, add p.s as a selected option when it is not in names, so the dropdown shows the real state.

results.title: Drums pad level slider max 255 clamps driven pads (up to 1023) on Apply
results.claim: The pad level slider tops out at 255, but the firmware level is uint16 up to DR_LEVEL_MAX = 1023 (knob 6 drives a pad clockwise up to 4x into the soft clipper). The emitted lvl can be above 255, but the DOM range input clamps its value to 255.
results.scenario: A pad is driven to level 700 with knob 6 or the panel. In the web page, press Apply anywhere in the params form. rpApply reads inp.value as 255 and posts pad[i].lvl = 255, so the driven pad drops to unity gain silently.
results.reasoning: Pad level is uint16 up to DR_LEVEL_MAX 1023 (drum_priv.h:162), set by knob 6 past noon (drum.c:253-260) or the panel Level row (drum_menu.c:731-735), and emitted raw as lvl (drum.c:736). A range input sanitises a value above max down to max, so inp.value reads 255 while the label span still shows the real number. rpApply posts lvl:255 and drum.c:807-811 stores it, so the pad drops to unity until the knob is moved again. Any Apply on the page does this, because rpApply harvests all [data-rp] inputs.
results.fix_sketch: Set the level slider's max to 1023 (DR_LEVEL_MAX) and note that 255 is unity in the label; leave pan at 255.

results.title: FX delay time slider max 1000 ms; firmware allows 2000, Apply shortens it
results.claim: The FX delay 'time' slider is capped at 1000 ms. The firmware delay runs to FXD_MAX_SEC = 2.0 s (2000 ms). The panel's Time row steps +10 ms with no 1000 ms cap, and sync divisions at slow tempos give more than 1 s. dlyt is emitted as that value, and the slider clamps it.
results.scenario: Delay time is 1500 ms (panel, or 1/2 note at 40 bpm). In the web page, press Apply on the FX or CV MATRIX card. The slider value reads 1000, dlyt:1000 is posted, and the delay is shortened by a third without the user touching it.
results.reasoning: fxdelay_set_time_ms clamps only at FXD_MAX_FR-1, about 2000 ms (fxdelay.c:70-77, fxdelay.h:27), and the panel Time row steps +10 ms with no lower cap (fxrack.c:70). fxrack_save emits dlyt as that value (374), the range input built at index.html:1796 with max 1000 clamps it, and rpApply posts dlyt:1000, which fxrack_load applies (441). This only happens with Delay in FX1/FX2 (otherwise no slider is rendered) and only sticks for free-running time: with sync on and a tempo, fxrack.c:202 recomputes the time every block, so the finder's 40 bpm example self-heals.
results.fix_sketch: Change the dlyt entry in FXP to max 2000, matching FXD_MAX_SEC.

results.title: In-place rename truncates long ids to 8 uppercase chars on OK/Enter
results.claim: In-place rename still enforces the stale 8-char / A-Z0-9_ rule (rest-api.c:434 `if (tl < 1 || tl > 8)`), although pool ids can be 31 chars and may contain '-' or lowercase (upload, Freesound and editor names). The input is prefilled with the full name (maxlength does not truncate a preset value) and OK/Enter commits.
results.scenario: A sample is listed as 'KICK_DRUM_01' or 'snare-hard'. The user clicks the name to rename and presses OK or Enter, even just to dismiss the box. `to` becomes 'KICK_DRU' (or 'SNAREHAR') and differs from the name, so POST /files/rename renames the audio, .JSN and .OT to the truncated id. Presets and kits that reference the old id silently lose their sample, and two long names with the same first 8 chars collide. A long name cannot be kept at all.
results.reasoning: The #lrn input is prefilled with the full name (1171; maxlength does not truncate a preset value), and libCommit uppercases, strips to A-Z0-9_ and slices to 8, so an unchanged long name gives to !== name and posts /files/rename. files_rename_handler still enforces 1-8 chars A-Z0-9_ (rest-api.c:432-444) and accepts the truncated id, moving audio, .JSN and .OT. This is step 5 of plans/long-filenames-20260913.md ('relax rename validation, make maxlength agree'), which 4722ac9 did not do. No audio is lost, but the long name is, and presets referencing the old id stop resolving, so the class is wrong-behaviour rather than data-loss. A second name with the same 8-char prefix is refused with an alert, not merged.
results.fix_sketch: In libCommit and the #lrn input, use the upload rule already at index.html:1382 (/[^a-zA-Z0-9_-]/g, substring(0,31), maxlength 31). In files_rename_handler, accept strlen(to) < SAMPLE_ID_LEN with the same character set; from_p/to_p[80] already fit a 31-char id.

results.title: Query names are never percent-decoded; DELETE /files answers 200 when nothing was removed
results.claim: get_query_param does not percent-decode, but the page sends every name with encodeURIComponent. Names containing any char it escapes (space, '#', '&', '+', '%', non-ASCII) reach the file handlers still encoded. Affected: DELETE /files, /files/move, /files/rename, /files/raw, /peaks, /trk/get, /trk/delete and /edit/apply. Keys ids like 'PNOF#3' (CLAUDE.md) and card-copied names with spaces are such names. files_delete_handler (line 354 `httpd_resp_sendstr(req, "{}")`) also returns 200 even when nothing was removed. Separately, the page builds onclick="del('NAME')" with esc(), which leaves a name containing ' unescaped, so those row buttons are dead.
results.scenario: Sample 'PNOF#3' is listed. The delete button sends name=PNOF%233, the handler looks for 'PNOF%233.RAW' and removes nothing, yet answers 200 {}. The page drops the row and shows it deleted, and the file reappears on the next reload. Rename and move return 404 and the waveform and download give 404 for these names. A name like "Don't Stop" breaks the row's onclick JavaScript.
results.reasoning: IDF 4.3 httpd_query_key_value copies the value verbatim (httpd_parse.c), and get_query_param adds no decode; only the /ice handler calls urldecode_inplace afterwards (rest-api.c:2407-2411). The page sends every name through encodeURIComponent, so 'PNOF#3' arrives as 'PNOF%233' in delete, move, rename, raw, peaks, /trk/get, /trk/delete and editor_web.c qparam. files_delete_handler ignores remove() results and always sends 200 (349-354), and the page then drops the row locally (index.html:1275). Page uploads and Freesound strip such characters, but tools/curate.py ids with '#' and card-copied names that gained a sidecar are listed by /files; esc() (index.html:1260) also leaves ' unescaped inside onclick strings. Not in the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: Decode inside get_query_param with the existing urldecode_inplace (rest-api.c:2380): fetch into a qlen-sized temp, decode, then refuse if it does not fit buflen, and drop the five now-double decode calls in the /ice handler. Give editor_web.c qparam the same treatment, and make files_delete_handler return 404 when no remove() succeeded, as mod_delete_handler does. In the page, pass names to handlers through data-name attributes instead of quoted onclick strings.

results.title: /trk/upload still clamps the module name to 8 chars and silently replaces a same-prefix module
results.claim: /trk/upload still clamps the module name to 8 chars (stale 8.3 rule; LFN is on). The page sends nameOf(b), up to 31 chars, reports success, and the upload silently replaces any module whose first 8 chars match (f_unlink(path) then rename). mod_list_handler lists names up to 31 chars, so the truncation is inconsistent with the rest of the module handling. (name[16] and path[48] would also need to grow when this is fixed: 13 + 31 + 1 + 4 overflows 48.)
results.scenario: Upload 'AMBIENT_PART1.xm' and then 'AMBIENT_PART2.xm'. Both are stored as usr/TRACKER/AMBIENT_.XM and the second silently overwrites the first, while the page says 'Done: 2 uploaded'. A module the user sees on the card as AMBIENT_PART1.XM is also never matched by name.
results.reasoning: `if (nl > 9) b[8] = 0;` cuts the Name header to 8 chars into name[16], then f_unlink(path) and f_rename publish over whatever already has that name (2113-2114). The page sends nameOf(b), up to 31 chars (index.html:1346, 1423), and counts each PUT as uploaded, so AMBIENT_PART1.xm and AMBIENT_PART2.xm both land as AMBIENT_.XM. Every module name over 8 chars is truncated; the overwrite needs two that share the first 8 chars and the extension. This is a long-filename leftover the 09-16 theme A sweep did not list; path[48] is also too small for a 31-char name (13+31+1+4+1 = 50).
results.prior_ref: theme A (6.1/6.2 related, not listed there)
results.fix_sketch: Follow drop_sample_put_handler and drop_ot_put_handler: refuse rather than truncate. results.title: Download link always names the file NAME.RAW although /files/raw streams WAV/AIFF verbatim
results.claim: The download link always names the file NAME.RAW, but GET /files/raw streams the file verbatim via sample_resolve. Recordings, looper saves, tape takes and imports are WAV, and the pool can hold AIFF. /files does not emit a container or extension for the page to use.
results.scenario: Click the download arrow for a REC_0001 take (a .WAV on the card). The browser saves REC_0001.RAW containing a RIFF/WAVE file. Opened as raw PCM it starts with a 44-byte burst of noise, and audio apps that trust the extension refuse it or mis-detect it.
results.reasoning: The anchor hardcodes download="<name>.RAW". files_raw_handler resolves the id with sample_resolve and streams whatever container exists, as application/octet-stream with no Content-Disposition (rest-api.c:528-549). /files emits name, dir, size, bpm, dur, mtime and ot only (288-296), so the page cannot know the container. CLAUDE.md states recordings and looper saves are written as .WAV, so every REC_/LOOP/tape take downloads as a RIFF file named .RAW; index.html was outside the 09-16 review.
results.fix_sketch: In files_raw_handler add a Content-Disposition: attachment header whose filename is the basename of the resolved `path`, and change the anchor to a bare `download` attribute so the header's name is used. Alternative: keep the audio extension seen in the /files f_readdir pass (cls == 0) in fidx_t, emit it as "ext", and build the download name from it.

results.title: Delete/rename/move sweep an id across all seven folders; same id in two folders is handled as one
results.claim: DELETE /files (and likewise /files/rename and /files/move) sweep the id across ALL seven folders. /files lists each folder separately, so the page can show the same id twice (for example KICK in DRUMS and KICK in KEYS or pool), and the page sends only `name`, never the folder. The page also removes or re-tags every local row with that name.
results.scenario: Kit sample KICK in usr/DRUMS and a different KICK in usr/KEYS. Double-click the X on the DRUMS row: both KICK files (audio, .JSN, .OT) are deleted, and the other machine's sample disappears with no warning. Rename renames both. Move sends only the first file and leaves the same-named twin behind, yet the page re-tags both rows as moved.
results.reasoning: files_delete_handler removes name+ext in every del_dirs entry (346-350), rename renames every match (464-471), and the page sends only `name` and filters or re-tags every local row with that name (index.html:1235, 1253, 1275). /files lists each folder on its own, so twins show as two rows. The sweep is deliberate for pieces of ONE sample, but id uniqueness is not enforced: drop_sample_put_handler opens /usr/<id>.RAW with FA_CREATE_ALWAYS and no cross-folder check (1362, 1389), so re-uploading a name that was moved to DRUMS/KEYS creates a twin, as does a card copy. The second twin is already shadowed for loading (sample_resolve takes the first folder, sampfile.c:88), but one delete click removes both files and their sidecars.
results.fix_sketch: Enforce the invariant where twins are created: in drop_sample_put_handler call sample_resolve(id) and refuse (or replace in place) when the id already lives in another folder, as files_rename_handler already does with 'Target name already exists'. Additionally accept an optional `dir` on delete/move/rename (mv_tags lookup already exists) to restrict the sweep, and have the page send f.dir and match rows on name+dir.

results.title: Station name/url and Freesound query are sized for the decoded value but receive the encoded one
results.claim: The page sends the station name percent-encoded (index.html:2798). The value is copied into name[RADIO_NAME_LEN = 24] BEFORE url_decode, so an encoded name of 24 chars or more is truncated. httpd_query_key_value then returns an error, hn is false and the station is saved as 'custom'. The same pattern applies to the url (RADIO_URL_LEN 176 holds the encoded form) and to /fs/query q (fs_web.c:163, FS_QUERY_LEN 48 holds the encoded form, answering 'missing q').
results.scenario: Import a .m3u whose #EXTINF title is 'SomaFM Groove Salad (128k)' (26 chars, 32 once encoded). Every such station is saved under the name 'custom', and the list becomes a column of identical buttons. In the Freesound card, a 40-char query with 6 spaces encodes to 52 chars and returns 'missing q'.
results.reasoning: qparam copies the still-encoded value into name[RADIO_NAME_LEN = 24]; httpd_query_key_value returns ESP_ERR_HTTPD_RESULT_TRUNC when the encoded length is 24 or more, so hn is false and radio_station_add gets "custom" (119). The m3u import sends encodeURIComponent(j.name) (index.html:2798), so 'Radio Paradise Main Mix' (23 chars, 3 spaces, 29 encoded) already fails, and longer titles become 'custom' instead of being truncated. The same pattern holds for url[RADIO_URL_LEN 176] (400 'need ?url=') and fs_web.c:162-163 q[FS_QUERY_LEN 48] ('missing q', though that needs an unusually long query). The 09-16 chunk 13 note only cleared RADIO_NAME_LEN as a long-filename leftover.
results.fix_sketch: Read each encoded value into a buffer sized for the encoded form (3x the target, or a malloc of the query length as qparam already does), run the existing url_decode / urldecode, then strlcpy into the RADIO_NAME_LEN / RADIO_URL_LEN / FS_QUERY_LEN buffer; radio_station_add already truncates with strlcpy. Best done once inside qparam / q_param so every caller gets decoded, length-checked values.

results.title: POST /settings persists an empty ssid; the page posts ssid:"" whenever the SSID row is blank or absent
results.claim: POST /settings accepts an empty ssid and persists it (passwd and apikey treat empty as 'unchanged', ssid does not). The page's saveSet always posts ssid:g('gsSsid'). When the GET /settings behind the GLOBAL screen failed or returned {} (glLoad's J() swallows errors; the handler returns {} when CONFIG.JSN cannot be read, which happens under RAM pressure), the SSID row renders blank.
results.scenario: GET /settings returns {} during a busy moment. The GLOBAL screen shows empty Hostname/SSID rows. The user types a new Api Key and clicks Save: the body is {ssid:"",passwd:"",apikey:"...",hostname:""}. The handler sets settings.ssid = "", marks wifiChanged, writes CONFIG.JSN and calls restartWifi() with an empty SSID. The unit drops off the network and cannot rejoin after reboot until the card is edited by hand.
results.reasoning: The ssid branch has no empty check, unlike passwd (1102) and apikey (1110), so "" replaces the stored SSID, sets wifiChanged, is written to CONFIG.JSN and goes to restartWifi. saveSet always sends ssid:g('gsSsid'), and g returns '' when the element is missing (index.html:1503-1506): that is the case before glLoad resolves (globCard renders an empty screen while rpGlob is null, 2430) and the row is blank when GET /settings failed or returned {} (J swallows errors, 2354). The finder overstates recovery: the AP fallback returns after about 2 min and at every boot (wifi.c:263-268, 316-318) and the panel can re-enter the SSID, so no card edit is needed. Not in the 09-16 review (6.4/6.5 cover a wrong password and missing keys).
results.fix_sketch: Treat an empty ssid as unchanged, exactly like the passwd and apikey branches (add `&& j->valuestring[0]`). In saveSet, send ssid and hostname only when their inputs exist and differ from rpGlob.s, so a Save on an unloaded screen posts nothing destructive.

results.title: Boot-logo header check does unaligned 32-bit loads (claimed LoadStoreAlignment panic)
results.reasoning: The ESP32 LX6 core handles unaligned loads in hardware: esp-idf-v4.3/components/xtensa/esp32/include/xtensa/config/core-isa.h:171-174 defines XCHAL_UNALIGNED_LOAD_EXCEPTION 0 and XCHAL_UNALIGNED_LOAD_HW 1. The casts at buf+10/18/22/30 therefore read correctly and raise no exception; the fault the finder describes is ESP8266 (LX106) behaviour. The casts are non-portable style only, and the little-endian field reads give the right values.
